544054|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 presales rose 35% YoY to INR206 crores, while PAT fell to INR23 crores from INR33 crores; FY27 presales guidance kept at INR700 crores.
544054|2026-09.overview: Suraj Estate reported Q2 FY27 sales value of INR206 crores (+35% YoY) and collections of INR104 crores (+46%), with H1 sales value of INR347 crores (+48%). Total income rose 18% YoY to INR171 crores, but EBITDA fell to INR56 crores from INR66 crores and PAT fell to INR23 crores from INR33 crores. Management reiterated FY27 presales guidance of INR700 crores and a launch pipeline of about INR1,600 crores, and said the Suraj One Business Bay GDV was raised to about INR2,000 crores after acquiring adjoining land rights. Net debt rose to INR710 crores, and management targets about INR600 crores by year-end.

segments.name: Residential (value luxury)
segments.commentary: Suraj Nova (Mahim West) and Suraj Madonna (Dadar West) have commencement certificates, with combined GDV of about INR250 crores. Both are targeted for launch and RERA registration in Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What contributes the INR353 crores of H2 presales needed to reach the INR700 crores guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance relies mainly on launched ongoing projects plus a couple of upcoming residential components, with commercial (Business Bay) expected to drive much of the traction. No split was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the approval and construction timelines for the expanded Business Bay project?
qa_highlights.answer: Concession plans and environment clearance are in hand; IOD for the combined potential is being issued. Only amalgamation and excavation of the additional component remain, expected within about 60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Has the FY27 INR1,600 crore launch pipeline changed in timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Launch plan is unchanged: about INR800 crores commercial (phase 2 of Business Bay) and INR250 crores residential targeted in Q3, with the remaining about INR550 crores in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of debt, the use of new borrowings and the leverage target?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt rose about INR96 crores, mainly to acquire Business Bay adjoining development rights for about INR85 crores. Cost of debt is about 13-13.25%. Net debt target is about INR600 crores by year-end, helped by 5-6 project handovers worth about INR150 crores of debt reduction.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline to monetise the INR1,168 crores receivable from sold inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a timeline on the call; it offered to send IR a roughly one-year cash-flow schedule covering completed and ongoing projects.

qa_highlights.question: Are there other redevelopment opportunities and is the company looking outside South Central Mumbai?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is evaluating a couple of society redevelopments and one or two commercial build-to-suit deals, and it remains focused on South Central Mumbai to first execute its existing land inventory.

544055|2026-03.headline: Muthoot Microfin Q4 FY26: AUM ₹14,005 crore (+13% YoY), Q4 profit ₹71 crore, GNPA down to 3.89%; Vision 3030 targets ₹30,000 crore AUM by 2030.
544055|2026-03.overview: Management used its maiden Capital Markets Day (7 May 2026) to unveil Vision 3030: ₹30,000 crore AUM, ROA of 5%+, ROE of 20%+ and 10 million lives by 2030. FY26 showed a full-year loss of ₹222 crore in the prior year turning into a ₹170 crore full-year profit, with Q4 profit of ₹71 crore described as the best in seven quarters. Asset quality improved: GNPA 3.89% (from 4.85%), net NPA 1.14%, Q4 credit cost 2.8% and FY26 credit cost 3.5%. Diversification moved non-JLG to about 17% of the portfolio, and cost of funds fell to 10.27% from 11.02%.

segments.commentary: FY26 disbursement ~₹26.5 crore, with monthly disbursement near ₹11 crore; average ticket ~₹4 lakh; 100% collection and no delinquency as stated; ROI 18-22%; Kerala is 45% of the book.

segments.commentary: Referral volume ~₹7 crore per month; co-lending with Muthoot FinCorp under consideration; yield ~17-21%.

guidance_outlook: Vision 3030: AUM ₹30,000 crore by 2030, implying ~21% CAGR from ₹14,000 crore; the company says it aims for >15% growth in FY27 (management earlier cited a 12-15% range in analyst questions).
Long-run credit cost target ~2.5%; FY30 ROA target 5%+ (~₹1,000 crore profit in FY30 confirmed); ROE 20%+.
NIM: management expects FY27 NIM of roughly 12.5% and 13.5-14% (13% 'across cycles') by FY30; no credit rating upgrade assumed for FY27.
Opex to fall to 5% or below by 2030 from 6.4%; weighted average portfolio yield to rise from 18.8% to 22-23%.
Balance sheet leverage target ~4x (3.3x on balance sheet now); about 12-15 months of current capital to fund growth before equity is needed.
NCD/ECB share of borrowings to rise from 22% to ~40% by 2030; digitally collected share of collections to reach 75% by 2030 (about 40% now).
capex_capacity: Network: 1,670 branches across 21 states and UTs, 390 districts; 91 branches merged or closed under branch-profitability review, while new branches opened in Assam, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
Workforce 15,735 employees, ~90% in field roles; ~12% of field roles are female ROs, with attrition about 50% lower than male counterparts.
Credit underwriting: dedicated team of ~1,800 (about 2,000 in the credit vertical) with generative-AI-assisted credit appraisal memos.
Vision 2030 product mix: JLG 53%, individual loans ~33%, MSME LAP ~10%, retail secured ~3%.
Contingency funding of ₹2,000-3,000 crore available at short notice; ₹700-800 crore free funds carried through the year, plus HQLA.
CGFMU / CGTMSE guarantee applied for, pending budget allocation; the new CGS-MFI scheme capped at ~₹300 crore for the company.
demand_pricing: Wallet-share study: for ~30 lakh overlapping customers, FY24 to FY26 microfinance exposure fell ~32% while total loan balances rose from ~₹40,000 crore to ~₹45,000 crore; gold exposure rose from ₹4,093 crore to ₹7,456 crore.
Yields: JLG effective ~24.5%, individual loans ~23.5%, LAP 18-22%, gold 17-21%; management says micro-LAP at 27-28% due to processing fees.
Rejections: post-MFIN guardrails the JLG rejection rate is ~60% (Karnataka ~65%); productivity per employee fell to ~₹7 lakh in Q1 due to rejections.
Rural focus: 98% of branches are rural; competition described as relatively limited in these areas.
Lending rates were cut multiple times in 2024; management says ~70% of FY26 disbursements were made at rates ~200 bps lower than the prior year.

qa_highlights.question: How does the 21% CAGR to ₹30,000 crore square with FY27 guidance of 12-15%, and what gives confidence growth accelerates from FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 beat four of five guidance items (AUM growth 13% vs 5-10% guided, credit cost 3.5% vs 4-6%, mix 83:17 vs 85:15) and expects more than 15% growth in FY27, with the step-up from diversification.

qa_highlights.question: Will diversification shield the company from the microfinance cycle, and what is FY30 asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said diversification and deeper household engagement should smooth the cycle, with long-run credit cost of about 2.5%; FY30 profit of ~₹1,000 crore was confirmed as the target.

qa_highlights.question: How is underwriting done without over-reliance on talent, and why a hybrid rather than centralised model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a human-in-the-loop model: field credit officers use AI-assisted appraisal memos and aggregator data, and a central team sets loan ceilings within which branches decide.

qa_highlights.question: How do individual loans differ in credit risk from JLG, and how can the bounce and delinquency record be trusted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 0+ and 30+ delinquency of zero on ~₹2,300 crore, ~10% NACH bounce collected within eight days, a 700+ bureau score floor, and 2-3 years of repayment track record with the company.

qa_highlights.question: How will NIM rise from 12% to 13-14% when new-disbursement yields are similar to the new loan rates?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 NIM was 12.8% at the start of the year and about 12% in FY26; repricing benefits from the Q2 FY26 yield changes fall into FY27, with NIM back to about 12.5%. The 13%+ level rests on mix, cost of funds and yield, and FY27 excludes any rating upgrade.

qa_highlights.question: What are branch rationalisation plans and the benefit from the CGS-MFI guarantee scheme?
qa_highlights.answer: 91 branches have been merged or closed, while new branches open in new states. CFO said the CGS-MFI scheme caps the company at ~₹300 crore and adds little for a large MFI, with cost of funds already at ~9.9% on incremental borrowing.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company charge higher yields for lower-risk products, and why would credit cost fall as yields rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the yield rise is driven by higher-yield new originations and the shrinking of the defaulting denominator, and that Muthoot's brand and gold-custody service let it price slightly higher than peers.

qa_highlights.question: What are leverage and capital needs to reach 5% ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company targets about 4x leverage (3.3x on balance sheet now), with NIM +100 bps, opex -50 bps and credit cost around 2.5% sufficient for 5% ROA, plus about 1% of fee income.

risks_watch: Dependence on the JLG segment (about 83% of AUM) and on Southern states, where 55% of customers sit; state-level regulatory risk raised by a questioner, with management saying regulated entities are exempt from local rules.
Execution risk on the ~21% AUM CAGR and on yield uplift to 22-23%; the FY27 guidance of 12-15% is below the FY30 path.
Credit quality of new individual/MSME/LAP products over a full credit cycle, since they have limited seasoning (about 2.5-3 years of track record for the cohort).
Interest rate and inflation risk: management flagged a possible modest policy-rate increase.
Equity dilution: management said equity will be needed at some point, with the current capital covering about 12-15 months of growth.
Rising rejection rates (~60%) constrain JLG sourcing and productivity; watch employee productivity and attrition.
key_quotes: So we are confident that we will overachieve our guidance.
So effectively what is happening is that whenever we do a rate change or a yield change that is always a prospective impact.
So we'll be looking at four times leverage.
So I think the idea is to have a qualitative growth and a sustainable growth.

544055|2026-06.headline: Muthoot Microfin Q1 FY27: record Q1 disbursement of INR2,644 crore, cost of funds down to 10.13%, credit cost 2.6%, and AUM growth guidance raised to 20%.
544055|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the start of an execution-led turnaround, with disbursements of INR2,644 crore (about 49% above Q1 FY26) and collection efficiency near 98%. Cost of funds fell 14 bps QoQ to 10.13% before the benefit of the AA- CRISIL upgrade, and credit cost eased to 2.6% from 2.8%. PPOP rose about 43% YoY and 3% QoQ, and AUM grew 18% YoY. Management raised FY27 AUM growth guidance to 20%, ROA to the upper end of 3.3%, and ROE to around 18%, and said NIM expansion would show from Q2.

financial_highlights.change: about 49% above Q1 FY26; highest Q1 ever

financial_highlights.value: Up about 43% YoY and about 3% QoQ
Flat QoQ; management cited about 50 bps YoY expansion in Q1
financial_highlights.change: Full-year FY27 NIM guided 12.3%-12.5%; management said 12.5% upper end is achievable

segments.name: Joint Liability Group (JLG)
segments.commentary: Yield on group loans about 24.85% after a rate hike from 23.5% at end of Q1. Remains one of three priority products.

segments.name: Individual loans
segments.commentary: About INR3,200 crore book with 0.02% 30+ delinquency and no 60+ or 90+. Yield about 23.5%. Built on a creamy layer of about 8.5-9 lakh customers with 700+ scores. Repayments are 100% digital.

segments.name: Gold loans (referral and co-lending)
segments.commentary: Disbursing about INR100 crore per month since April; about INR350-360 crore disbursed to date. Q1 was almost entirely referral business. Co-lending split is 60% on Muthoot Microfin's book and 40% on the parent's book. Referral earns 1.5%.

segments.name: Loan against property and consumer durables
segments.commentary: LAP yield 18%-22%. Consumer durable loans are a pilot of about INR500 crore at 22%-23% yield, funded through CP at about 8.1%-8.2%.

FY27 ROA guided at 3.3% (upper end expected), ROE around 18% (upper end). Management expects 4%-4.5% ROA within about 18 months and about 5% by FY30.
Credit cost guidance of 2.7%-3.5% for FY27, now expected to be better; long-term normalised range 2%-2.25%.
NIM guidance 12.3%-12.5%; NIM expansion expected from Q2 as liquidity drag eases.

Gold loans use parent Muthoot Finance branches for storage and assessment, so no separate gold branch capex is needed.
Consumer durables pilot of INR500 crore to be expanded depending on results.
demand_pricing: Industry AUM contracted, but quality is improving. Management says larger, well-capitalised players are gaining share. Industry active customers have fallen from about 8 crore at peak to about 6 crore.

Group yield raised to 24.85% from 23.5% at end of Q1, with no further hike planned for now. Management said the benefit should go to NIM rather than customers.

Liquidity is ample. About INR5,000 crore of sanctions are in hand, plus INR1,000 crore under CGFMU of which only INR200 crore has been drawn. About 20% of AUM is targeted for CGFMU cover; the application is pending.
Management said El Nino rainfall deficit fell from 43% to about 12%. Less than 2% of customers are directly exposed to agri activity in sensitive regions.

qa_highlights.question: Can disbursement return to INR1,000 crore per month, and can AUM growth exceed 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR1,000 crore per month is achievable, with FY27 disbursement above INR12,000 crore. Q1 at INR2,644 crore was the slowest quarter, and Q2 onward should rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended yield, given that the incremental cost of borrowing fell while NIM stayed flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended portfolio yield is about 23%. Reported yield is diluted by non-performing assets in the denominator. Management said Q1 NIM is up about 50 bps YoY, and yield expansion will follow as collections from NPAs improve.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Assam flood or the broader monsoon risk affect the book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has no exposure to upper Assam, where floods are seasonal, and its lower-Assam portfolio is unaffected so far. Natural calamity insurance covers all customers, including drought.

qa_highlights.question: How do the direct assignment (DA) income and gold referral and co-lending work?
qa_highlights.answer: DA income is booked under net gain on fair value changes, not interest income. Q1 DA was about INR355 crore, and FY26 DA was about INR1,600 crore. Gold co-lending began only at quarter-end, so about 98% of Q1 gold business was referral.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost guidance for FY27?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins and ROA/ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM guidance is 12.3%-12.5%, with the upper end expected. FY27 ROA is guided at 3.3% (upper end) and ROE at about 18%. Management targets 4%-4.5% ROA in about 18 months and about 5% by FY30.

qa_highlights.question: What are the MFI vs non-MFI mix targets?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM mix is at 76:24 (JLG to non-JLG) now and is expected to end FY27 at about 70:30. Management's long-term target is 55:45 on AUM and 60:40 on balance sheet after DA.

risks_watch: Cost of funds must reach single digits by end FY27; benefit of the AA- CRISIL upgrade and CGFMU drawdown (only INR200 crore drawn of INR1,000 crore; about 20% of AUM targeted cover, application pending) are not yet in the Q1 numbers.
NIM expansion is guided from Q2, but Q1 NIM was flat QoQ with negative carry from excess liquidity; watch whether disbursement recovery consumes liquidity and lifts NIM toward 12.3%-12.5%.

Credit cost of 2.6% is below the 2.7%-3.5% guidance; sustainability versus the long-term 2%-2.25% normal and exposure to El Nino and Assam floods are open questions, though management cites insurance cover and less than 2% agri exposure in sensitive regions.
Gold co-lending and referral and the consumer durable pilot (INR500 crore at 22%-23% yield) are early-stage; Q1 gold business was about 98% referral and co-lending only began at quarter end.
key_quotes: this is a turnaround that we have been talking about the quarter 1 performance actually reflects what strategy that we have developed and articulated, it is getting into motion and getting into execution.
In the quarter, we have reduced our cost of fund from 10.27% to 10.13%, 14 basis point reduction has already happened in the Q1 itself.
We feel that in the financial year, we should be able to come into single digits in terms of our cost of fund and availability of fund is already there.
So we are likely to overachieve that in terms of credit cost. We are looking at 2.7% at the lower spectrum, but we'll be better than that for sure, the way the asset quality is panning out.

544057|2026-03.headline: Happy Forgings Q4 FY26 revenue rose 20.4% YoY to Rs.424 crore, with EBITDA margin at 31.5% and FY27 volume growth guided to late-teens.
544057|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs.424 crore (up 20.4% YoY), EBITDA Rs.133 crore (up 30.4%) at a 31.5% margin, and PAT Rs.84 crore (up 23.6%). FY26 revenue reached Rs.1,546 crore (up 9.8%), with EBITDA of Rs.471 crore (30.4% margin) and PAT of Rs.302 crore (19.5% margin). Management guided to late-teens volume growth in FY27 with EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26, and flagged raw material and other manufacturing cost inflation linked to the US-Iran situation, which it is seeking to pass on to OEMs from 1 April. Management stressed a shift toward new PV, industrial and heavy-forging programmes at higher realisations (Rs.340-350/kg vs current Rs.245/kg).

EBITDA rose 39.3% to Rs.141 crore, margin up about 275 bps YoY, the fourth straight quarter above 30%. Management says customer price revisions are partly in Q1 (about 30%) and will fully reflect from Q2. Exports were hit by transit delays, with the domestic CV business up about 18%.

segments.name: Farm equipment
segments.commentary: 32% of revenue; grew mid-20s. Domestic up over 20%; exports grew despite weak US and Europe tractor demand. Export share about 5% of revenue.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: 16% of revenue; around 50% growth in both domestic and export. Export share about 9% of revenue. Drivers cited: power generation, wind, railways, oil and gas, digital infrastructure.

segments.name: Off-highway
segments.commentary: 11% of revenue; over 40% growth in both domestic and export. Domestic construction equipment up about 9%. Export share about 5% of revenue.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles

qa_highlights.question: Can growth trajectory hold across industrial, export and PV, and can the high gross and EBITDA margins sustain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to strength across CV, farm, PV; a ~Rs.950 crore order book; and new high-realisation products. It said the last price increase was three years ago, supporting margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the price-revision benefit flow from Q2, and is it permanent?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% came in Q1. Domestic: 2% taken in Q1 versus 4.5-5% total, with OEMs passing on from Q2. Increases are on a three-year-old base and described as permanent; currency gains supported exports.

qa_highlights.question: Will solar benefit come in Q4 FY27 and can margins stay above 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar expected on stream from January, with some generation in Q4 and connection through April. Management is confident of upwards of 30% EBITDA margin, citing a 1-1.5% power benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CV revenue grow only ~7% against ~10% industry production growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic CV grew ~18% against ~10% production growth; exports fell ~12% because DDP contracts (Europe, Turkey) saw about a month of deliveries delayed by transit issues.

qa_highlights.question: What is the freight cost impact and recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Container costs rose from about USD 2,000 to USD 6,000. About 75% of contracts are pass-through; company expects a 15-20% hit and is negotiating recovery of about USD 4,500 per container.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export mix by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximate export share of revenue: CV ~7%, PV ~8%, farm ~5%, off-highway ~5%, industrial ~9%.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the Rs.950 crore order book and the Rs.650 crore capex, and plant-level margins for the new industrial line?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book roughly 35-40% industrial, 25-30% PV, 25-30% CV, rest off-highway/farm; 60% export, 40% domestic. New heavy-line gross margins expected around 60-65% with EBITDA about 50% of gross; plant-level margins not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: receivable and inventory days as of June 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days improved with no big change; inventory days about 50 as of date; overall working-capital days improved.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 guidance be revised given strong Q1 volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is high-teen volume growth and it should perform better than that, without giving a revised number.

qa_highlights.question: Asset turns and high base in PV and CV as capex comes on stream in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not worried about a temporary six-month to one-year dip in asset turns, since capacity is being built for future growth; PV growth is from two to three customers with customer acquisition ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Inorganic plans and funding of growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Open to acquisitions and JVs, mainly for technology in energy and aerospace; cautious on expensive valuations in farm/CV. Growth to be funded largely by internal accruals, possibly with a one-year bridge loan for LCs.

544058|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6% YoY to INR162 crore with EBITDA flat at INR42 crore; management guides FY27 to flat store count and mid-single-digit same-store growth at best.
544058|2026-03.overview: Credo Brands (Mufti) reported Q4 FY26 revenue up 6% YoY to INR162 crore, with gross margin of 58.8% and EBITDA flat at INR42 crore (25.6% margin) as advertising was stepped up to about 8% of revenue. FY26 revenue was flat at INR592 crore, with EBITDA of INR154 crore (26% margin). The company closed 24 stores and opened 7 in the quarter, reducing the network by 17. Management said FY27 is a consolidation year with roughly 20 openings and 20 closures, with ad spend rising to 8-10% of revenue and margins likely lower.

segments.name: Online / omnichannel
segments.commentary: Online channel is about 9% of revenue, of which the company's own platform is about 5%. Website business grew about 75% YoY in FY26; online EBITDA margin is lower because it is still discount-driven.

guidance_outlook: FY27: store count broadly flat, with about 20 closures and about 20 openings; throughput per store is the focus.
FY27 growth: management would be happy with mid-single-digit same-store growth; FY27 described as a consolidation year, with visibility limited by West Asia conflict and inflation.
Advertising and branding spend to rise to about 8-10% of revenue; Raman KV's 9-10% framing was confirmed as the broad direction, but not fixed.
FY27 EBITDA margin may be about 23-24%, lower than FY26's 26%, because of higher marketing spend.
Gross margin expected in a 56-58% range, though management said it could fall to 55%.
Capex of about INR40-45 lakh per new store, depending on high street or mall location.

544067|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 31% to INR1,630 crore and Q4 revenue grew 42% to INR447.8 crore; management guides to 20%+ volume growth in FY27.
544067|2026-03.overview: Innova Captab reported its highest-ever annual performance, with FY26 consolidated revenue of INR1,630 crore (+31% YoY) and Q4 revenue of INR447.8 crore (+42% YoY). Growth was led by the CDMO business (INR1,133 crore, +24% for FY26) and Branded Generics (INR497 crore, +51%), with the Jammu facility's first full year of ramp-up a major contributor. FY26 EBITDA rose to INR250.3 crore (15.4% margin) from INR198.2 crore, while PAT grew 10% to INR140.9 crore. Management said Jammu is near EBITDA breakeven and expects it to turn EBITDA-positive in the coming quarter.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,133 crore (+24%); Q4 INR314.8 crore (+41%). Customer base above 350 clients, including several leading Indian pharma companies. Baddi facility grew about 35% YoY, mainly on volumes.

segments.name: Branded Generics
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR497 crore (+51%); Q4 INR133 crore (+46%). Domestic is trade generics, roughly 70% domestic and 30-35% exports per management; not tracked by geography at segment level.

segments.name: Jammu facility
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR300 crore revenue in FY26; Q4 exit run rate above INR90 crore. Management says EBITDA is near breakeven and expects EBITDA-positive in the next quarter.

segments.name: Sharon Bio
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR240 crore; export regulated markets (Canada, UK, Europe, Australia); margin above company average per management.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of 20%+ revenue growth, and said volume growth of 20%+ at group level is maintained for FY27 from FY26.

EBITDA growth expected to outpace revenue growth as Jammu utilisation ramps up; PAT growth expected to outpace EBITDA growth because Jammu depreciation and finance costs are largely fixed and already in the base.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be better than FY26 (15.4%); management cited a few percentage points of improvement from operating leverage, without quantifying.
Proposed new Baddi general block: capex INR150-170 crore, spent across FY27 and FY28; optimum revenue potential INR450-500 crore. Still under deliberation.
Greenfield projects take about 1.5 years to reach commercial production, so new-plant depreciation and interest are expected to hit P&L mainly from FY28.
capex_capacity: Jammu facility completed its first full year of operation in FY26; ramp-up progressing steadily. Jammu houses injectables, general, cephalosporin, beta-lactam and penems; new formats include BFS and respules.

Baddi land parcel (about INR20-odd crore, disclosed earlier) acquired for a general oral tablet, capsule and oral liquid block to relieve high utilisation at Baddi; detailed note to follow once finalised.
Maintenance capex continues at recent percentage-of-revenue trend; new Baddi block capex of INR150-170 crore expected across FY27 and FY28.
Regulatory milestones: Baddi cephalosporin facility received UK-MHRA approval; Jammu blocks received PIC/S certification via SMDC Ukraine. Company also cites EU-GMP certification.
demand_pricing: Cephalosporin API prices fell in Q2 and Q3 FY26, stabilised in early Q4, and rose on a YTD basis into April 2026 amid the Middle East conflict; management said Q4 itself saw no meaningful sequential rise.

CDMO pricing is cost-plus, and management said raw-material increases have largely been passed through to customers. Management said raw-material availability is not a concern; the issue is price, not supply.
Gross margin decline YoY attributed solely to product mix; management said raw-material price increases had no impact on gross margin.
Management said the Jammu revenue contribution is being used to both CDMO and Branded Generics; split not disclosed.
Management did not give a split of CDMO growth between volume and realisation at group level.

qa_highlights.question: Split of CDMO growth between volume and realisation for FY26 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not track volume at entity level; Baddi grew about 35% YoY, mainly on volumes, with Jammu ramp-up a key driver.

qa_highlights.question: Is Jammu EBITDA positive, and how close to breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Jammu did about INR300 crore in FY26 and is nearing EBITDA breakeven in Q4; management expects EBITDA-positive and fixed-cost coverage in the coming quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall YoY despite a higher branded share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline only to product mix; raw-material price increases had no impact on gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: Ex-Jammu EBITDA margin of about 18%? Is it a good estimate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed with the analyst's back-of-envelope calculation of about 18.2% ex-Jammu EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for Baddi land purchase and FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Baddi general block is for higher-utilisation general portfolio; capex INR150-170 crore spread across FY27 and FY28, with optimum revenue INR450-500 crore; still under deliberation.

qa_highlights.question: Sharon Bio revenue and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Sharon revenue about INR240 crore in FY26, with a margin above the company average given its export regulatory market focus.

Raw-material and API price volatility from the Middle East conflict; cost-plus pass-through is assumed but timing lag is not quantified.
Jammu EBITDA breakeven timing and utilisation ramp; the company guided that it will turn positive next quarter.

544067|2026-06.headline: Innova Captab Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34% YoY to INR470.9 crores, with EBITDA up 33% to INR75.1 crores at a 16% margin.

EBITDA was INR75.1 crores (16% margin, +33%) and PAT was INR44.1 crores (+42%). Management said volume growth was 20-22% and the rest of growth came from mix and pricing. Jammu turned EBITDA-positive at roughly INR1-1.5 crores on about INR107 crores of quarterly revenue, up from about INR90 crores in the prior quarter.

segments.name: Branded generics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR142.2 crores, +39% YoY, with focus on deepening presence in existing markets and entering new domestic and international geographies.

segments.name: Jammu plant
segments.commentary: Around INR107 crores revenue in Q1 and positive EBITDA of INR1-1.5 crores; annualised utilisation about 25-30%; asset turn expected north of 3x at optimum.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: 20%+ revenue growth, with profitability growing faster than revenue; management clarified the 20%+ growth refers to volume.
Management said volume growth of 20%+ is expected for FY27 on a year-on-year closing basis, with the Q1 volume growth of 20-22%.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guidance held at 15-16% +/-2%; management suggested a normalised 17-18% band, with Jammu adding 2-3 pts once mature.
Gross margin expected to stay within +/-2% of about 35.5% for the full year.
Jammu peak revenue estimated at about INR1,400 crores at 65-70% utilisation; management said it could cross INR1,000 crores with new country and product approvals.
Sharon organic business guided to grow in the early teens; Jammu adds the top-up to reach 20%+ overall.
Maintenance capex guided at INR20-25 crores and growth/debottlenecking capex at INR20-30 crores per year for FY27 and FY28; Baddi new plot plan not yet firmed up.
capex_capacity: Jammu plant started ramping up in January of last year; annualised Q1 utilisation about 25-30%; asset turn expected north of 3x at optimum.
Jammu expansion is the INR500 crore project; management said future expansions would come in tranches of about INR200-250 crores, not a single INR1,000 crore outlay.
Jammu has capacity in penem, beta and cephalosporin categories sufficient for the next two to three years.
Future growth capex is for debottlenecking, equipment replacement or doubling equipment capability; any greenfield project would be announced to the market with board approval.

Logistics cost rose slightly in the quarter; management said it was not material.
Management said the company is present in six or seven therapeutic categories and will expand both existing capacity and new dosage forms/categories.
R&D spend is about 0.7-1% of revenue.
Semaglutide: batches being worked on by the plant team; development status unchanged from the prior call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle and is it normalising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cash conversion cycle is maintained at 90 days +/-10 days at group level, and Jammu working capital was built up in the prior year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin profile sustainable ex-Jammu?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 15-16% +/-2% blended guidance; said ex-Jammu margin around 20% is not the steady state and that 17-18% is a fair normalised level.

qa_highlights.question: What are the maintenance and growth capex numbers for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance capex INR20-25 crores per year; growth capex INR20-30 crores per year for existing capability augmentation and debottlenecking.

qa_highlights.question: Has there been any pricing pressure this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices moved in an upward direction in the quarter, passed through under the cost-plus model.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said branded generics are treated as a normal CDMO customer by plants, with arm's-length transfer pricing; no conflict per se.

544073|2026-03.headline: Manoj Ceramic FY26 total income rose 23.4% to ₹202.99 cr, but EBITDA was flat at ₹24.88 cr and H2 EBITDA margin fell to ~11% from ~14%.
544073|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 total income up 23.4% YoY to ₹202.99 cr, with PAT up 10.1% to ₹12.01 cr and EBITDA of ₹24.88 cr. H2 FY26 total income grew 23.3% to ₹120.82 cr, with EBITDA of ₹13.45 cr and PAT of ₹6.14 cr. Management tied the H2 margin compression to lower-margin tile volumes and service/project contracts with discounts, and said the margin would recover in FY27. Balance sheet metrics improved: debtor days fell from 163 to 114, trade receivables were about ₹63 cr, and long-term borrowings fell from ₹28.98 cr to ₹13.89 cr.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: Management said B2B is about 80-82% of sales, with B2C the balance. B2B is served through a West and South zone logistics network covering more than 900 dealers.

segments.name: B2C / Retail
segments.commentary: Six premium experience centres cover over 1,26,500 sq ft with more than 1,000 SKUs. Management described B2C as a small but growing contributor, supported by the Italian/imported marble division (Marmi Bella).

segments.name: Service / project supply and fixing
segments.commentary: The company said this business carries lower margins but higher volumes, and volume-linked discounts were passed on. This was cited as the main driver of H2 margin compression.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: A Dubai display centre was launched in FY26. Management is targeting African markets, with export operations expected to be operational in the first six months of FY27. No export contribution figure was given.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated a 25-30% CAGR growth target, saying it has been met since listing and will be pursued in FY27.
Margin recovery is expected in FY27 from premium products, exports and the reduction of low-margin service contracts. Management declined to quantify FY27 or FY28 EBITDA margins.
Working capital discipline is to be tightened further in FY27. No specific debtor or inventory day targets were given.
Management said Capex and expansion plans are on schedule, but gave no amounts and promised announcements later.
capex_capacity: Upper Thane cutting and polishing facility is operational and is the first step toward backward integration.
A new technology-based product launch that was scheduled has been delayed in production and is now expected in FY27.
Management said new depots, new products and new horizons are scheduled, but gave no capex quantum or timeline.
Management did not disclose FY27 or FY28 capex, store expansion counts or capacity figures.
demand_pricing: Volumes were up roughly 23-24% overall, per management. The company said it met its planned volumes despite the Iran-war gas supply disruption in the Morbi cluster.
Prices were raised in the last 15-20 days of March 2026 to pass on the cost impact to customers.
Exports have not been affected because Middle East exposure is limited, according to management.
Management said higher-volume service contracts required discounts, which lowered margins in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 EBITDA margin fall about 300 bps to ~11% from ~14%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed new design tile products that drove volume but not sustainable margins. It described the arrangement as temporary and said margins would improve once a delayed new technology product launches in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Has the Iran war and gas supply disruption hurt volumes or margins in March-May?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes met plan and prices were raised in late March to pass on costs. It agreed the position was fine 'so far' and gave no quantified impact for April or May.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivables ageing, and were all warrants converted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management deferred the ageing breakdown to the public balance sheet. It confirmed all warrants have been converted, including the last one held by the promoter group.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA bridge and steady-state margin, given EBITDA was flat YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to service/project contracts with lower margins and higher volumes, which required discounts. It declined to quantify FY27-28 EBITDA margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the B2B/B2C mix and aspirational direction?
qa_highlights.answer: B2B is about 80-82% of sales. Management said it will stay B2B-led while building B2C through word of mouth, the Italian marble division and experience centres.

qa_highlights.question: How does the asset-light model compare with manufacturers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued that sourcing from multiple manufacturers avoids machinery capex and depreciation, and that its logistics network lets it take up new products within about 15 days.

544081|2026-09.headline: Jyoti CNC Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 31% to INR588 crore with 28% EBITDA margin; order book at INR5,082 crore.
544081|2026-09.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue grew 31% YoY to INR588 crore, with EBITDA of INR164 crore (28% margin, up 320 bps) and PAT of INR115 crore (19.6% margin). Consolidated revenue rose 18.5% to INR602 crore, but consolidated EBITDA margin was 21.8% and PAT margin 12%, weighed down by Huron, where revenue recognition is pending end-user certificates and dual-use licences. Management said dispatches were about 1,900 machines, the highest quarterly volume in company history, and order intake was INR800 crore, taking the order book to INR5,082 crore. Management also disclosed PLI/ECMS approval for over INR1,020 crore of capex over five years with a 25% central capital subsidy (about INR255 crore).

qa_highlights.question: Will H1 interest cost fall to about INR14 crore despite higher net debt?

544088|2026-03.headline: Medi Assist FY26: total income up 23.6% to INR923.2 crore, operating EBITDA margin 19.3%, company turned debt-free in Jan 2026.
544088|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed strong top-line growth with total income of INR923.2 crore (up 23.6% YoY) and operating income of INR904.8 crore (up 25.1%). Operating EBITDA reached INR174.6 crore at a 19.3% margin, with quarterly margin expanding from 17.1% in Q2 to 18.6% in Q3 and 19.9% in Q4. Reported PAT was INR89.3 crore, while adjusted PAT was INR68.8 crore after exceptional items. The group became debt-free in January 2026, and Paramount TPA operations were transferred into Medi Assist TPA effective 1 February 2026.

qa_highlights.answer: Management described retail as a hybrid model: TPA-led for high-frequency outpatient products and technology plug-ins for insurers' own front ends, with the premium under MAtrix reported separately.

qa_highlights.question: How can investors track earnings on the technology business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose a take rate. It offered a directional aspiration of 1.5-2x traditional TPA margins, stating this was not guidance.

qa_highlights.answer: No material Middle East exposure; the international slowdown was limited to group, with some operational challenges on seafarer cover. Exceptional items remain open and are disclosed in the notes.

544088|2026-09.headline: Medi Assist Q2 FY27 operating revenue rose 3.9% YoY to INR241.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 20.4%; group retention held at about 90.5% in H1.

rows.why: Front-load washing machine pilot underway with mass production targeted end-Sept/October 2026, top-load already in production for three brands, and three new categories added in Q1 with four more in pipeline.

544095|2026-09.headline: EPACK Q2 FY27 revenue more than doubled to INR439 crores (+106% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 1.62% after no PLI income accrued.
544095|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 106% YoY to INR439 crores, with H1 revenue of INR1,325 crores (+51.3%), the company's highest-ever first half. EBITDA was INR7.1 crores (margin 1.62%) versus INR0.5 crores a year earlier, but the prior-year quarter included INR8 crores of PLI income, which was not accrued this year. Excluding PLI, the company says EBITDA improved by about INR14.6 crores YoY, and it cites a forex loss of about INR10 crores as a drag. Management said the Epavo JV stake (50%) is being transferred to Ram Ratna Group for INR15 crores, and two dormant subsidiaries are being wound up.

segments.commentary: Q2 RAC revenue about INR161 crores, up about 160% YoY on a weak base (INR61-odd crores); H1 RAC grew 58%. Prices are up about 15-20% YoY model-wise. Installed capacity about 2.3 million sets.

segments.name: Small and large domestic appliances (SDA+LDA)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about INR168 crores, up 57% from INR107 crores; H1 SDA and LDA grew 62%. Non-RAC share of revenue was 63% in Q2, with washing machines and air fryers leading growth.

segments.name: Components
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about INR47 crores, up 45% from INR32 crores; captive integration deepening in heat exchangers, copper tubing, PCB, cross flow fans and moulding parts.

segments.name: Hisense (via EMTPL, wholly owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Approximately INR90 crores of Hisense sales in H1 FY27; about 18,000 ACs sourced so far this year. Front-load washing machine pilot production through end-November 2026, mass production from December.

capex_capacity: Capex plan of about INR470 crores announced about 18 months ago; INR370 crores actualised by end-September 2026.

Front-load washing machine for Hisense via EMTPL (Sri City): pilot by end-November 2026, commercial production from December; takes EMTPL into multiple product categories.
Dehradun and Bhiwadi plants reported significantly better utilisation; capacity utilisation was the challenge in prior quarters.
Pipeline for FY27 includes oil filter heaters, washing machines, air purifiers and other products under development; vacuum cleaners, tower fans and nutri blenders launched during the year.

Non-AC share of business rose to nearly 50% from 45% year-on-year; air coolers were softer this year.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q2 RAC growth came from volume versus pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a volume split; it said RAC revenue grew about 160% YoY, with model-wise price increases of 15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Has the 15-20% price hike covered all cost escalation to date?
qa_highlights.answer: Largely yes, with an ongoing lag as escalations pass through in subsequent quarters, and most vendors have had increases passed on.

qa_highlights.question: Post-PLI margin outlook and need for further price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins to improve as PLI discounts given to brands are rolled back in phases and mix shifts to SDA and LDA; no numerical margin guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Hisense sales figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximately INR90 crores in H1; about 18,000 ACs sourced this year to September.

qa_highlights.question: Debt, finance cost and working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt about INR770-775 crores, similar to last year; total finance cost flat despite revenue doubling; debt/equity about 0.8x in the medium term.

qa_highlights.question: Is any margin pass-through still left and what is the utilisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Some lag remains, but no significant gap; utilisation to improve with Hisense, washing machines and new southern customers; no explicit earnings guidance.

544105|2026-03.headline: Harshdeep Hortico H2 FY26 revenue rose to INR 36.1 crore-range with EBITDA of INR 11.3 crore, but FY26 revenue of INR 69 crore missed the INR 85 crore internal expectation.
544105|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 H1 revenue of about INR 32.64 crore and H2 of about INR 36.1 crore, versus INR 24.9 crore and INR 31.51 crore in FY25. EBITDA rose to INR 8.4 crore in H1 and INR 11.3 crore in H2 (from INR 5.95 crore and INR 9.0 crore), and PAT to INR 5.7 crore and INR 6.82 crore. The CFO said full-year revenue of INR 69 crore fell short of the INR 85 crore expectation because of LPG gas cuts of about two months, raw material (PP) prices up 20-25% or more, and deferred luxury orders. Management said demand is holding flat year-on-year but not growing, and that margins are being defended by passing on only part of the cost increase.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 24.90 crore in H1 FY25 (about +31%)
vs INR 31.51 crore in H2 FY25 (about +15%)
vs internal expectation of INR 85 crore; FY27 guidance cited as INR 115 crore

segments.name: Roto moulded series
segments.commentary: About 30.66% of FY26 revenue per management; described as the highest-quality, high-volume, high-margin category with about 10-year warranty. Management said this segment was hit hardest by the price-driven slowdown.

segments.name: Grower series (injection moulded nursery pots)
segments.commentary: Described as about 30-40% of revenue and 42-43% of margins; high volume, low margin, about 1 lakh pots per day. Management said demand is not materially affected, with about 10-15% growth in the segment.

segments.name: Decorative series
segments.commentary: About 14% of revenue; affected by deferred purchases alongside roto moulded products.

segments.name: AgriShield shade nets
segments.commentary: Introduced in FY26; about 3% of revenue. Management guided to roughly 10-20% growth and said capacity at 100% efficiency, with the Pune line fully booked.

segments.name: Fiberglass, EcoSeries, garden furniture and fountains
segments.commentary: Fiberglass about 3.78%, EcoSeries about 1-2%, garden furniture about 1%. Roto moulded fountains launched in March 2026 with a 10-year warranty, and management reported 15-20 days of order backlog.

segments.name: Channel mix
segments.commentary: B2B about 75% and B2C about 25% per one answer; later a B2C ballpark of 15-18% of current revenue excluding wholesaler sales. Management said 13 major distributors and seven showrooms, mainly for wholesalers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance of INR 115 crore was referenced by an analyst; management did not confirm a firm number and avoided giving one.
Management said 25-30% annual growth is achievable if geopolitical conditions normalise.
Management said the current infrastructure can support revenue above INR 100 crore, and claimed comfort with 35-40% growth from existing capacity.
Management said it will hold margins as far as possible and expects to pass on only part of the cost increase.
Next detailed commentary expected after H1 FY27 results; no formal con-call scheduled before then.
capex_capacity: Three factories: Bhiwandi (about 1 lakh sq ft, largest), Pune (about 40,000 sq ft) and Delhi (about 20,000-25,000 sq ft, newly added this year).
Two warehouses (Bhiwandi and Bangalore), with an added Pune warehouse and a Kolkata warehouse serving the Northeast.
About 10% of facility capacity affected by raw material and LPG shortages, per management.
Solar panels installed on the Pune factory; management expects savings of about INR 10-15 lakh per month, MW capacity not disclosed.
No FY27 capex plans announced; management said it is comfortable and would discuss any future capex.
demand_pricing: Raw material (PP) prices up about 60% per management, from INR 100-120/kg to INR 160-170 (some grades INR 220); company passed on about 20-25% in wholesale prices, with competitors at 25-30%.
Customers are holding back orders; management said April-May sales are flat year-on-year with no decline and no exponential growth.
Current order book: three airport orders (Lucknow, Mumbai, Visakhapatnam) worth about INR 1.5 crore, plus ongoing showroom orders.
Ugaoo is the largest customer, at about 10% of business, up from about INR 1 crore to about INR 10 crore this year.
Export share about 2% of revenue; new export markets in Canada, USA and the Netherlands this year.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue mix between B2B and B2C, and whether B2B is order-book driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2B is about 75% and B2C about 25%, with pots purely B2B and garden furniture and fountains sold B2C. Current order book was about INR 1.5 crore of airport orders.

qa_highlights.question: Realistic FY27 revenue and three-year growth aspiration after the FY26 shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a firm number, citing LPG cuts, labour shortage, raw material spikes and deferred projects. It said 25-30% annual growth is realistic if conditions normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold around 30% after raw material inflation, and has price been raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices were raised about 20-25% on wholesale rates (not MRP), with the company holding back on full pass-through to avoid losing customers. Management said it will keep margins as high as possible.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rising YoY, and what is the sustainable level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to inventory build for capacity growth and sudden orders (e.g., about INR 1 crore in two weeks for an event), plus credit to large customers and new stores. It gave no target number.

qa_highlights.question: Is inventory (up 62%) and receivables (up 51%) growth due to pre-stocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no pre-stocking; it held stock for only 15-20 working days during raw material shortages and expects the condition to be temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H2 EBITDA margin about 31% vs about 28% last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonality, with H2 driven by festivals and landscaping projects and higher-margin roto moulded and decorative products, plus the new fountain launch.

qa_highlights.question: How are large B2B and infra orders won, and what is the margin differential versus distributors?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders come through landscapers and subcontractors who tender on the company's behalf, as payment security is needed. Management said distributor and project margins are the same, with discounts of 45-50% based on order value, and the project margin is about 17%.

Working capital stress: inventory up 62% and receivables up 51% YoY, with credit extended to large customers.
Demand softness in roto moulded and decorative series as customers defer discretionary spend; FY27 growth targets unconfirmed.
Fuel and transport cost increases (about 10-15% extra per management) could further squeeze margins or demand.
Customer concentration: Ugaoo at about 10% of revenue, and reliance on a few large infra projects that management said have been deferred.
Disclosure gaps: solar capacity (MW), B2C split including wholesalers, and export data were not provided; the company said it would revert by email.

So, there is no dip in the business as of now because of all these conditions, but we are not seeing any exponential growth as well.
Distributor margins and the big project margins are the same. We don't differentiate in any much way.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Roto moulded fountains launched in March 2026 with 15-20 days of order backlog, and new export markets in Canada, USA and the Netherlands were opened this year, though exports are only about 2% of revenue.

rows.why: Three airport orders (Lucknow, Mumbai, Visakhapatnam) worth about INR 1.5 crore are the only large concrete backing, against FY26 revenue of INR 69 crore, so they cover about 2% of annual revenue.

544111|2026-03.headline: Apeejay Surrendra Park Hotels FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12% to INR 707 crore, with PAT of INR 66 crore; Q4 revenue up 4% to INR 184 crore.
544111|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated operating revenue was INR 184 crore (up 4% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 53 crore (28.85% margin) and PAT of INR 12 crore (6.44% margin). Management blamed Q4 cancellations in Delhi and Hyderabad on the Middle East war, saying occupancy there has recovered to over 90%. For FY26, revenue grew 12%, EBITDA was INR 218 crore (30.82% margin) and PAT was INR 66 crore (9.21% margin), with profitability hit by the Middle East war and higher depreciation and finance costs. Management reiterated the plan to double hotels to 85 and keys to 6,635 over four years, and said the EM Bypass Kolkata apartment sales are ahead of plan on cash flow.

financial_highlights.change: resilient despite high base; YoY not stated
ARR up 9% YoY; RevPAR up 7% YoY

segments.name: Hotels
segments.commentary: Park Calcutta ran at 100% occupancy for Q4 and FY26; Park Chennai (95%) and Park Navi Mumbai (93%) were the other top-three occupancies. Delhi and Hyderabad saw large Q4 cancellations, now recovered to over 90% occupancy.

segments.name: Flurys (F&B retail)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 29% YoY and the brand has 110 outlets. Management said it is profitable but did not share segment EBITDA. Plans to add 30+ outlets in 10 months (NCR 8, Pune 5, Bangalore 4).

segments.name: F&B overall
segments.commentary: F&B revenue crossed INR 300 crore in FY26, about 43% of total revenue.

segments.name: Real estate (EM Bypass Kolkata)
segments.commentary: 29 of 34 apartments sold in the first block at an average INR 20,857 per sq ft. Cash flow improved by over INR 11 crore up to April 2026, with a further ~INR 70 crore expected this year; second block launch planned for Sep-Oct 2026.

guidance_outlook: Reach over 3,000 keys by FY27 after adding 12 hotels (472 keys), of which 8 are asset-light.
Over four years: hotels from 42 to 85, keys from 2,677 to 6,635; owned hotels to double, asset-light to triple.
Flurys to reach 140 outlets (or slightly more) after 30 additions in 10 months, and 40-50 more outlets by 2030.
Park Mumbai Juhu (78 rooms) construction to start June 2026, completion by about March 2027.
Malabar House (Cochin) acquisition expected to close in June 2026; Vizag (100 rooms) moved to early 2030 opening due to environmental clearance delays.
Interest cost at about 8.35% (MCLR), expected to stay below that level; capex and acquisition needs of about INR 1,500 crore over five years, mainly funded by internal accruals.
Management said earlier mid-teens top-line growth guidance was missed; FY26 came in at 12%.
capex_capacity: Five projects (Pune, Mumbai, Vizag, EM Bypass, Jaipur) totalling 950 rooms at about INR 1.2 crore per room, about INR 1,100 crore before the EM Bypass reduction.
EM Bypass expected to contribute INR 350 crore, of which INR 70 crore is expected this year.
Zillion and THALI acquisition/project cost about INR 330 crore; normal capex about INR 40 crore per year; Flurys capex about INR 30-40 crore per year.
Q4 FY26 launches: Zone by the Park Darjeeling, Zone Connect by the Park Gangtok and Zone Connect by the Park Katra; 7 properties (283 keys) launched in FY26.
Flurys moving from central kitchen to an outsourced manufacturing vendor (agreement signed).
Room renovations planned at Chennai, Bangalore, Kolkata and Vizag; 20 rooms at Park Calcutta to be refurbished.
demand_pricing: Management cited limited branded supply in India (about 216,000 rooms) and said supply growth is 200-300 bps below demand growth.
Kolkata has 5,101 keys with about 1,702 keys expected over five years; management said the outlook is positive, helped by the change of state government.

Ran Baas The Palace (Patiala, leased) ran at ARR of about INR 31,000 in FY26; Lotus Palace Chettinad at about INR 12,000 ARR and about 30% occupancy; Patiala targets about 50% occupancy in the Oct-Dec season.
Cancellations in Delhi and Hyderabad in Q4 due to the Middle East war; management said contracts with ministries and corporates have been re-established.
Park Calcutta has about 30% repeat customers and T-RevPAR near INR 24,000, which management said is above luxury peers in its CBD.
Management said the Operation Sindoor disruption hit Q1 FY26 and the Middle East war hit from late February into April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ADR decline sequentially and grow only 3% YoY in Q4, and why was FY26 growth 12% against a mid-teens expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 weakness to large cancellations in Delhi and Hyderabad from the Middle East war, which have since stabilised. It said 12% growth was good given two disruptions (Operation Sindoor in Q1 and the Middle East war).

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Flurys outlet count below earlier guidance, and what is the achievable expansion plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan is 30+ outlets in the next 10 months (from 110 to about 140), largely cafes, with flagships in each new market; 40-50 more outlets by 2030. Management said the asset-light model with outsourced production allows faster rollout.

qa_highlights.question: How is 100% occupancy at Park Calcutta calculated when the website shows rooms available?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 100% means all rooms occupied every day, that the hotel has delivered near-100% occupancy for about 10 years (excluding COVID), and that its revenue management and repeat base (about 30%) drive this.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kolkata outlook and how is the EM Bypass sales progress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kolkata supply is limited and the state government change is positive. Apartments were launched at about INR 18,225 per sq ft and are now selling near INR 21,000; second block expected around the festive season.

qa_highlights.question: How will Flurys maintain quality with the central kitchen dropped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the central kitchen plan was dropped in favour of an outsourced vendor, with recipe standardisation, quality checks and quality chefs on site at the production facility.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company keep interest costs under control during the capex cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Atul Khosla said the interest rate is about 8.35% (MCLR) and will stay below that. Capex of about INR 1,500 crore over five years is mostly funded by internal accruals, with about INR 80 crore cash on hand; project interest will be capitalised as IDC.

qa_highlights.answer: Vizag was delayed by environmental clearance, which is now in place; the project has no basement, so it may be faster, but management kept a 2030 timeline. Malabar House acquisition is expected to close in June 2026 after bank approval for foreign payment.

544111|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10% to Rs.172 crore and EBITDA 8% to Rs.52 crore, while PAT fell 14% to about Rs.12 crore on finance costs and a tax-regime shift.
544111|2026-06.overview: Management reported operating revenue of Rs.167 crore (+8% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs.47 crore (+3%, margin 28.12%) for Q1 FY27, with consolidated revenue of Rs.172 crore (+10%) and EBITDA of Rs.52 crore (+8%). Occupancy held at 92%, but ADR growth was only about 2% amid West Asia disruption, weak international air traffic and flat domestic air traffic. PAT declined about 14% to close to Rs.12 crore, reflecting about Rs.2.5 crore higher finance charges from Zillion acquisition financing and a Rs.2.2 crore deferred tax provision on the move to the new tax regime. Management guided to a stronger ADR trend from Q2 onward, with the BRICS Summit, weddings and exhibitions cited as drivers.

segments.name: Food and Beverage
segments.commentary: F&B contributed about 43% of total revenue in Q1; Flurys stood at 111 outlets (cafes, kiosks, tea rooms) after adding one at Inorbit Mall Vizag, with first standalone North India cafe opened in Gurugram in August.

segments.name: Hotels (owned and managed)
segments.commentary: Portfolio stated as 42 hotels with 2,677 keys (one slide reference in call says 2,667). Ran Baas Patiala ARR about Rs.33,000 and Lotus Palace Chettinad about Rs.13,000, both still stabilising.

segments.name: EM Bypass Kolkata mixed-use project
segments.commentary: 33 of 69 service apartments sold at average about Rs.20,633 per sq ft; expected cash inflow Rs.70-80 crore this year, of which Rs.21 crore received.

guidance_outlook: ADR growth guided to high single digits for the coming season, supported by BRICS Summit in Delhi, about 40 wedding dates Nov-March, Aero Show Bengaluru and Bharat Mobility Expo.
Pipeline of 12 hotels with 472 keys in FY27, taking portfolio to 3,149 keys by end-FY27 from 2,677 keys.
Flurys target of 29 additional outlets in FY27, taking count to about 140; target of 400 outlets by 2030.
Long-term ambition of more than 6,000 keys by FY2030; management also cited 87 hotels and 6,719 keys over four years.
Other income guided at about Rs.3.5-4 crore per quarter; further cash inflow of about Rs.50 crore expected from EM Bypass by year-end.
Effective tax rate guided to fall to about 30-35% in Q2-Q4 FY27 under the new regime (from about 40% in Q1).
capex_capacity: EM Bypass Kolkata: 218 hotel rooms plus 69 service apartments, completion targeted early 2030; second Kolkata hotel referenced for opening in 2030.
The Park Juhu (78 rooms, converted from service apartments): design complete, launch targeted October 2027; long-term financing tied up for Zillion acquisition.
Vizag 100-room hotel: on site, launch expected in August 2026, completion early 2030.
Malabar House, Fort Kochi (17 keys, about half an acre): acquisition in progress, completion expected October-November 2026; acquisition cost about Rs.64 crore.
Pune FSI raised from 2.5 lakh to 6.7 lakh sq ft; plan of 2.5 lakh sq ft for hotel and 4 lakh+ sq ft for residential.

Capex for Pune (200 rooms), Navi Mumbai (250), Vizag (100), EM Bypass (220) and Jaipur (150) over 4-5 years: about Rs.1,140 crore at Rs.1.2 crore per room, plus Zillion acquisition about Rs.210 crore, Juhu renovation about Rs.80 crore and Kochi about Rs.64 crore (total about Rs.350 crore additional, cited with EM Bypass funding offset). Operating capex Rs.40 crore per year plus Flurys Rs.40 crore per year. Net capex about Rs.1,500 crore, to be funded from EBITDA of Rs.240-250 crore per year. About Rs.200-250 crore of capex expected within FY27.
Completed SAP S/4HANA implementation for Finance during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Occupancy 92%, described as India's leading occupancy; RevPAR leadership in upper upscale maintained.

Juhu ARR about Rs.18,000-20,000; management expects Bombay ARR growth of 10-15%.
Management expects ADR to improve from Q2 onward; said Q2-Q4 should be distinctly better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Given 92% occupancy, how should ADR evolve and what long-term ADR growth should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ADR pressure came from West Asia disruption, flat domestic passenger traffic and about 10% decline in international inbound traffic. All-India ADR growth was 6% in the quarter; it expects Q2-Q4 to be distinctly better and high single-digit ARR growth in the coming season, helped by BRICS Summit, about 40 wedding dates Nov-March, Aero Show and Bharat Mobility Expo.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Flurys still at 111 outlets versus aggressive plans, and how will the 29 additions be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Flurys has grown at a 21.5% CAGR since 2019 (17 outlets); five outlets opened so far with the rest mapped, including 3 Pune, 3 Mumbai, 5 Hyderabad, about 7 Delhi NCR, 4 Bengaluru and up to 10 PVR outlets under negotiation, targeting about 140 by year-end and 400 by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.4.79 crore other income run-rate sustainable over the next three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income of Rs.4.79 crore included about Rs.2.7 crore from mutual funds; management guided Rs.3.5-4 crore per quarter. About Rs.50 crore more EM Bypass cash is expected by year-end, to be added to mutual funds of about Rs.97 crore, so other income may rise.

qa_highlights.question: How mature is the existing portfolio and how long does stabilisation take for new hotels?
qa_highlights.answer: Ran Baas (ARR about Rs.33,000) and Lotus Palace Chettinad (about Rs.13,000) are entering maturity, with occupancy stabilising over the year; a 15-room Vembanad Lake property acquired this year is expected to stabilise with its Q3-Q4 season. Typical stabilisation is 2-3 years, but high-potential markets like Mumbai and Pune are expected to stabilise in 1-1.5 years or the first year.

qa_highlights.question: How does the EM Bypass service apartment model change return on capital and land evaluation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the model could lift RoCE from about 9-10% toward 20%+ as the project goes live, with cash flows of about Rs.70 crore this year, Rs.120 crore next year, Rs.100 crore in year three and Rs.30-40 crore in year four; sales of Rs.300-325 crore are meant to fund the hotel build, which management described as virtually free.

qa_highlights.question: What is the updated capex guidance for FY27 and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex for Pune (200 rooms), Navi Mumbai (250), Vizag (100), EM Bypass (220) and Jaipur (150) over 4-5 years is about Rs.1,140 crore at Rs.1.2 crore per room, plus about Rs.350 crore of Zillion, Juhu, Kochi and related items; net capex about Rs.1,500 crore against EBITDA of Rs.240-250 crore a year. About Rs.200-250 crore of capex falls within FY27, and Juhu's long-term financing is tied up.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall 14% when revenue rose 8%, and what is the tax outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance charges rose about Rs.2.5 crore YoY mainly on Zillion acquisition financing, and a Rs.2.2 crore deferred tax provision came from moving to the new regime. Q1 tax was about Rs.8.71 crore at roughly 40%; the effective rate is guided to about 30-35% in Q2-Q4, and management asked that PAT be compared with Q4 rather than Q1.

risks_watch: ADR recovery in Q2-Q4 depends on the BRICS Summit, wedding season and exhibitions; Q1 ADR growth was only about 2% for the company versus 6% for the market.
International inbound air traffic fell about 10% and city-level domestic traffic declined (Mumbai -3.5%, Hyderabad over -12%, Chennai -13%), so West Asia and air-connectivity pressure could persist.
Finance costs will rise with Zillion acquisition debt and capex of about Rs.1,500 crore net over 4-5 years; FY27 capex of Rs.200-250 crore must be funded from EBITDA and EM Bypass cash.

Execution risk on the EM Bypass sales (Rs.70-80 crore this year, Rs.21 crore received), the Juhu conversion (78 rooms, October 2027), Vizag launch in August 2026 and the Kochi acquisition (October-November 2026).
Flurys needs 29 net additions in FY27 to reach about 140 outlets; progress against the 400-outlet 2030 target and the Adani, DLF, Phoenix and PVR tie-ups still unconfirmed.

Tax rate step-down to 30-35% from about 40% is guided but not yet visible; the PAT trend depends on it. Mutual fund holdings (about Rs.97 crore) were questioned for being regular rather than direct plans, and an investor's request for the fund list was not answered on the call.
key_quotes: So, we expect that the quarters ahead are going to be distinctly better than the quarter which has gone by.

This decline is due to the impact of higher finance costs to propel expansion during this period as well as deferred tax provision of Rs.2.2 crores as the company shifts to the new favorable income tax regime.
And I would also request that if you are comparing PAT compare with the Q4 not to the tax rate with the Q4 not to the Q1.
So, we can expect definitely high single digit ARR growth as we go forward.

544117|2026-03.headline: Signpost India FY26 revenue rose 27% to INR576 crore with EBITDA margin up ~590 bps to 25.5%; management guides 20%+ growth and 25-27% margin for FY27.
544117|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 46% YoY and 14% QoQ to INR162 crore, with operating EBITDA more than tripling YoY to INR42 crore at a 26.3% margin. FY26 revenue rose 27% to INR576 crore, EBITDA rose 65% to INR147 crore and net profit more than doubled to INR70 crore. Receivables rose about 80% YoY to INR317 crore, which management attributed to multi-city campaigns requiring regional compliance approvals, and it targets faster collections by Q3 FY27 through milestone-based billing. This was the company's maiden earnings call.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 net profit / net margin

financial_highlights.change: more than doubled from 7.5% margin in FY25

segments.name: Transit media
segments.commentary: Management calls transit the primary focus on long-term contracts; industry transit segment grew 22% in 2025 to INR20.2 billion. Bangalore Metro stations under contract rose from 18 to 25 against 67 stations on the line.

segments.name: Digital out-of-home (DOOH)
segments.commentary: Management cites DOOH as a higher-margin contributor; digital ad space reportedly rose from 25,000 sq ft to 80,000 sq ft between Q3 and Q4. Transit and digital together are about 48% of FY26 top line.

segments.name: Street furniture / bus queue shelters
segments.commentary: Mumbai contract requires 20% of about 3,000 bus queue shelters to be upgraded within 3 years; about 11% completed so far. Digitisation is not a binding commitment.

Electric premium bus fleet additions across Mumbai, Hyderabad and Goa.
Management says new assets typically take 4-6 months to mature; some (e.g., Shimla) take 5-6 months.
demand_pricing: Management says around 3/4 of revenue is direct from advertisers; anchor client share about 29% of revenue; over 1,600 active advertisers.
Management cites FICCI-EY data: organised OOH market grew 13% in 2025 to INR66.9 billion, projected about INR85 billion by 2028; DOOH about 18% share, transit about 30%.
Management says customer mix includes PSUs and fintech/banking (e.g., SBI, NPCI, PNB), with FMCG, education, MSME and BFSI as other key categories.
Management says it is shifting from short-term intermediary-led campaigns toward multi-month and annual brand contracts; average remaining contract tenure about 14 years.
Most contracts are minimum-guarantee (fixed licence fee) models; revenue-share contracts are below 10% of portfolio, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How will receivables increase (noted as higher this quarter) be addressed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to multi-city campaigns where regional office approvals delay invoicing; milestone-based billing is being pushed with clients, targeting improvement by Q3 FY27. Bill discounting was explored but rejected due to added cost.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue cross INR1,000 crore by 2029?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 48% of FY26 revenue is already in the FY27 engine and it would be 'the first person to see that number in 2029', but it could not assure that target.

qa_highlights.question: What drives gross margin and how much can cost fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of services includes licence costs and production/display costs such as Wi-Fi and power; management sees a 7-8% scope to reduce these costs next year without hurting top line. Most licences are minimum-guarantee, not linked to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Sector split of revenue and receivable sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give numbers; said PSU/government-linked and FMCG, education, MSME and BFSI are the main categories, not real estate or luxury brands.

qa_highlights.question: Can gross margin move to 30% in 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new geographies need 4-6 months to mature and gave no margin target beyond the 25-27% EBITDA range guidance; Bangalore Metro ramp was cited as an example.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue potential of recent contracts (Kolkata, Bengaluru Metro, OMC petrol pump hoardings)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kolkata implementation expected at 60-70% by Sept-Oct 2026; Bangalore Metro stations now generating revenue, with some signed for 2-3 years; FY27 growth expected at 20%+.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive advantage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited multi-city techno-commercial bidding track record, 7+ year contract tenures, direct advertiser relationships and the Captura AI planning platform; example of MSRDC bid where 27 agencies bid and few qualified.

qa_highlights.question: Founder shareholding fell from 66% to 44% after merger with Pressman; rationale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on valuation; said Pressman promoters converted equity to non-promoter base due to family losses and age.

qa_highlights.question: How many Mumbai bus queue shelters are digitised?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract requires 20% of about 3,000 shelters to be upgraded (refurbishment, not necessarily digital) within 3 years; about 11% completed. Digital is at company's discretion.

544118|2026-03.headline: Jana SFB met all Q4 FY26 guidance: PAT INR140 crore, net credit cost 0.47%, SMA 3.66%; FY27 guided to PAT growth of 80%+.
544118|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered on every guidance point set in Q3: PAT of INR140 crore (guided INR140-160 crore), net credit cost of 0.47% (INR156 crore) against 0.79% in Q3, and SMA of 3.66% versus a guided ceiling of below 4%. Gross slippages of about INR334 crore were the lowest in roughly eight quarters, and management said the MFI stress is behind it. Advances grew 23% YoY to INR36,289 crore and deposits grew 23% to INR35,784 crore, with cost of funds down to 7.46%. FY27 guidance calls for gross loan growth of 19-21%, deposit growth of 23-25% and PAT growth of 80%+.

segments.name: Affordable housing
segments.commentary: Largest product at INR8,174 crore with average ticket of INR12.7 lakh. Relocations and split branches were the main FY26 branch drivers.

segments.name: Micro LAP
segments.commentary: INR6,300 crore book with average ticket of INR6.7 lakh, growing only 9.4% YoY and the weakest secured segment; management expects 12-15% growth in FY27.

segments.name: MSME / commercial banking
segments.commentary: INR5,281 crore MSME book, with commercial banking growing about 23.3%; management is watching for Middle East war spillover.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: INR2,358 crore book, up 140% YoY, average ticket about INR2 lakh; yields said to be competitive with market but below gold NBFCs.

segments.name: Vehicle loans (2-wheeler and used car)
segments.commentary: Vehicle loans grew 79.6% YoY. Used car business launched October 2025, running at about INR25 crore disbursals per month in 15 cities, targeted to reach 35 cities by September 2026.

segments.name: Microfinance (MFI)
segments.commentary: MFI book was about INR10,000 crore in March 2024 and INR8,900 crore in March 2025, and has risen about 10% since but is still below March 2024. Unsecured slippages were about INR150 crore in Q4, down 35% QoQ and about 50% YoY; the SMA book fell about 24%.

segments.name: Term loans to NBFCs
segments.commentary: INR1,935 crore book.

guidance_outlook: FY27 gross loan portfolio growth of 19-21%, deposit growth of 23-25%, and PAT growth of 80%+ over FY26; guidance excludes any benefit from a possible universal bank licence.
Secured book to grow 25-30% and unsecured 10-12% in FY27; total secured advances growth expected closer to 30% in FY27.
