rows.why: Credit line on UPI (proof of concept in Q2), loans against shares and mutual funds (November) and trade FX via AD-1 licence (December) are all guided with dates.

rows.label: Net NPA below 1% after guarantee claim
rows.why: Net NPA is 1.08%, and INR 68 crore of CGFMU claims expected within about 2 months should bring it below 1%, with the remaining INR 251 crore lodged in Q3 next year.

rows.label: CASA ratio recovery to ~20% in H2
rows.why: CASA grew 13% YoY and fell 2% QoQ in ratio terms; management targets about 20% CASA via affluent offers and digital onboarding by January, but rate environment is tough and deposit pricing is competitive.

rows.label: AI-led headcount and cost reduction
rows.why: Headcount in September 2026 was lower than March 2026 despite asset and liability growth, and cost-to-income fell from 67.0% to 64.3% QoQ, with opex up 15% YoY against NII up 35%.

tone.note: Management was confident on profitability (raised PAT guidance to 100%), asset quality and cost trajectory, but candid on CASA, deposit shortfall, gold and micro LAP growth, and sub-60% cost-to-income being unlikely this year; analysts probed the sustainability of cost-to-income, CASA and NIM in a r

544119|2026-03.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 51% YoY to INR 4,489 crores, with PAT up 65% to INR 87 crores.
544119|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations grew 51% YoY to INR 4,489 crores, EBITDA rose 41% with margin at 2.95%, and PAT grew 65% to INR 87 crores (1.93% margin). For FY26, revenue grew 15% to INR 15,827 crores, EBITDA rose 53% to INR 459 crores (2.90% margin, up 72 bps), and PAT rose 35% to INR 282 crores. Management attributed H2 growth mainly to price increases in the PES category, with H1 growth driven by volume and customer additions. Management guided to a ~20% CAGR and said the PC super cycle could last another 1-2 years, while flagging a possible 5-10% unit decline in CY26 and H2 consumer softness.

financial_highlights.change: Described as healthy vs prior-year outflows

segments.name: PES (Personal computing / enterprise)
segments.commentary: About 58% of business; grew 37% YoY in FY26, aided by higher H2 PC demand and ASPs. Management expects ~20% average price increase in this category going forward.

segments.name: LIT (Lifestyle IT)
segments.commentary: About 42% of business; grew 24% YoY in FY26. Price increases described as routine only; management says LIT is growing about 2x the industry.

segments.name: Semiconductor
segments.commentary: Grew 131% YoY from a small base; customers include large automotive, robotics and IoT manufacturers. Operations moved into a newly created subsidiary; management says meaningful P&L impact is a few years away.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated a ~20% CAGR (sustained for 20 years) and expects to maintain this trajectory in FY27; regular-business growth aspiration of 15-20% YoY.
Management estimates PES unit market could degrow 5-10% in CY26 (IDC concurs), but with 20-25% price growth, PES revenue could still grow 10-15% on an as-is basis.
Consumer demand could soften in H2 FY27 on affordability; management is discussing 24- and 36-month interest-free EMI schemes with vendors.
Working capital days expected to stay in a similar range in FY27 (CFO).
Distribution PAT margin range of 1.5-1.75% considered applicable to the industry absent mix change; margins described as intact despite price hikes.
Management said the super cycle could continue for another 1-2 years.
Project business (AI data centre) planned for FY27 subject to viability and ROI; funnels of INR 20,000-25,000 crores under consideration.
capex_capacity: Branch network expanded to 55 city branch offices with three new branches added (Nanded, Baramati, Solapur, Maharashtra); 10,000-plus customers across 700-plus towns.
Working capital was increased on inventory to capture demand; management said inventory days cannot fall while regular business grows ~30%.
Project business: FY24-25 included INR 2,000 crores of AI data centre project (Yotta, 512 servers, 4,000 GPUs); no substantial project business in FY26; FY27 plans subject to ROI.
Semiconductor business moved into a separate subsidiary to focus operations and accelerate partnerships and customer acquisition.
Management says it has post-IPO capacity to pick up data centre projects on a selective ROI basis without compromising regular growth.
demand_pricing: Price increases began mainly in H2 FY26; management estimates roughly half of H2 growth (46-47% H2-on-H2) came from pricing, i.e. ~20-22 percentage points.
Management says FY26 growth ex the one large AI project was 31%; FY26 growth without large deals was 15% reported.
Q3 and Q4 FY26 growth reported at 42% and 51% respectively (non-project business).

AI PCs are about 25% of PCs and notebooks sold in India; NVIDIA DGX Spark and Dell (server, storage, PCs, monitors) partnerships cited; Dell described as at low-single-digit share of revenue, expected to reach close to double digits next FY.
IDC: India traditional PC shipments 15.9 million units in CY2025 (+10.2%); IDC flags possible 5-10% dip in CY2026 shipments.
Enterprise refresh delayed by some large corporates during price hikes is reversing as buyers see 30-40% higher prices a year later.
Management said demand is not softening currently; affordability risk in consumer segment in H2.

qa_highlights.question: How much of top-line growth came from pricing vs volume, and what is normalised growth for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases were minimal in H1 and substantial in H2; H2 growth of 46-47% H2-on-H2 included about 20-22 points from price. Management reiterated 20% CAGR for 20 years and expects to maintain it.

qa_highlights.question: What is a PC classified as an AI PC, and how big is that segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Devices with an NPU or high-end processors/GPUs capable of AI workloads; about 25% of PCs and notebooks sold in India are AI PCs, expected to grow further over 1-2 years, lifting ASPs.

qa_highlights.question: Is refresh demand being delayed by price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Some corporates extended refresh cycles initially, but the trend is reversing as buyers realise delay could cost 30-40% more; refresh expected to normalise as in prior years.

qa_highlights.question: Does the semiconductor business carry high working capital, and when will it affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is higher (100-plus days cited), but gross margins and ROCE are higher than the regular business; the business is small, so meaningful margin impact is a few years away.

qa_highlights.question: How will RP Tech participate in AI data centre projects given capital needs and lower margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Funnels of about INR 20,000-25,000 crores are under consideration; the company will pick projects selectively on ROI without compromising 15-20% regular growth; margins vary by project.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of revenue from large deals, enterprise and core distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 had no large AI deals (only INR 5-15 crore deals); enterprise non-AI growth is high, driven by NVIDIA solutions; growth ex-Yotta was 31%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the ST Finserv channel finance programme affect working capital and credit risk?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a non-recourse channel finance programme for channel partners; the company bears no credit risk or funding cost unless it draws funds early, which it normally does not.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT margin aspiration, and what caused the Q4 gross margin dip?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution PAT margin range of 1.5-1.75% is typical absent mix change; Q4 gross margin dip was due to additional provisioning for slow-moving inventory, not a structural decline.

risks_watch: Possible 5-10% unit decline in PC market in CY26 and H2 FY27 consumer softness from affordability as prices rise further.
Potential supply shortages in PES due to component (DRAM, NAND, GPU) pricing firmness.
Data centre project participation is capital-intensive with lower margins; scale of funnel conversion uncertain.
Inventory days (56) unlikely to fall while regular business grows ~30%; slow-moving inventory provision taken in Q4.
Semiconductor working capital cycle of 100-plus days; benefits to margin a few years away.
Dependence on Dell ramp-up (low-single-digit share now, expected near double-digit next FY).
544119|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the PC super cycle and multi-year growth, with growth targets reiterated. Evasive on specifics: declined to give Dell revenue numbers and deferred distribution-channel and margin-trajectory questions offline, and clarified several analyst misreadings of its figures.
key_quotes: So we are very confident to maintain our trajectory of 20% CAGR in the coming year as well.
This is not a 1-quarter tailwind. It is a structural multiyear upgrade super cycle.

Rashi will pick up proportionate to our capacity amongst these opportunities and obviously not run after everything because they are, one, capital intensive, and second, the margins are also lower on this front.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says distribution PAT margin of 1.5-1.75% is the industry-applicable range absent mix change; FY26 EBITDA margin 2.90% (+72 bps) was driven by price hikes, and Q4 gross margin was dented by slow-moving inventory provisioning, so further expansion is not guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Three new branches (Nanded, Baramati, Solapur) already commissioned, taking the network to 55 city branches; no plant or fixed-capacity capex is described, and the AI data centre project is subject to ROI with FY27 timing.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: IDC flags a possible 5-10% dip in CY26 PC shipments and management flags H2 FY27 consumer affordability softness, so unit volumes are expected to fall even though revenue grows about 10-15% on 20-25% price increases.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was only held at a ~20% revenue CAGR and 15-20% regular-business growth, with no raise, and FY26 growth was 15% reported (31% ex the large AI project).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Consumer affordability risk and a possible 5-10% PES unit decline in CY26 could weigh on the 20% CAGR, and DRAM/NAND/GPU component pricing could cause supply shortages.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Dell ramp (low-single-digit share now, near double digits next FY) and AI PC mix (about 25% of Indian PCs/notebooks) are rising, but no specific product launch dates were given.

rows.label: AI data centre project funnel
rows.why: Funnels of INR 20,000-25,000 crores are under consideration, but projects are subject to ROI and FY26 had no substantial project business (FY24-25 included INR 2,000 crores Yotta project).

rows.label: PES price increases of ~20-25%
rows.why: Management expects ~20% average price increase in PES going forward; H2 FY26 pricing added about 20-22 points to H2 growth of 46-47%, and this supports PES revenue growth of 10-15% even as units fall 5-10%.

rows.label: Working capital days held
rows.why: CFO expects working capital days in a similar range (inventory 56, debtors 46, creditors 44, net 58 days), since inventory cannot fall while regular business grows about 30%.

tone.note: Management was confident on the PC super cycle, the 20% CAGR and the 1.5-1.75% PAT margin range, but evasive on Dell revenue numbers and deferred channel and margin questions offline; analysts probed price vs volume split, the Q4 gross margin dip and the AI data centre funnel.

544119|2026-06.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 62% YoY to Rs 5,102 crore, with PAT up 69% to Rs 105 crore and ROCE near 19.5%.
544119|2026-06.overview: Management reported record consolidated revenue, EBITDA, PAT and annualised ROCE for the quarter ended June 2026, driven by price increases in memory, storage and CPUs plus a rise in unit volume. Management said about 30-35% of the revenue growth came from price, 20-25% from quantity, 5-10% from new products and brands, and about 10% from market share gains. Pillars cited were the core distribution engine, the VDA Infosolutions acquisition (67% stake) and a semiconductor JV with Restar Japan (74:26). Management guided to similar growth in Q2 but a slower pace of price increases.

financial_highlights.change: up 55% YoY (CEO cited 50% on the opening remarks)

segments.name: Consolidated group
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 5,102 crore and PAT Rs 105 crore; management stated all-time highs on topline, EBITDA, PAT and annualised ROCE.

segments.name: Commercial vs consumer (B2B mix)
segments.commentary: Management estimates 30-35% consumer-centric and 60-65% commercial (SMB and enterprise). Consumer demand is slowing on affordability, with laptop prices reportedly about 2x year-on-year.

segments.name: Semiconductor / embedded
segments.commentary: Semiconductor revenue in Q1 grew about 70% versus the Q1 FY26 base (not 70% of full-year revenue, per clarification). Growth is described as near double-digit and sometimes higher.

segments.name: VDA Infosolutions (acquired)
segments.commentary: Majority stake (67% in year one) in a pan-India system integrator; FY26 revenue was about Rs 850 crore. Management expects integrated services and value-added solutions to be about 5% of revenue, with Q2 as the next update point.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 growth expected to be similar to Q1 (about 60%), with price increase speed roughly halving; management described Q2 as on a strong footing.
Management expects the price uptrend to continue through FY27, with some slowdown in trajectory.
Management cited third-party reports of about a 10% unit decline in the overall PC market, offset by price increases.
Management reiterated a 20% CAGR track record over 20 years; cited about Rs 3,000 crore as 20% of a Rs 16,000 crore base.
Semiconductor JV targets more than US$100 million revenue within three years; the JV numbers will be reported with Q2 results.
Large AI data centre deals not pursued aggressively in Q1 due to working-capital needs; management said the pipeline should last at least three quarters.
capex_capacity: Two new branches planned in Udaipur and Dhule to extend reach into C and D class cities.
Presence across 57 towns in India, per management.
Semiconductor JV Rashi Restar Semiconductor Solutions Private Limited to be formed as a step-down subsidiary; Restar to take 26% stake, with the existing embedded business moving into the JV.
Plans to add 50+ local engineering hires over the next two years for the semiconductor JV.
Debt-to-equity ratio cited at around 0.5; management said large data centre projects could push it to at least 2x.
demand_pricing: Memory, hard drive and CPU shortages are pushing prices higher; management expects the uptrend to continue through FY27.
Management said about 10% market share gain contributed to growth; unit growth ex-SanDisk was about 20%, with SanDisk unit declines pulling reported units lower.
Entry-level laptops face about 50% shortage per management; medium and premium notebooks available if prices are accepted.
T2 partners are holding elevated channel inventory to earn double-digit margins; management said it is not a concern given demand.
Refurbished PCs are seen as small: management estimated the refurbished pool at 0.5-1 million units against a 15-16 million PC TAM in India.
Management said Dell commercial business contributed about 5% of revenue in the quarter, and is above target for FY27.
Management said the company has allocations from NVIDIA, Intel and AMD; supply risk is tracked weekly ('orange alert').

qa_highlights.question: Why is India demand strong relative to global peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited economic strength, digitisation and education focus, plus data centre-related demand; commercial demand is holding up while consumer demand is slowing on affordability.

qa_highlights.question: Split of Q1 growth between price, volume and mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Price 30-35%, quantity 20-25%, new products and brands 5-10%, market share about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 growth match Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 should show a similar trend (about 60%), but the speed of price increases should roughly halve.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin decline: price or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to mix (higher PES share, lower margin than LIT) and to last year's hived-off subsidiary whose service cost sat in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a supply constraint risk in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is potential risk, but allocations so far are good given supplier relationships; the company tracks it weekly.

qa_highlights.question: Why not pursue large AI data centre deals aggressively?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prioritised run-rate business with higher ROCE and working-capital needs; it still participates through smaller Rs 20-70 crore supplies and focuses on neo-clouds and smaller operators.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY28 look after the tailwinds fade?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 20% CAGR track record and cited VDA and the Restar JV as longer-term growth levers.

qa_highlights.question: Semiconductor JV economics and Restar's investment amount?
qa_highlights.answer: Restar's investment depends on fair valuation at SPA signing, so it is not quantified; management targets over US$100 million JV revenue in three years and said the JV margin profile is higher than co-distribution.

risks_watch: Supply risk: management called supplier allocation a potential H2 risk (orange alert, tracked weekly); entry-level laptops reportedly about 50% short.
Consumer affordability: consumer demand slowing with laptop prices about 2x YoY; management flagged possible consumer pressure in H2.
Channel inventory: T2 partners holding elevated inventory to earn double-digit margins; management said it is not a concern, but it is a watch item for price-driven sell-through.
Price increase pace: Q2 price increases expected to roughly halve; management said unit market may fall about 10% and growth depends on price offsetting volume.
Working capital and leverage: large AI data centre deals not pursued aggressively; management said debt-to-equity (around 0.5) could reach at least 2x if such projects are taken on.
Semiconductor JV: Restar's investment amount unquantified (depends on SPA valuation); JV numbers to be reported with Q2; VDA integration and contribution still undefined until Q2.
key_quotes: So, as of now, I do not have any guidance to give that in next few quarters it will run anything together.
The only correction will happen on the speed of the price increase. Price increase speed should be half.
But yes, this is an orange alert for us. We track it on a weekly basis.
So, we are very optimistic that similar trend will continue in July-August-September also.
So, it is not that we are not there. It is only that we have not prioritized to do INR 500 crores or INR 1000 crores of deals
544119|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, pricing and the Q2 outlook, repeatedly calling the quarter a record and the industry a super cycle. Cautious and evasive on specifics: declined to quantify Restar's JV investment, JV addressable market, VDA contribution and the Dell target, and said it is too early to guide on the acquisitions.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin was 3.38% and PAT margin 2.05%, with gross margin down on mix (higher PES share, lower margin than LIT) and management guided price increases to roughly halve in Q2, so spreads are not expected to widen.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Only two small branches (Udaipur, Dhule) are planned, with no size or capex quantified and 57-town presence; AI data centre deals were deprioritised on working capital, so no large new capacity is firmly committed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Units grew about 20-25% in Q1 ex-SanDisk, but third-party data show about a 10% unit decline in the overall PC market and entry-level laptops are about 50% short, so volume growth depends on supply and price offsetting it.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Debt-to-equity is about 0.5 and no utilisation figure was given; capex is not discussed beyond branches and the Restar JV, and management said large data-centre projects could push D/E to at least 2x, which it is avoiding for now.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided Q2 FY27 growth similar to Q1 (about 60%) with price increase speed roughly halving, so no upgrade is signalled and the price tailwind is fading.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged H2 supplier allocation risk (orange alert, tracked weekly), consumer affordability pressure with laptop prices about 2x YoY, and possible unit market decline of about 10%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New products and brands contributed 5-10% of Q1 growth and the semiconductor JV (Restar 26%) is being formed, but no specific product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Semiconductor JV revenue target above US$100 million in three years
rows.when: JV numbers reported with Q2 FY27; target over three years
rows.why: Management has a concrete target (over US$100 million in three years) and says JV margins are higher than co-distribution, though Restar's investment and JV addressable market were not quantified.

rows.label: VDA Infosolutions integration and contribution
rows.why: VDA (67% stake, FY26 revenue about Rs 850 crore) is expected to be about 5% of revenue as integrated services, but management declined to quantify its contribution until Q2.

rows.label: Large AI data centre deals deferred
rows.when: pipeline lasts at least three quarters
rows.why: Deals were not pursued aggressively in Q1 due to working-capital needs (working capital at 56 days); management says the pipeline should last at least three quarters, and D/E could reach 2x if taken on.

tone.note: Management was confident on pricing, demand and the Q2 outlook (about 60% growth, record quarter), but cautious and evasive on Restar's JV investment, VDA contribution and the Dell target; analysts pushed on the gross margin decline, price vs volume split and H2 supply risk.

544120|2026-03.headline: Capital SFB Q4 FY26 PAT rose 17% YoY to ₹40 crores, with NIM up to 4.06% and FY27 ROA guided to 1.35%–1.4%.
544120|2026-03.overview: Gross advances reached ₹8,687 crores (+20.9% YoY, +6.4% QoQ) and total deposits crossed ₹10,000 crores (+20% YoY). Q4 PPOP rose 28% YoY to ₹62 crores and cost of deposits eased to 5.75% from 5.86% QoQ, with NIM at 4.06% versus 4.01% in Q3. Asset quality was broadly stable: GNPA 2.54%, NNPA 1.24%, with Q4 credit cost of 0.26% driven by higher provisioning (PCR 51.89%) rather than losses. Management guided to FY27 advances growth of 22%+, ROA of 1.35%–1.4%, and credit cost of 0.15%–0.25%.

segments.name: MSME / business banking
segments.commentary: Growth driver: +9% QoQ and +46% YoY in Q4. Management expects it to remain a growth leader in FY27.

segments.name: LAP (loan against property)
segments.commentary: +5% QoQ and +19% YoY; yield 12.33% in Q4 vs 12.56% in Q3. Named as a FY27 growth leader.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Book grew 7% QoQ but net NPA was static at 2.76% vs 2.75%. Growth to be slower than the overall book, limited to Punjab and Haryana.

segments.name: Mortgage / housing
segments.commentary: Housing yield 9.85% in Q4 vs 9.83% in Q3. Cited as a driver for growth in newer states.

segments.name: NBFC-MFI
segments.commentary: Outstanding net NPA ₹5.49 crores vs ₹6.08 crores a quarter earlier; total exposure about ₹39 crores. No fresh lending in Q4; an OTS was signed with one lender.

segments.name: Out-of-Punjab advances
segments.commentary: 24% of advances at March 2026 vs 21% a year earlier; growing more than twice the Punjab rate YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 secured advances growth of 22%+; advances above ₹16,000 crores by FY29.
Branches: target of 235 by end of FY27 (current year) and 300+ by FY29.
NIM expected to improve slightly in Q1 FY27 and more meaningfully in Q2; 53% of term deposits are high-priced and reprice in the next two quarters.
FY27 ROA target of 1.35%–1.4%, rising to 1.6%+ by FY29; ROE of 15%+ by FY29.
FY27 opex/average assets guided to 2.9%–3.0% (lower bias), with opex/average assets below 2.85% over the medium term.
FY27 credit cost guided to 0.15%–0.25% with negative bias; target of about 0.3% up to FY29.
Fee income/average assets guided to 0.85%–0.95% with upward bias; Banca to be expanded by one product in FY27 and one more later.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 211 across 5 states and 2 union territories at March 2026; 77.3% are SURU branches.
Target of 235 branches by end of FY27 and 300+ by FY29; 50% of new branches to be opened outside Punjab and 40–45% in Punjab.
Management said cost of new branches in FY27 is mainly last-mile branch cost, as senior and head-office costs are already built in.
Business per branch (5+ year branches) is ₹106 crores in Punjab vs ₹73 crores outside Punjab; PPOP of 5+ year branches is 2.75%–3.25% vs 2.1% entity level.
demand_pricing: Disbursements were ₹919 crores in Q4 (+20% YoY) and ₹3,508 crores in FY26 (+23% YoY).
Average ticket size ₹18.3 lakh vs ₹17.8 lakh in Q3; about 98% of the book is secured and about 89% of the non-corporate book is backed by property or FDRs.

Yields: agriculture 12.54% (vs 12.62%), business 10.55% (vs 10.6%), corporate 10.77% (vs 10.8%); overall advance yield fell to about 10.8% from about 11.1%, partly due to a 25 bps rate cut and agri accounts moving to NPA with interest reversals.
Fee income was ₹25.8 crores in Q4 vs ₹26.1 crores in Q3 (0.9% of assets, vs 1.0% a year earlier); treasury income fell due to weaker market opportunities.
Cost of deposits 5.75% in Q4 vs 5.86% in Q3; average CD ratio 82.3%, period-end 86.7%; retail deposits above 90%.

qa_highlights.question: Gross NPA additions and provisioning: are provisions increasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ₹22 crore FY provision figure includes tax; PCR was raised to 51.89% from 50.45%, so provisioning was increased within the profit outlook.

qa_highlights.question: Agri NPA stickiness: will it fall back toward 2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not target 2%; it expects agri NPA to stay range-bound with a lower bias. Recoveries concentrate in Q1 and Q3 cash-flow periods.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the new ECL framework on credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial view is P&L neutral to positive, as current provisions are considered sufficient against the ECL requirement; detailed evaluation is ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Co-lending / BC model and FLDG cover?
qa_highlights.answer: The bank runs a business correspondent lending model (not co-lending) with more than one partner, and the FLDG cover is 5% per regulation. Branches are to remain 90–95% of disbursements.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of the NII margin expansion and CD ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Term deposit repricing (53% repricing in Q1–Q2) and an improving CD ratio are the two NIM levers; management expects an opex/average assets ratio of 2.9%–3.0% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost and cost-to-income guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost for FY27 is 0.15%–0.25%. The Q4 credit cost of 0.26% was provisioning-driven, linked to NBFC-MFI slippage. Cost-to-income is expected to improve, with opex/average assets at 2.9%–3.0%.

risks_watch: Agri asset quality: net NPA at 2.76%, and monsoon or input-cost stress could affect the book, although management cites Punjab irrigation and collateral.
Pace of deposit repricing and whether NIM reaches the guided improvement in Q1–Q2 FY27.
Yield pressure: advance yields fell to about 10.8% amid rate cuts and NPA reversals; 8–10 bps of the decline is described as temporary.
Fee income and treasury income momentum; Banca and fee targets depend on new product approvals.
ECL transition impact, which management expects to be P&L neutral to positive but is still under evaluation.
Growth outside Punjab through business correspondent partners, which is early-stage and carries FLDG exposure.

rows.why: Management guides secured advances growth of 22%+ for FY27 after advances grew 20.9% YoY to ₹8,687 crores and disbursements rose 23% in FY26 to ₹3,508 crores.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q4 PAT rose 17% YoY and ROA reached 1.33% in Q4 vs 1.16% in Q3, but FY27 ROA guide of 1.35%–1.4% is only modestly above the 1.23% FY26 level, so an upgrade depends on sustaining the Q4 run rate.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Agri net NPA is 2.76% and stuck, NBFC-MFI slippage drove the 0.26% Q4 credit cost against a FY27 guide of 0.15%–0.25%, and yields fell to ~10.8% from ~11.1%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans to expand Banca by one product in FY27 and one more later, and fee income guidance of 0.85%–0.95% of average assets depends on new product approvals.

rows.label: Term deposit repricing lifts NIM
rows.why: 53% of term deposits are high-priced and reprice in the next two quarters, with cost of deposits already down to 5.75% from 5.86% QoQ.

rows.label: Opex/average assets held at 2.9%-3.0%
rows.why: Cost-to-income fell to 58.2% in Q4 from 61% for FY26, and the 5+ year branches run PPOP of 2.75%-3.25% vs 2.1% at entity level, with new branches mainly last-mile cost.

rows.label: Out-of-Punjab growth via BC partners
rows.why: Out-of-Punjab advances are 24% of the book vs 21% a year earlier, and 50% of new branches are to open outside Punjab, though the BC model is early-stage with 5% FLDG exposure.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 22%+ FY27 growth, NIM repricing, and branch build-out to 235, and defensive on agri NPA stickiness and the 0.26% Q4 credit cost, which it attributed to provisioning. Analysts pressed on asset quality and provisioning.

544120|2026-06.headline: Capital SFB Q1 FY27 PAT rose 29% YoY to INR 41.3 crore, with NIM at 4.21% and GNPA down to 2.47%.
544120|2026-06.overview: Gross advances reached INR 9,074 crore, up 22% YoY and 4.5% QoQ, while deposits grew 16% YoY to INR 10,596 crore with CASA at 36.7%. NIM improved to 4.21% from 4.06% a year ago, helped by deposit repricing and a higher average CD ratio of 83%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 2.47% and NNPA at 1.14%, as the bank raised PCR to 54.5%. Management guided to stable NIM near 4.2% for FY27, ROA of 1.35-1.4% for FY27, and 22% advance growth.

financial_highlights.change: from 4.06% in Q4 FY26 and 4.06% in Q1 FY26
GNPA -28 bps YoY, -7 bps QoQ; NNPA from 1.39% YoY and 1.24% QoQ
broadly in line with last year

segments.name: Business loans (MSME and other)
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 27% of book (22% a year ago) and 35% of incremental disbursements; MSME grew 49% YoY and 11% QoQ, with average ticket INR 28 lakh and yield on business loans at 10.5%.

segments.name: Mortgage
segments.commentary: Stable at 25% of book (around 26% a year ago); grew 3% QoQ and 10% YoY, with housing yield at 9.87% vs 9.85% in Q4 FY26; average housing ticket INR 20-25 lakh.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Share fell to about 27% from 30% a year ago; target ticket INR 5-35 lakh (average INR 30 lakh), with yields of 12-12.5% over the last 7-9 quarters and 50% LTV collateral.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Stable at 14% of book; calibrated lending to well-rated corporates.

segments.name: Loan Against Property (LAP)
segments.commentary: Yield of 12.27%; grew 5% QoQ and 18% YoY.

segments.name: Consumption loans
segments.commentary: Stable at around 7% of book, mostly top-up loans; 2-3% of the book is loan against deposits or securities.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Advances outside Punjab grew over 30% YoY and are 25% of the book (24% in Q4 FY26, 21% a year ago).

guidance_outlook: FY27 advance growth guided at 22%; FY29 loan book target of INR 16,000 crore plus.
NIM expected to hold around 4.2% through FY27, with expansion in FY28 and FY29 as average CD ratio rises from 83% toward mid-to-high 80s.
ROA targeted at 1.35-1.4% in FY27 and 1.6% plus by FY29; ROE targeted at 15% plus by FY29.
Medium-term net NPA target of around 1% (below 1% per Vision 2029); management expects stable PCR from here.
Opex to see some improvement in FY27 (currently 2.95-2.98% of assets) after Q1 salary increments; larger opex growth expected in FY29.
Around INR 1,597 crore of term deposits reprice in Q2 FY27, with a 10-12 bps benefit that management expects to be offset by higher incremental deposit costs.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 216 branches across 5 states and 2 union territories as of June 2026; 74% of branches are semi-urban and rural.

Average CD ratio at 83% (vs 80.9% in Q1 FY26); management targets mid-to-high 80s, implying an incremental 3-6% from deployment of investments and interbank balances (yielding about 7-7.5%) into advances at about 10.5-11%.
Liquidity coverage ratio averaged 184.18%; capital adequacy at 21.6%.
demand_pricing: Competition in housing loans from PSU banks has eased due to deposit repricing, with mortgage growth recovering to 10% YoY; housing yields held at about 9.87%.
Private universal banks focus above INR 1 crore tickets, leaving the INR 10-50 lakh MSME band to the bank; management says it prices slightly above market for service and turnaround time.
Agri yields are priced 25-35 bps above PSB rates for INR 5-25 lakh tickets; management cites industry-wide risk premium rather than bank-specific pricing.
Cost of deposits fell to 5.6%; the spread target of cost of deposits vs advance yield is 5.05-5.3%. Advance yield fell to 10.9% from 11.1% a year ago.
Management said 50% of advances are fixed-rate and 50% floating-rate; 48.67% of the book resets annually, mainly MCLR-linked; MCLR was raised by 10 bps in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Split of MSME growth between Punjab and Haryana, and how it is trending
qa_highlights.answer: MSME (INR 28 lakh average ticket, middle-income, collateralised) grew 49% YoY and 11% QoQ; growth within Punjab and outside Punjab, and between Punjab and Haryana, is similar. Advances outside Punjab are 25% of the book vs 24% a quarter ago and 21% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Why PCR has been rising over recent quarters and whether it will stay stable
qa_highlights.answer: PCR was raised to 54.5% to move net NPA towards the medium-term 1% target; management says most of that action is done and it expects a stable PCR from here.

qa_highlights.question: Headroom for cost of deposit repricing and ROA path
qa_highlights.answer: Remaining repricing is not material; the bulk was done in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27. ROA is targeted at 1.35-1.4% in FY27 and 1.6%+ by FY29; Q1 ROA was 1.3% vs 1.18%, and PPOP margin rose to 2.04% from 1.94%.

qa_highlights.question: What keeps NIM stable at around 4.2% given cost-of-deposit and yield pressure
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,597 crore of term deposits reprice in Q2 FY27 for a 10-12 bps benefit, which management expects to be offset by higher incremental deposit costs. Advance yield fell to 10.9% from 11.1%; 50% of the book is fixed and 50% floating; NIM expansion is expected in FY28-29 as average CD ratio (83%) rises to mid-to-high 80s.

qa_highlights.question: Why PSU competition in housing eased and whether mortgage growth will pick up
qa_highlights.answer: Deposit repricing helped the bank compete with PSBs in the INR 20-25 lakh housing ticket; mortgage grew 3% QoQ and 10% YoY at a 9.87% yield vs 9.85% in Q4, but management says growth will stay moderate with some portion still to be recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Agri yield levels and risk mitigation
qa_highlights.answer: Agri average ticket is INR 30 lakh (range INR 5-35 lakh), with yields of 12-12.5% over the last 7-9 quarters, priced 25-35 bps over PSB rates in the INR 5-25 lakh band; collateral LTV is 50%, and management attributes the premium to industry-wide risk perception.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 repricing of about INR 1,597 crore of term deposits: the 10-12 bps benefit is expected to be offset by higher incremental deposit costs, so NIM holding at about 4.2% depends on this.
Advance yield has fallen to 10.9% from 11.1%, and the business loan yield is 10.5%; further yield compression would pressure the 5.05-5.3% spread target.
SMA-2 rose to 3.11% from 2.71% in the quarter, though total SMA-1 and SMA-2 fell to 4.78% from 5.47% a year ago; management called the rise not meaningful.
Opex at 2.95-2.98% of assets; management expects a moderate FY27 increase, with larger opex growth in FY29, which could weigh on the ROA path.
Average CD ratio of 83% needs to reach mid-to-high 80s; management says advance growth will outpace deposit growth in Q2 and Q4, and deposit growth is strongest in Q1 and Q3.
Universal bank conversion depends on getting net NPA to about 1%, which the bank currently reports at 1.14%.
key_quotes: We expect NIM to stabilize at the current levels for the FY27 and start further expanding, supported by improving CD ratio i n the coming years.
So, our advance should outpace our deposit growth for some peers, maybe 2 years or so, which is the one factor which we are taking care.
Now we think a majority of that action has been done.
We are not taking advantage of that and believe that particular benefit will be taken away /off setted by the increasing cost of deposit.
544120|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and specific on growth, asset quality and the ROA trajectory, with the NIM and yield outlook framed as stable rather than expanding in FY27. Management was more cautious on housing growth, which it said is still recovering, and on how much cost-of-deposit repricing is left.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM guided to hold near 4.2% through FY27 (Q1 at 4.21% vs 4.06% a year ago), with expansion only in FY28-FY29 as average CD ratio rises from 83% toward mid-to-high 80s; Q2 repricing of INR 1,597 crore (10-12 bps benefit) is expected to be offset by higher incremental deposit costs.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reaffirmed 22% FY27 advance growth against gross advances of INR 9,074 crore (+22% YoY) and deposits +16% YoY, with MSME growing 49% YoY and fresh disbursements +17% YoY to INR 1,009 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Average CD ratio at 83% is well below the 80%+ utilisation threshold framing for a capex trigger, the bank has 216 branches and CAR is 21.6%, and capex was not discussed on the call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 guidance (22% advance growth, ROA 1.35-1.4%) rather than raising it, with Q1 ROA at 1.3% and opex to rise moderately in FY27.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: SMA-2 rose to 3.11% from 2.71% in the quarter and advance yield fell to 10.9% from 11.1%, which could pressure the 5.05-5.3% spread target and the 1.35-1.4% ROA path if not offset.

rows.label: Net NPA glide path to about 1% (universal bank conversion)
rows.why: Net NPA is 1.14% after PCR was raised to 54.5%, and management expects stable PCR from here, so further NNPA reduction is guided but not yet dated within 2-4 quarters.

rows.label: Term deposit repricing benefit in Q2 FY27
rows.why: About INR 1,597 crore of term deposits reprice for a 10-12 bps benefit, but management expects this to be offset by higher incremental deposit costs, so net gain is uncertain.

rows.label: CD ratio rise from 83% toward mid-to-high 80s
rows.why: Average CD ratio is 83% (vs 80.9% a year ago); reaching mid-to-high 80s implies a 3-6% shift of investments and interbank balances (yielding 7-7.5%) into advances at 10.5-11%.

tone.note: Management was confident on 22% advance growth, ROA 1.35-1.4% and asset quality/PCR stability, but cautious on housing recovery and on how much cost-of-deposit repricing remains; analysts pushed on NIM sustainability given falling advance yield (10.9% from 11.1%).

544120|2026-09.headline: Capital SFB Q2 FY27: gross advances up 23.4% YoY to INR9,755 crore, PAT up about 31% to INR46 crore, NIM 4.24%.
544120|2026-09.overview: Gross advances grew 23.4% YoY and 7.5% QoQ to INR9,755 crore, with disbursements of INR1,095 crore (up 36% YoY). Total deposits reached INR10,831 crore (up 16.2% YoY), with CASA at 34.5% and cost of deposits down to 5.68% from 5.92% a year ago. Asset quality improved, with gross NPA at 2.36% and net NPA at 1.12%, while PPOP of INR68 crore and PAT of INR46 crore rose about 31% YoY. Management reiterated the Vision 2029 targets of over INR16,000 crore loan book and 300-plus branches, and flagged a possible regulatory change to bancassurance income.

financial_highlights.change: vs 33.9% a year ago; lower QoQ (seasonal)
vs 5.92% a year ago; 5.6% in prior quarter per management
vs 4.04% a year ago, 4.21% last quarter

segments.name: Business loans
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 28% of the book, up from 23% a year ago and 27% last quarter. Management said business loans are growing faster than the overall book.

segments.name: Mortgages (LAP)
segments.commentary: About 24% of advances, down from 26% a year ago and 25% last quarter.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: About 26% of advances, down from 27% last quarter. Agri grew 6.23% QoQ; lending is confined to Punjab and Haryana.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Held deliberately flat at about 14% of advances, lending only to well-rated borrowers.

segments.name: Consumption
segments.commentary: About 7% of portfolio, growing 6.89% QoQ and 21.9% YoY; net NPA 0.47%. Offered mainly as a second or third product to existing customers.

segments.name: Punjab vs outside Punjab
segments.commentary: Outside Punjab has 21% of branches (47), 25.7% of advances and 8.2% of deposits. Outside-Punjab advances grew 39% YoY vs 19% for Punjab; GNPA 0.87% outside vs 2.88% in Punjab.

guidance_outlook: FY27 loan growth guidance was 20-22% at the start of the year; H1 growth was 23%, and management said it is aiming to overachieve.
Vision 2029 targets: gross advances over INR16,000 crore and more than 300 branches by FY29. Management said the current run rate exceeds what is needed.
ROA target of 1.6% by FY29 from 1.39% today, driven by NIM expansion (guided 4.3-4.35%, a 7-12 bps gain) and opex (operating cost to average assets guided 2.80-2.85% by FY29 from about 3.05%).
Target net NPA below 1%.
Target of 30%+ branches outside Punjab by FY29, with out-of-Punjab advances expected at 32-37% of the book.
Universal bank license aspiration after FY29, at a balance sheet of about INR21,000-23,000 crore.
capex_capacity: Network of 222 branches across 5 states and 2 union territories; 77% of branches are in semi-urban and rural centres (SURU), contributing 75% of deposits.
Business per branch outside Punjab reached INR80 crore-plus for branches of 5 years and above, vs INR72 crore at end-Q4 FY26.
Target of more than 300 branches by FY29, with 30%+ outside Punjab.
Rajasthan presence is limited to 7 branches; the bank is following an asset-first approach in new geographies such as Rajasthan and NCR.
Capital adequacy ratio of 20.8% (Tier 1 18.5%), with no immediate need to raise fresh capital.
demand_pricing: Industry credit grew about 19.4% YoY vs deposit growth of about 17.8% as of September 2026.
RBI raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% in October 2026 and moved to calibrated tightening; management expects rates to stay higher for longer.
Yield on advances was 11% in Q2 FY27, flat YoY and up 10 bps QoQ. The October repo hike has not yet flowed into advance yields.
About 52% of advances are fixed-rate and 48% floating; EBR-linked loans are 13-14% of the portfolio and get a 25 bps EBR increase from 1 November 2026.
Term deposit ATS is about INR12 lakh; savings average ticket is about INR50,000. Retail deposits are over 90% of the total, with rollover above 90%.
Management sees its deposit premium at 25-35 bps over top private sector universal banks.

qa_highlights.question: Is the weak monsoon affecting the agriculture book, and is collection efficiency holding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is not visible in Punjab and Haryana, citing canal water and tube wells. H1 gross slippage was 1.11% annualised, net slippage 0.24%, and SMA1+2 fell to 3.31%. Early paddy productivity data is the same or better than last year in 25 of 26 districts.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the cost of deposits fallen only 22 bps when the RBI cut rates by 125 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank has a premium over peers, a CASA ratio above 34%, and fixed-rate TD repricing. About 60-62% of the benefit has come through repricing, and the cost of deposits is 5.68%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NIM path and the scope to expand it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided NIM to 4.3-4.35% from 4.24%, citing a CD ratio move from 85.4% toward the mid-to-high 80s over 1.5-2 years. It said this can happen without changing deposit or loan pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Why are consumption-loan yields low, and will the bank go to fresh customers via dealers?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumption loans are about 7% of the book, mainly cross-sell to existing customers. About 25-30% is loan against own FDRs at 7.5-8%. Management said pilots are running to fast-track sub-products, but it did not give details.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the draft IRDAI circular on bancassurance, and what is the other fee income plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Bancassurance commission was INR10.2 crore out of INR30 crore non-interest income, about 33%. Management said the bank is waiting for a draft circular, expects an impact that is not material, and cited a 0.92% non-interest income-to-assets ratio. The ROA plan does not rely on fee income.

qa_highlights.question: What are the universal bank aspirations and when will they be pursued?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims to apply for a universal bank licence after FY29, at a balance sheet of about INR21,000-23,000 crore, once the bank reaches the FY29 targets.

risks_watch: Weak monsoon and drought in parts of India (management said Punjab and Haryana remain unaffected); watch agri slippages and SMA trends.
Margin pressure if deposit repricing outpaces the loan-yield pass-through in a higher-for-longer rate cycle; yield on advances was flat YoY at 11%.
Bancassurance fee income (about 33% of non-interest income) at risk from the IRDAI draft circular; the bank has not yet detailed alternatives.
Growth and profitability outside Punjab: CASA there is 25.3% vs 35.3% in Punjab, and outside-Punjab deposits are only 8.2% of the total.
CASA ratio fell QoQ (seasonal, per management) in a high term deposit rate environment.
544120|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and the Vision 2029 targets, with management saying it is growth-hungry and that the run rate exceeds plan. More measured on rates and the IRDAI draft, where it said it is waiting for a draft circular and declined to size the alternatives.
key_quotes: Our priorities are quite simple, remain the same, grow the franchise, strengthen the deposit base and protect the quality of the balance sheet.
We are a growth-hungry organization, and we believe the complete foundation is available to grow.
We will keep lending the way we always have, secured, granular with careful customer selection and strong collection.

544122|2026-03.headline: Entero FY26 revenue rose 31.5% like-for-like to INR6,591 crore with 4% EBITDA margin; FY27 guidance is 23% growth and 5% margin excluding new acquisitions.
544122|2026-03.overview: FY26 met all three initial targets: like-for-like revenue growth of 31.5% (organic 15.6%, inorganic 16%), 4% EBITDA margin (+67 bps) and operating cash flow of INR96.2 crore. Q4 revenue grew 42.6% YoY, with organic growth of 17.1% and acquisitions contributing 26%, and Q4 EBITDA margin reached 4.5%. Minority interest jumped sharply in Q4 (about 38% of PAT) due to an abnormal, pulled-forward MedTech sale at a partly-owned subsidiary, which management says will normalise. FY27 guidance is 23% consolidated revenue growth excluding new acquisitions (about 11 points from calendarisation), 5% EBITDA margin, and at least 50% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion.

segments.name: MedTech
segments.commentary: Now above INR1,000 crore annualised revenue after 3 MedTech acquisitions in FY26 (Anand Chemiceutics, Ace Cardiopathy, Bio de Technology). Management says MedTech is over 15% of revenue, could reach about 20% in 2-3 years, and earns higher margins than pharma due to commercial/agency role.

segments.name: Pharma distribution
segments.commentary: Remains the core business with about 100,000 retail pharmacies, 3,600 hospitals, 97,500 SKUs and 3,300+ manufacturers. Management expects pharma and MedTech to contribute equally to FY27 organic growth.

segments.name: GLP-1
segments.commentary: Management says current GLP-1 sales are about INR10-12 crore per month, roughly 5% of industry GLP value, with a share above its overall India share due to cold-chain warehouses; included in FY27 guidance.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 23% YoY excluding new acquisitions; about 11 points from calendarisation of FY26 acquisitions and the rest organic (management also cited about 22% in one answer).
FY27 EBITDA margin of 5%, about 50 bps above Q4 FY26's 4.5%, from MedTech mix, operating leverage and exiting low-margin businesses.
EBITDA-to-operating cash flow conversion of at least 50% in FY27.
Tax rate of about 22-23% for FY27.
Minority interest to be about 25-27% of PAT before minority interest in FY27, down from about 38% in Q4.
Finance cost to stay relatively stable for a couple of quarters, then decline over the next couple of years as IPO funds were used up.
No new acquisitions assumed for the next 6-8 months; guidance would be revised upwards if acquisitions are made. Acquisitions are priced at 5-7x EV/EBITDA.
capex_capacity: Seven acquisitions closed in FY26, including 3 in MedTech; management says no new acquisitions are planned for the next 6-8 months, focusing on organic growth.
Some MedTech IVD machines are placed at customer sites on 5-year reagent rental contracts and are depreciated; cardiology and other MedTech lines carry little depreciating equipment.
Cold-chain facilities in all warehouses support GLP-1 distribution.
Depreciation rose about 50% QoQ in Q4, and interest costs rose because acquisitions were debt- or investment-funded after IPO proceeds were used up.
demand_pricing: Organic growth outperformed IPM by 1.6x for FY26 (15.6% vs IPM); Q3 and Q4 multiplier fell to about 1.4x as IPM grew about 12% versus 7-8% earlier, while organic growth stayed at 16-17%.
FY27 like-for-like growth is about 15% (1.5x IPM) per management; some low-ROIC businesses are being exited and some are now booked on a net-revenue basis, lowering reported revenue.
Gross margin gains come from scale purchasing and a commercial/agency role; full commercial role accounts for 10-15%+ of sales, with margins at least double normal distribution margins.
Management pointed to the 8-15% gross margin band on slide 28 for distribution; Q4 gross margin was 10.9%.
Middle East conflict: direct imports are a very small share of sales, so management says the company is largely insulated.

qa_highlights.question: Why did minority interest jump in Q4 and how much will it be in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 minority interest was abnormally high, about 38% of PAT, due to a customer pulling forward equipment sales at a partly-owned subsidiary. FY27 minority share is guided at about 25-27% of pre-minority PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 23% FY27 growth include calendarisation and GLP-1?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Calendarisation is about 11 points, and GLP-1 is built into guidance, with the company taking a disproportionate share given its cold-chain network.

qa_highlights.question: Why is working capital falling, and how much working capital will FY27 growth need?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop mainly to higher payables from MedTech, which has longer credit terms than pharma. Q4 annualised revenue of about INR7,600-8,000 crore means most working capital is already in the balance sheet, so incremental needs should be small.

qa_highlights.question: Will acquisitions continue, and at what valuations?
qa_highlights.answer: No new acquisitions are assumed for 6-8 months. Valuations remain 5-7x EV/EBITDA, and call options on remaining stakes are pre-agreed, typically over 3 to 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROCE outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 ROCE above 20%, with further upside possible over time, though not necessarily in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the company's competitive moat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a two-way network: about 100,000 customers and over 3,000 manufacturers. It said retail consolidation will stay limited, with chains under 15,000 stores versus over 1 million pharmacies.

risks_watch: Minority interest of 25-27% of PAT in FY27 materially reduces attributable earnings; watch for further put-option liability effects on net worth, which was flat in FY26.
Finance cost is expected to stay stable for a couple of quarters before declining; interest and depreciation rose sharply in Q4.
IPM growth outperformance has narrowed to about 1.4x as IPM rose to about 12%; FY27 organic growth depends on sustaining this.

qa_highlights.question: What is capacity utilisation at the Sundargarh plant, its total capacity and the timeline to full utilisation?

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split by product?

qa_highlights.question: Which products earn the highest margins, and what is the crash barrier margin?

qa_highlights.answer: Rejected: export EN10255/EN10217 galvanized orders, 1161/3601 BIS orders, and hollow section orders with thin margins, because galvanizing tanks are full. Priority goes to dealers under MOUs, then end users are not taken; no percentage of rejected orders was quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 revenue outlook?

544133|2026-03.headline: Exicom Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 46% YoY to INR 388 crores and consolidated EBITDA turned positive at INR 0.3 crore for the first time since Tritium acquisition.
544133|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 revenue grew 33% YoY to INR 282 crores with EBITDA of INR 29.9 crores (10.6% margin), driven by Critical Power (+23% YoY) and EVSE (+60% YoY). Consolidated revenue of INR 388 crores (+46% YoY) included Tritium, and consolidated EBITDA turned marginally positive. For full FY26, consolidated EBITDA was still negative at INR 103 crores and adjusted PAT was negative at INR 258 crores, with higher finance cost and one-time exceptional costs (VRS, Tritium retention, labour code). Management flagged a temporary inventory and receivables build as Hyderabad ramped up alongside Gurgaon.

segments.name: EVSE / EV charging (standalone)
segments.commentary: Grew 60% YoY in Q4 and 40% for FY26; record quarterly EV charging revenue of INR 88 crores (management figure, basis not specified). Full-year EVSE consolidated growth 72%; Q4 consolidated EVSE +83% YoY.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about $10 million (sales $9.7 million), record order intake $10 million; EBITDA losses down about 30% QoQ. Management targets ~3x revenue and 25% lower EBITDA losses, with EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Tritium: revenue to scale about 3x and EBITDA losses to fall about 25%; EBITDA breakeven targeted in Q4 FY27. Management said losses fall less sharply than revenue because low-cost acquired inventory is being used up, with margins normalising after about one quarter.
Exports: target to lift Critical Power export share to 20% in FY27 from ~10-15%.
Non-telecom BESS: internal target of over INR 50 crores business in FY26 from pilot-stage orders; management sees BESS possibly reaching ~30% of Critical Power over 2-3 years if successful.

Three Tritium products (TRI-FLEX inverter and two others) launching May-July 2026; management cites about INR 850 crores of combined FY28 revenue potential, subject to pilots. TRI-FLEX hyperscaler factory acceptance test ongoing, potentially $30-35 million FY28 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What charging infrastructure is needed for commercial EV adoption and where is it happening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said adoption is in fixed-route captive use such as ports, cement distribution and mining with 200-300 trucks; intercity commercial electrification is still about two years away.

qa_highlights.question: What is the product and revenue potential of the TRI-FLEX inverter and its applications?
qa_highlights.answer: TRI-FLEX converts grid power to high-voltage DC for DC microgrids, BESS integration and 800V data centres. A hyperscaler pilot is in testing and, if successful, could unlock significant FY28 revenue ($30-35 million cited).

qa_highlights.question: How will the company win customers for the two other new Tritium products in the US and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said development was done with existing strategic customers, and it has line of sight to long-term contracts once pilots succeed.

qa_highlights.question: Does Exicom have OEM tie-ups for supplying chargers with vehicles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Exicom is the largest home charger maker, with about a 50% chance a new EV in India comes with an Exicom charger, and it has OEM partnerships for home and fast chargers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS offering and its scaling path over 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets commercial and industrial modular BESS, not utility, transmission, distribution or home. About 10-20 small projects were deployed in Q4, with an FY26 target above INR 50 crores, and BESS could reach about 30% of Critical Power over 2-3 years.

544133|2026-06.headline: Exicom Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 57% YoY to INR237 crore with EBITDA margin at 8.8%; consolidated EBITDA loss narrowed to INR22 crore.
544133|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 57% YoY to INR236.8 crore, with Critical Power up 80% to INR176 crore and EV up 15% to INR61 crore. Standalone EBITDA more than doubled to INR20.9 crore (8.8% margin), helped by operating leverage and richer mix. Consolidated revenue rose 61% to INR331.1 crore, but consolidated EBITDA was a loss of INR21.9 crore (down from INR38.6 crore loss), as Tritium margins normalised after drawing down low-cost acquired inventory. Management guided to consolidated EBITDA breakeven within two quarters and Tritium breakeven by Q4 FY27, while working capital rose on parallel Gurgaon and Hyderabad plant operations and higher receivables.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR61 crore, up 15% YoY but down QoQ from Q4 DC-charger pull-forward; consolidated EV grew 50%. FY26 standalone EV revenue was INR277 crore, about 30% of total.

segments.commentary: Revenue about USD10-10.5 million in Q1, second consecutive quarter above USD10 million; bookings about USD20.8-21 million, roughly double the usual ~USD10 million per quarter.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q4 seasonality in Indian business and Tritium's low-cost acquired inventory eroding, lowering Tritium margins. It still expects Tritium EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27 and consolidated breakeven within the next two quarters, without specifying Q2 or Q3.

qa_highlights.question: When will Tritium's doubled order intake convert to revenue, and is the 3x growth and Q4 FY27 breakeven target still intact?

qa_highlights.question: What is Hyderabad plant utilisation and where will it reach in FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EV revenue mix and growth outlook, and why is the AC capacity figure inconsistent with the annual report (42,000 to 222,000 units)?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 standalone EV revenue was INR277 crore, about 30% of revenue, with mix expected to stay similar or rise slightly. Management said the 222,000 figure is right and that 48,000 was single-shift, with the doubling based on double-shift operation; it will revert with an exact answer.

qa_highlights.answer: Standalone depreciation rose about 67% YoY to INR10.3 crore, with management attributing an increase of INR10-12 crore to the new plant. Tritium's higher depreciation reflects capitalised R&D and acquisition-related servicing costs, which management expects to be amortised over 5-7 years.

qa_highlights.question: Can EV charger market share and unit volumes be estimated from EV registrations, and why was standalone EV growth only 15% when AC demand is strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has a very high share of wallbox chargers but not portable chargers, and volume depends on whether OEMs bundle wallboxes. The 15% standalone EV growth reflects Q4 DC charger pull-forward; AC may have grown about 30% and DC about 10%.

544134|2026-03.headline: Platinum Industries Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 37% YoY to INR 132 crore, EBITDA up 95% to INR 15.3 crore; FY27 guidance above 40% revenue growth.
544134|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 132 crore (+37% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 15.3 crore (+95%, margin 11.6%, +350 bps) and PAT of INR 14.8 crore (+164%). Full-year consolidated revenue was INR 450 crore (+15%), but EBITDA (INR 59.8 crore, +4.2%) and PAT (INR 51.2 crore, +3.7%) grew far slower. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth above 40% and a 35% CAGR over FY26-29, with the Egypt plant slated for Q3 FY27 and oleo chemicals sales starting April 2026. Raw-material inflation from the March geopolitical events created a temporary margin pressure that management expects to pass through over time.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the resin capacity is complementary, since additives are about 25% of a CPVC compound and resin about 75%. The company has supplied Supreme and Prince Pipes for 1-2 years, and the transition will take time.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no direct CPVC additive competition in India apart from one other Indian company. In lead-free, Baerlocher and Reagens are the main competitors, Goldstab is mainly lead-based, and pricing levels are understood by all players.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook versus the roughly 23% margins of FY23-FY24?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the change to a mix shift from high-margin lead-free to lower-margin CPVC, which started at a 3-7% contribution margin. Guidance is PAT margin of 11-12% and EBITDA margin of 13-15%, reiterated from the previous call.

qa_highlights.question: Project-wise capex, timelines and revenue potential for Egypt and Palghar?
qa_highlights.answer: Egypt is expected by December 2026, with INR 250-300 crore top line over three years. Palghar peak potential is INR 700-800 crore over three years, and top-line CAGR is about 35% over three years.

qa_highlights.question: What bottlenecks could delay commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not expect much delay.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the stearates plant and its effect on revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: The 6,000 tpa stearates plant has slipped to September/October 2026 from August due to a delay in one equipment item. Management said it would not materially affect FY27 revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Rivadu Lifesciences pharma and the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Business model is still being defined. Some revenue started this quarter, with collaborations with overseas companies under negotiation. No figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material inflation pass-through and contractual mechanisms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can pass on raw material price rises in normal conditions, but in the current war and shipping environment it cannot pass on sudden freight, CFS and transport costs. Lower lead-free PVC offtake was cited as the main Q1 margin driver.

qa_highlights.question: Egypt versus Palghar capex and why revenue potential differs?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR 67 crore for Egypt and INR 71 crore for Palghar. Both have about 60,000 tpa capacity, but Egypt is mainly lead stabilisers, priced at INR 110-150 per kg versus INR 250-300 for CPVC and INR 170-220 for calcium zinc in India.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects roughly a three-month working capital cycle.

Q4 EBITDA of INR26.8 crores implied a margin of about 10.26%, held back by a March spike in raw material (zinc dross) and energy costs. Capacity remains the focus, with the Dahej (Gujarat) plant due for commissioning in H1 FY27 and Naidupeta debottlenecking targeted for December 2026.

Consolidated EBITDA margin targeted at 14% to 15% in about 3 years; management says the current level is sustainable.
Internal target to double revenue every 3 years; management expects FY27 revenue well above INR1,200 crore.
Dahej revenue potential of about INR900 crore now expected around FY29 to FY30, with peak potential said to be higher.
Net cash expected above INR100 crore at FY27 end; no borrowing expected even if H1 revenue doubles.

Post both projects, installed capacity to be over 115,000 tons of zinc chemicals, per management.

JG TUR (Tire Upscaled Rubber, recycled rubber): pilot trials successful with key customers; full-scale venture being planned, with capex and timeline to be shared later.

Pricing: management says it is agnostic to zinc price, since selling price follows the prior month's LME average. Per-ton price may fall if zinc falls, but volume growth is the focus.

qa_highlights.question: What was the volume growth in Q2, and why did gross margin fall about 130 bps QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth was in the mid-teens. Management said gross margin moves with inventory lead and lag, and it focuses on EBITDA and per-ton margin instead. It sees a blended EBITDA margin of 14% to 15% within about 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative in H1 FY27, and will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is 90 to 100 days. Management said March inventory was low due to shipping delays from the West Asia crisis, and that cash should be significantly higher at 31 March. Debtor days are in line with history.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall QoQ, and was the procurement discount on dross and ash changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed a time lag: lower-cost material bought at lower LME prices arrived late, while higher-cost domestic material hit plants first. Management expects this to average out by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Dahej timeline, Phase 2 start, and the sustainability of non-rubber growth and margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 is expected around mid-to-late 2028. Specialty grades for pharma, cosmetics and specialty chemicals are expected to lift margins more than ceramics. Blended EBITDA is expected to move toward 14%.

qa_highlights.question: Is demand sustainable into Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tire demand is strong, with OEM and replacement demand both firm. It expects no demand aberration given 7% to 8% economic growth, and says Dahej should help with ceramics, which has a low base.

qa_highlights.question: Dahej utilisation, tire versus non-tire mix, and ceramics target?
qa_highlights.answer: Dahej utilisation is targeted at about 60% to 70% in FY28. Management aims for 10% to 15% of the ceramics market, against over 30% share in India overall, and notes two large tire plants about 5 km from Dahej.

Recycled rubber (JG TUR) and battery-grade zinc oxide still at pilot or qualification stage with no quantified revenue.
Zinc sulphate utilisation about 50%, with ramp-up dependent on new specialised grades.

544140|2026-03.headline: Gopal Snacks Q4 FY26 revenue rose 29% YoY to Rs 409.6 cr; FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 8-9% with Rajkot plant fully commissioned.

For FY26, revenue grew 2.7% to Rs 1,508.2 crore, EBITDA was Rs 101.3 crore (6.7%) and PAT Rs 73.7 crore (4.9%). Management said supply was restored after the fire-related disruption, with Rajkot commissioned (installed capacity 1,05,000 MT) and the Modasa plant fully integrated. Insurance receipts reached about Rs 37.4 crore in FY26, with a further claim expected to be settled around Q2 FY27.

544140|2026-06.headline: Gopal Snacks Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR 422.3 cr (+31.1% YoY) with EBITDA margin up to 7.4%; FY27 EBITDA guided at 8-9%.
