qa_highlights.question: Is the company satisfied with core-state (Gujarat) growth against the INR 100 crore/month run-rate aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not satisfied with the Gujarat run-rate and is aiming at INR 100 crore per month without cutting margins; pricing and grammage are being managed carefully.

qa_highlights.question: How much of gross margin is from pricing versus mix and grammage?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin gain came from a mix of grammage correction, price correction, and about 0.4% from lower trade discount and mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume outlook in namkeen after price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 namkeen value grew 18.3% against 8.6% volume growth. Grammage cuts are taken SKU by SKU, and two new namkeen products are planned for next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What progress has been made on dual servicing of outlets?
qa_highlights.answer: Dual servicing reached 42% at September end and 43.5% at October end in Gujarat. The target is 65-70% by FY27 end, and 25-30 Western snacks ready-stock distributors will be added in Gujarat.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company growing 20% a year after FY27 and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will be at least 20% a year. H1 network additions of about 130 distributors contributed INR 13 crore, rising to about INR 60 crore in the full year and about INR 80 crore next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins reach double digits by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 8-9% guidance stands and double digit is an aspiration that depends on raw material inflation easing.

qa_highlights.question: What are the H2 CFO drivers, and why was H1 CFO weaker?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 CFO should be better because of the INR 36.4-36.5 crore insurance receipt and inventory falling from about INR 200 crore to INR 100-120 crore. H1 was weaker because of higher inventory, including about 50% more chana storage and laminate stock.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company handle competitors burning cash in Gujarat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said competitors cannot sustain losses for long and will need to take price or grammage decisions; distributor count was held flat deliberately to protect per-distributor revenue.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation: palm oil (about 27% of basket), laminate/packaging (about 22-23%) and chana (about 19%); management ties margin recovery to easing of the 'war scenario', so the 8-9% EBITDA guidance and the double-digit aspiration depend on input costs.
Gujarat core-state run-rate remains below the INR 100 crore/month aspiration; distributor count held near 311-312 by design, and competitors' cash burn is a stated concern.
Namkeen volume growth (8.6% in H1) lags value growth (18.3%) as grammage cuts are taken SKU by SKU; watch whether two planned new namkeen products arrive next quarter.
Network expansion is behind plan: about 220 distributor additions expected in calendar 2026 versus an earlier 250 target ('not exactly on track'); Nagpur/Maharashtra additions slower than expected.

Cash flow: H1 CFO weaker than usual due to higher inventory (laminate, chana storage up about 50%); H2 relies on insurance receipt of INR 36.4 crore and inventory falling from about INR 200 crore to INR 100-120 crore.
Drought and possible chana and potato price increases in the next financial year; management said pass-through will rely on mix, lower trade marketing and price/grammage moves.
Non-core channels (exports, railways, modern trade, quick commerce) targeted at INR 30-35 crore in FY27 and INR 75-90 crore in FY28; watch execution, with exports only about INR 1 crore in October.
key_quotes: So definitely we are not satisfied with this run rate in Gujarat.
So once the war scenario eases out, definitely we'll reach to double-digit margins.
So we have almost got 1% of the benefit as far as operating leverage is concerned, and that will continue to give us the benefit go ing forward also
Not exactly on track, but we are confident that in the full calendar year we will be able to add roughly 220 distributors.
544140|2026-09.management_tone: Management was confident on volume momentum (22-23% current growth, Gathiya and wafers ahead of category) and on operating leverage, but cautious on margins, saying double-digit EBITDA depends on easing raw material inflation. It was candid on shortfalls: Gujarat run-rate below aspiration, distributor additions not exactly on track, and H1 cash flow weaker.

544141|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 36.8% YoY to INR14.3 crores, the company's highest first half, on revenue up 29.6% to INR34.2 crores.
544141|2026-09.overview: Pune E-Stock Broking reported H1 FY27 (six months to 30 September 2026) consolidated revenue from operations of INR34.2 crores, up 29.6% YoY and 24% HoH, with PBT of INR19.1 crores (+38.8%) and PAT of INR14.3 crores (+36.8%). Net profit margin was 41.7%, up 220 bps YoY but down from about 50% in H2 FY26. Management said the quarter was shaped by a weak secondary market (F&O volume cuts, higher STT in April 2026) and used the call to position MTF, merchant banking, insurance distribution and AIF as fee-based growth drivers, most of which are only months old and contribute little revenue yet. Equity rose to INR225 crores from INR180.6 crores in March, helped by warrant conversions and a new warrant issue.

financial_highlights.change: +29.6% YoY vs INR26 crores; +24% HoH vs INR27.5 crores
+36.8% YoY vs INR10.4 crores; +51% HoH vs INR9.5 crores
+220 bps YoY; below ~50% in previous half
vs INR9.3 crores a year ago

segments.name: Broking and MTF
segments.commentary: Foundation business; MTF book crossed INR100 crores, fully collateralised by client shares and cash, and is being grown 'carefully'. Short-term borrowings (INR65 crores) mainly fund the MTF book.

segments.name: Research
segments.commentary: Team of MBAs, CAs, economists and CFAs; curated equity basket lets clients invest in a research team's ideas with a single order. No revenue split disclosed.

segments.name: Mutual fund distribution
segments.commentary: Works with 36 AMCs and more than 500 schemes; over 1,600 investors, AUM above INR240 crores, SIP book over INR1.5 crores. Capital-light, fee-based, recurring.

segments.name: PESB Alpha Fund (Cat III AIF) / PESB Asset Management LLP
segments.commentary: Launched November 2025, about INR55 crores under management; PESB invested INR15 crores. Management claims about 25% post-fee, post-tax return in year one; income accrues to the wholly owned fund-manager LLP. Clients typically commit for at least three years.

segments.name: Merchant banking
segments.commentary: Licence obtained about a year ago (2025); first fees earned in 2026. First mandate Apar Advertisers (SME) approved and expected to list within a couple of months; several other SME and mainboard mandates in pipeline. No fee figures disclosed.

segments.name: Insurance distribution (Pune Finvest / QURA Insure)
segments.commentary: Pune Finvest (79.8% subsidiary) received IRDAI corporate agency approval in July 2026; advisory operations began September 2026 under the QURA Insure brand, initially targeting the existing 65,000 clients. No revenue disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Sustain double-digit profit growth.
Improve return ratios as fee-based businesses (wealth, merchant banking, insurance, AIF) scale; management expects ROE and ROCE to move up steadily but gave no targets.
Grow to more than 1 lakh customers by 2027 (client base currently above 65,000, of whom above 17,000 are traded clients).

Plans: open flagship branches in high-visibility locations, grow the MTF book carefully, scale an open API-based algo trading platform for retail, and build GIFT City merchant banking, secured lending and insurance businesses.

Warrant proceeds (16 lakh warrants at INR234 each, 25% received) to be deployed mainly in MTF and merchant banking; branches and technology funded as needed; promoters participated in the warrant round so dilution is limited.
capex_capacity: Capital allocation is driven by MTF book growth and merchant banking; branch and technology spend is 'on need basis' per management.
Warrant issue: 16 lakh convertible warrants at INR234 each, 25% of subscription received; 18 lakh equity shares issued on warrant conversion during H1.
Dividend: final dividend of INR1 per share for FY26 paid.
PESB committed INR15 crores to PESB Alpha Fund; AIF size about INR55 crores.
Planned flagship branches in high-visibility locations; no count or timelines disclosed.
demand_pricing: Industry context: SEBI F&O measures more than halved option volumes in 2026 and cut individual F&O traders by about a fifth; higher STT on derivatives from April 2026 added pressure.
Industry margin trading book rose from above INR1.4 lakh crores (June 2026) to about INR1.6 lakh crores (September 2026), per management.
Mainboard IPOs raised a record INR94,200 crores across 78 issues in H1 CY26 (35% higher YoY per management); total IPO fundraise including SME exceeded INR1 lakh crores.
Management expects margins on insurance to fall under IRDAI commission-cap proposals but volumes to rise; sees MTF rule tightening as a long-term positive that reduces speculation in weak scrips.

Management said the call's market backdrop was weak: Nifty about 1% up for H1, down about 6% in September; FIIs net sellers of over INR2.3 lakh crores in April-September 2026; domestic institutions bought about INR3.9 lakh crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the view on merchant banking and the IPO pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Ronak Jhaveri said the first mandate, Apar Advertisers (SME), is approved and listing is planned within a couple of months; several SME and mainboard mandates are in the pipeline and will be disclosed on BSE as they are signed.

qa_highlights.question: Will share capital increase, where will growth be funded, and how are Pune Finvest, PESB Alpha Fund, PESB Asset Management LLP and IFSC structured?
qa_highlights.answer: Arpit Shah said growth will be funded by internal accruals and the recent warrant issue, mainly into MTF and merchant banking. Pune Finvest is a 79.8% subsidiary holding the NBFC and insurance business; the AIF trust has appointed PESB Asset Management LLP, a wholly owned subsidiary, as fund manager. He did not detail the IFSC entity.

qa_highlights.question: Why a corporate agency licence rather than an insurance broking licence?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate agency approval came faster from IRDAI, with a consultant's guidance, and the holding-company structure delayed the insurance-company route; management said many NBFCs operate as corporate agents with no major structural difference.

qa_highlights.question: How will warrant proceeds be deployed and how is dilution weighed?
qa_highlights.answer: Proceeds go mainly to MTF and merchant banking, with branches and technology funded as needed. Promoters participated equally in the warrant round, so promoter stake is not expected to dilute materially.

qa_highlights.question: What are the return-ratio drivers and the biggest risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fee-based businesses are capital-light and returns should improve as they contribute; new licences are only a year old, so contribution is still small. The main risk cited is regulatory change, which is industry-wide, and management said it is confident of coping given over 15 years in the business.

qa_highlights.question: How will IRDAI commission caps and SEBI's MTF rule review affect the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance margins will fall, but volumes should rise; management expects no major issue from MTF rules and said it is prepared if final rules are stricter, with benefits over the long term rather than the short term.

qa_highlights.question: How will cross-selling of mutual fund and advisory products be done, and is it RM-led or digital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management uses RM-led face-to-face coverage for suitability and risk-profiling, backed by a digital team to reach clients in locations without physical presence.

qa_highlights.question: Is AIF fee income lumpy and how will the AIF scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AIF fees are consistent because investors commit for at least three years; year one delivered about 25% post-fee, post-tax return, and marketing through RMs and word of mouth is planned.

qa_highlights.question: How is MTF concentration risk managed in a sharp fall, and what is the collateral shortfall record?
qa_highlights.answer: Software tracks positions, MTM and collateral shortfalls, with staff contacting clients; if a shortfall persists for more than five days, the stock is liquidated. No historical shortfall figures were given.

risks_watch: Regulatory risk: SEBI review of MTF rules and IRDAI proposals to cap insurance commissions could compress margins; management called the impact short-term.
Net profit margin fell from about 50% in H2 FY26 to 41.7% in H1 FY27; watch whether this is a trend as new businesses scale.
Weak F&O activity and higher STT on derivatives could keep broking volumes under pressure.
MTF book growth of INR100 crores plus INR65 crores of short-term borrowings raise funding and collateral-shortfall risk in a sharp market fall; no shortfall history was disclosed.
Warrant conversion (16 lakh warrants at INR234) and merchant banking/IPO execution depend on primary-market momentum; the Apar Advertisers listing is a near-term test.
Management gave no quantified revenue targets for new businesses, and merchant banking and insurance revenue was not separately disclosed.
key_quotes: Our consolidated revenue from operations grew around 30% to INR34.2 crores. EBITDA grew by 31% to INR22.3 crores, and net profit grew almost 37% to INR14.3 crores, our highest for any first half of the year.
We will not pursue growth at any cost. We will build with discipline, invest where we see clear opportunity, and remain mindful of the trust our clients and shareholders place in us.
So yes, we may find a short-term hitch in our profitability or margins, but in the longer term, it is actually working in our favour.
Since these licenses have come just a year back, there is no significant contribution to revenue from these segments as yet.

Cautious on the market backdrop, regulation and risk, which management called a short-term hitch, and it gave no quantified targets for new businesses.

544144|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue up ~28% YoY and FY26 EBITDA up 16% to INR203.4 crore, but FY26 reported PAT still a loss of INR12.5 crore.
544144|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew about 28% YoY and total income reached INR1,758.8 crore (up 27.8%), with EBITDA of INR57.5 crore (margin about 3.3%) and a loss of INR5 crore versus INR13.7 crore loss a year earlier. FY26 total income was INR6,401.1 crore (up 15.1%) and reported EBITDA INR203.4 crore (margin 3.2%), while PAT was a loss of INR12.5 crore against INR10.5 crore loss in FY25. Management said the FY26 revenue and EBITDA were hit by acquisition costs, a cess provision and the new labour code impact, and it apologised for an error in the April 17, 2026 business update that misstated Q4 growth figures. Management guides FY27 to high double-digit top-line growth and consolidated EBITDA margin of about 4.8-5%, with sustainable profitability from Q2 FY27.

up 28% YoY, after adjusting Honda/Piaggio divestment, acquisition impact and one-off provision

financial_highlights.change: adjusted PBT loss about INR5 crore; adjusted PBT before exceptional items positive INR8.8 crore

segments.commentary: Q4 service volumes 52,443 units (up 13%), income INR97 crore (up 75%). FY26 volumes 2,02,647 (up 10%), income INR351 crore (up 28%).

segments.commentary: Q4 new vehicles 3,079 units (up 138%), income INR50 crore (up 113%); service volumes 11,261 (up 81%), income about INR3 crore. FY26 new vehicles 8,154 units (up 89%), income INR137 crore (up 72%); service volumes 39,659 (up 79%), income about INR9 crore (up 18%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 target of high double-digit top-line growth and consolidated EBITDA margin moving to about 4.8-5%; PAT approaching FY24 levels.
Sustainable profitability expected from Q2 FY27; Q1 FY27 still expected to be loss-making due to Maruti and JLR supply constraints.
PV service volumes guided to grow at least 10-12% in FY27, with ASP growth of about 12-13%; CV service volumes guided up 7-8% with ASP up 8-10%.
Standalone sales margin guided at about 3-4% in FY27; spare parts margin guided back to 5.5-6% with revenue growth of 6-8% (ex-BKT).
JLR volume guidance of 550-600 vehicles in FY27 after about 380 Audi/JLR volume shortfall in FY26 (guided about 450); Audi expected to break even this year.
Non-Keralam revenue share to exceed 50% in FY27 from about 47% in FY26; no high-value acquisitions planned in FY27, focus on consolidating FY26 acquisitions.
Inventory to be held at or below 30 days for passenger cars; debt increase attributed to acquisitions, with ~INR520 crore of INR600+ crore debt inventory-linked.
capex_capacity: Three acquisitions in FY26: BharatBenz dealership in Punjab, Maruti Suzuki dealership in Telangana, and Audi dealership operations in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh; Honda and Piaggio businesses divested (volumes counted to August 2025).
JLR Nagpur operations commenced April 1, 2026; new Maruti touchpoints and multiple Ather touchpoints opened in Q4.
Bank loan facilities increased from INR468 crore to INR643 crore; CRISIL A/Stable rating extended to March 2027.
Management said capex spends will be more monitored and no additional debt is planned beyond what is needed to run the current business.
Acquired Audi and Telangana assets totalled about INR85-90 crore of equipment and showroom assets, with acquisition cost approximately equal.
demand_pricing: Management said demand improved in H2 FY26 after GST reforms in September 2025, with stronger footfall, conversion and entry-level recovery; discounting moderated.
Shortages of entry-level vehicles in Jan-Mar 2026 eased in April-May; Baleno and Fronx have waiting periods.
Post OEM price increases, management reported no noticeable change in demand so far; some pre-ponement of bookings was seen.
Luxury segment: Q4 delayed by UK FTA price-cut expectation; price cuts applied to Range Rover SP and Autobiography, with bookings rising from April.
Service volume: running repair fell about 17-18% as the company deprioritised low-value jobs; collision repair volumes flat; free service volumes recovered in last 6 months.
Maruti share of service volumes about 65-70%; Maruti service volume decline narrowed from -7% (to Q3) to -2% in Q4.
Overall Maruti ASP up about 13% YoY; PV new vehicle weighted ASP up to about 6.5% from about 5.5% three years earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why did service volumes fall and what service volume and ASP growth is guided for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 service volumes fell about 6% and ASP rose about 14%, with revenue up over 8%. For FY27 it guided 10-12% PV service volume growth and matching ASP growth; CV service volume growth of 7-8%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the service EBITDA margin gap versus peers close?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated margin will not reach 18% because of CV and Ather mix, but the Passenger Car business should reach 18-19% service margin.

qa_highlights.question: How will standalone margins move from about 3% to 5% consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin drag to acquisitions and Telangana expansion; growth is to come from PV service volumes and ASP, plus JLR and Audi ramp-up, with consolidated EBITDA guided to 4.8-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add acquisitions and how will debt be reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: No high-value acquisitions planned in FY27. About INR520 crore of the INR600+ crore debt is inventory-linked; term loans will be repaid on schedule, and debt will fall if inventory release generates free cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is inventory under control and what is the demand reaction to OEM price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days fell from 49 to 36 (FY25 to FY26); management aims to keep it below 30 days. Post price hikes, demand was flat and supply has normalised in April-May.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company turn sustainably profitable and what happened in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable profitability from Q2 FY27. Q1 remains affected by Maruti and JLR supply constraints; service volumes expected to grow Q1 over Q1.

risks_watch: Reported FY26 PAT loss of INR12.5 crore; Telangana loss of about INR26-27 crore and cess provision weigh on profitability, with Ind AS depreciation on acquisitions.
Debt rose after acquisitions; management says inventory debt is about INR520 crore of INR600+ crore total, with inventory days to stay below 30.

CEO Raj Narayan has resigned to pursue an opportunity outside the industry; successor not named on this call.

Service volumes in running repair down 17-18%; management needs to show Q1 FY27 volume growth.
Fuel price and geopolitical uncertainty (referred to as a war situation) flagged as demand risks.
key_quotes: Before moving to the business performance, I would like to sincerely apologize for the error in the business update published on April 17 , 2026, for the quarter and the year ended March 31 , 2026, and take this opportunity to clarify the same.

In terms of profitability from Q2 of FY '27, we should be having sustainable profitability.

544144|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~44% YoY to INR1,890 crore and reported EBITDA rose ~87% to INR71.5 crore (3.8% margin), with reported PBT turning positive at INR1.9 crore.

segments.name: Luxury (JLR and Audi)
segments.commentary: Reported revenue +42%; new vehicles +39%; service volumes +87%. Organic luxury revenue +21%, service volumes +9%. JLR EBITDA INR10.5 crore vs INR8.2 crore a year ago; Audi EBITDA ~nil, with margin dip attributed to Audi.

544149|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue fell about 12% YoY to INR364.94 crore on selective bidding, while PAT rose 11% to INR18.85 crore; FY26 consolidated order book is about INR2,500 crore+.
544149|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR364.94 crore, down nearly 12% YoY but up 19% QoQ, as management deliberately skipped low-margin bids. EBITDA excluding other income fell 11% YoY to INR23.78 crore, yet margin edged up 3 bps to 6.51% and PAT grew over 11% YoY to INR18.85 crore. For FY26, revenue rose 5.32% to INR1,277.28 crore, EBITDA rose 7.5% to INR83.53 crore (6.54% margin), and PAT was INR64.35 crore (up nearly 3%). Management guided to upwards of 20% consolidated revenue growth in FY27 and announced the 100% acquisition of Citelum India, its first acquisition, for smart lighting and urban infrastructure.

qa_highlights.question: How does Krystal differentiate from global players such as CBRE, JLL, SIS and Sodexo in large corporate mandates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the services are similar but Krystal is the direct service provider, while global players are property managers that outsource services. Many new customers were won against these players.

qa_highlights.answer: Rebalancing the government/corporate mix from about 70:30 by adding corporates, with government growth in waste management, O&M and city infrastructure. Management aims to be a diversified player with all verticals revenue-making and profitable within 5 years.

544149|2026-09.headline: Krystal Q2 FY27 revenue rose 46.25% YoY to Rs 414.47 crore, but EBITDA margin eased to 6.0% from 6.32% on higher employee cost.
544149|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 reached Rs 414.47 crore, up 46.25% YoY and 14.9% QoQ, with H1 revenue at Rs 775.18 crore (up 27.82%). EBITDA excluding other income grew 38.82% to Rs 24.86 crore, but margin moderated to 6.0% from 6.32% as employee cost rose to 75.9% of revenue from 72.3%. PAT grew 41.66% to Rs 18.67 crore in Q2, helped by a lower effective tax rate of 12.5%. Management highlighted the Citelum India acquisition, new segments (solid waste management, solar EPC, technical FM) and a Rs 2,980-3,000 crore order book spanning about 3 to 3.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will Citelum focus on government or private projects, and does it need heavy assets to reach Rs 300-350 crore?

demand_pricing: Footfall-to-conversion ratio of 81%; average ticket size about INR157,000.
Old gold exchange contributed about 25% of Q1 FY27 sales.

Inventory mix: about 80% 22-karat, 15% 18-karat, balance lower karat. Management said customers still prefer 22-karat, with lightweight 22-karat designs as the affordability response.
Management said FY26 had no meaningful industry volume growth; competition noted from national brands with multiple stores in Indore.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company hedge gold and silver as it expands?
qa_highlights.answer: Uses real-time replenishment (3-4 bookings a day with vendors), exchange-based old gold purchases, gold metal loans for extra inventory, and MCX hedging.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth and what is the gold-price effect on sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27 volume grew about 1-2% YoY; the balance of revenue growth came from higher gold prices and making charges. Inventory gains were about 10-15% of growth. Management said volume was not growing meaningfully in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why does operating cash flow stay negative and how will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 95-98% of assets are inventory, so operating cash flow is linked to inventory build. It expects working capital efficiency to improve as the business scales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory carrying value versus market price, and how is it accounted for?
qa_highlights.answer: Weighted-average cost is about INR1,20,000 vs market of INR1,51,000-1,52,000 per gram (a gap of about 20%); the gap will narrow as fresh purchases at INR1,45,000-1,50,000 enter inventory. Management said profitability depends on making charges.

qa_highlights.question: What volume and revenue growth should be expected for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 10% volume growth for both FY27 and FY28; revenue growth will depend on gold prices.

Gold import duty hike to 15% (May 2026) and gold price volatility affect demand and expansion pace.
Inventory is carried at about 20% below market; gross margin depends on making charges and product mix.
Store rollout risk: 51-store FY30 target needs about 6-8 openings a year, while FY27 has only 5-6 planned; new stores ramp slowly.

544162|2026-03.headline: Bharti Hexacom FY26 revenue grew 9.4% and EBITDAaL 17.9%, with Q4 revenue at Rs 2,414 Crores (+2.3% QoQ) and EBITDAaL margin of 47.9%.
544162|2026-03.overview: Bharti Hexacom reported strong FY26 operating leverage, with EBITDAaL margin up 3.4 points to 47.6% and a record 395,000 net homes adds. Q4 revenue grew 2.3% sequentially to Rs 2,414 Crores, while ARPU of Rs 252 was dented by two fewer days and was about Rs 257-258 on an EDB basis. Management flagged handset price rises, lower international roaming and 5G pack consumption as ARPU headwinds, and a Rs 4,000 Crore-range regulatory provision was booked on a changed interpretation of an existing issue. The call was largely a joint Airtel-Hexacom webinar; Hexacom questions focused on lagging mobile growth versus Airtel, FWA versus fiber strategy, and payout.

segments.name: Homes and office
segments.commentary: Record net adds of 148,000 in Q4 and 395,000 for FY26; FY26 homes and office revenue grew 51%. Q4 homes revenue rose about 21% sequentially, helped by FWA expansion to new pin codes, FTTH deepening and IPTV rollout.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given; management said it does not provide guidance and that Hexacom remains committed to progressively increasing dividend payout.
ARPU headwinds expected to persist from lower international roaming, handset price rises and 5G consumption packs; management said there are no red flags on ARPU.
Management expects Hexacom to stay competitive and look for ways to grow faster, including new convergence offers; smartphone upgrades could see some stress.
Hexacom will not give up on homes acquisition; in difficult terrain FWA is used to reach homes where fiber is costly, with fiber-first where available.
capex_capacity: Q4 capex was Rs 586 Crores, described as acceleration as planned.
FY26 capex directed to 5G densification, network modernization and homes and IPTV growth.

demand_pricing: Smartphone upgrades and feature-phone-to-smartphone shift face pressure from rising handset prices; management said FWA connection costs have risen versus fiber in the last three to four months.

Homes ARPU on new adds is slightly lower than the traditional base, but acquisition ARPU has not declined materially, per the parent's commentary.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Hexacom mobile revenue growth (8.3%) lagged Airtel (close to 12%), and should it accelerate?
qa_highlights.answer: Soumen Ray said Hexacom is underpenetrated in its two circles and the ARPU gap has closed; postpaid and international roaming differences and smartphone upgrade stress may cause some lag, and convergence offers are being launched.

qa_highlights.question: Should Hexacom have a sharper payout ratio given limited growth engines and funded capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said dividend moved from Rs 3-4 to Rs 10-18 per share and it remains committed to a progressively rising payout, while growth engines available to the parent are not open to Hexacom.

qa_highlights.question: Could homes growth slow due to chipset and memory cost issues affecting FWA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FWA remains useful for reaching homes in difficult terrain such as the North East, and it will not give up on home acquisition, pivoting to fiber where available.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the ARPU shortfall beyond international roaming?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 5G pack adoption that breaks the price ladder, handset price increases pressuring 2G to 4G upgrades, and lower roaming; the quarter-average ARPU is not a red flag per management.

qa_highlights.question: Should homes subscriber additions continue at the current pace?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined forward-looking guidance but said the objective is to keep growing homes and there is no fundamental reason to ease efforts, though competition exists.

qa_highlights.question: What does the regulatory charge in Q4 relate to and is it new demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not new; an existing matter was re-interpreted with auditors and the audit committee and a provision was taken under prudent accounting, with no specifics disclosed.

risks_watch: ARPU trajectory with handset price increases, lower international roaming and 5G unlimited packs; Q4 ARPU was Rs 252 reported.
Homes momentum if chipset and memory costs keep FWA more expensive and push the company toward slower fiber rollout in difficult terrain.
Regulatory provision booked in Q4 on a changed interpretation of an existing matter; amount not disclosed in the call.

We have increased the dividend payout significantly and we have been committed that we will be looking at a progressively increasing dividend payout and we continue to remain on that.

544162|2026-06.headline: Bharti Hexacom Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4% QoQ to Rs2,510 Cr with EBITDAaL margin of 48.2%, while homes net adds slowed to 75k.
544162|2026-06.overview: Bharti Hexacom reported Q1 FY27 revenue of about Rs2,510 Crores, up 4% sequentially, with EBITDAaL of about Rs1,210 Crores at a 48.2% margin. Mobile added about 210,000 net customers on a 29 million base, with ARPU at Rs259 helped by one extra day. Homes, office and other business net adds were 75k and revenue grew about 8% sequentially; management attributed the slower homes intake to a deliberate tightening of acquisition quality. Operating free cash flow (EBITDAaL minus capex) was about Rs830 Crores and net debt excluding leases was about Rs960 Crores (0.2x EBITDAaL). The call was a joint Bharti Airtel and Bharti Hexacom webinar, and most Q&A addressed group-level topics.

Homes, office and other net adds

segments.name: Homes, office and other
segments.commentary: Net adds of 75k, with revenue up about 8% QoQ. IPTV rollout is adding depreciation; EBIT margin for the CPE-based homes business is negative or immaterial until scale is reached.

Capex priorities are 5G densification, network modernisation, fiberisation and homes/IPTV; management said it will spend adequately if needed for competitive growth.
Management said it would provide the count of the roughly 15-17 of the 400 relevant cities that fall in the Northeast and Rajasthan circles, a figure it did not confirm on the call.

Hexacom operates in the Northeast and Rajasthan circles, where it uses a mix of wireless and wired lines because of terrain.

Homes acquisition was tightened after the FWA push brought weaker quality and higher churn; management said fundamentals of the homes market have not changed.
Rajasthan was described as extremely competitive, while the Northeast position is comfortable; intensity on customer acquisition is said to be no different from other circles.

qa_highlights.question: Has the homes outlook changed given acquisition-policy changes and rising chipset costs?

qa_highlights.answer: Karthikeyan Velu cited seasonal solar-powered tower benefits and some one-offs. Soumen Ray added that diesel stock in DG sets means the full diesel price impact has not yet flowed through, and that the underlying sequential trend is as planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation rise 4.9% QoQ, and when will homes turn profitable at EBIT?

qa_highlights.question: How many of the 400 relevant cities are in Hexacom's circles, and how big is the homes opportunity?

544162|2026-09.headline: Bharti Hexacom FY26 revenue grew 9.4% and EBITDAaL 17.9% to a 47.6% margin, but Q4 ARPU of Rs.252 was dragged by roaming and 5G pack dynamics.
544162|2026-09.overview: This is a combined Bharti Airtel and Bharti Hexacom Q4 FY26 (quarter ended March 31, 2026) earnings webinar, held May 14, 2026, with the Hexacom segment covered in the second half. Hexacom delivered record FY26 net adds of 395,000 and a 3.4-point margin expansion to 47.6%, while Q4 revenue rose 2.3% sequentially to Rs.2,414 crore. Q4 ARPU was Rs.252 (about Rs.257-258 on an EDB basis) and management acknowledged headwinds from lower international roaming, handset price increases and 5G pack adoption. The Board recommended a Rs.18 dividend per share versus Rs.10 last year. A parent-level Africa share swap (additional 16.3% stake in Airtel Africa) was also announced, though it does not directly affect Hexacom.

Management said FY26 revenue growth was 8.3% against about 12% at Airtel, and the ARPU gap has narrowed.

segments.name: Homes and offices (Hexacom)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 51% with record net adds of 395,000 for the year; Q4 added a record 148,000 with revenue up about 21% QoQ. Growth is driven by FWA expansion to new pin codes, FTTH deepening and the IPTV rollout.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Hexacom is under-penetrated and the ARPU gap has narrowed; postpaid and international roaming mix will differ, and smartphone upgrades may stress growth. It is not lagging the market.

qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged that parent growth engines are not available to Hexacom, which limits new growth; dividend payout has moved from Rs.3-4 to Rs.10-18 per share and will keep rising progressively.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cost of connecting homes is higher in difficult terrain and FWA lets it reach more homes; it will not give up acquisition and will prefer fiber where available.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5G pack adoption (eat-as-much-as-you-can packs) is a headwind alongside lower roaming and handset prices; Q4 ARPU is an average, with no red flag on the exit rate.

544167|2026-03.headline: JNK India Q4 FY26 revenue rose 69.2% YoY to Rs 344.6 crore, with EBITDA margin at 15.2%; FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-30%.

Management attributed margin expansion mainly to project mix (legacy orders completed in Q1-Q2) and guided 14-15% EBITDA margin as sustainable. rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Non-heating adjacencies (process plants, metals and minerals, offshore, renewables) are targeted at about 40% of revenue in 3-5 years, but management said diversification will not ramp within 1-2 years and the initial hit rate is only 10-12%.

rows.label: Refinery and fertiliser order finalisation and Dangote Phase 2
rows.why: Management expects refinery and fertiliser orders to be finalised in Q2-Q3 FY27, and Dangote Phase 2 is described as a likely repeat order within an export pipeline of about INR 3,000 crore.

rows.label: Unbilled revenue and bank guarantee limit needs
rows.why: Unbilled revenue is about INR 200-221 crore at end Q1 after the shift to input-method recognition, and new contracts may need a non-fund-based limit enhancement, though management expects no significant debt raising in the next 4-6 quarters.

rows.label: JNK Chemdist EBITDA-positive by year-end FY27
rows.why: Chemdist lost about INR 3.6 crore in Q1 on 8.8% of group revenue, with current green hydrogen orders of about INR 50 crore, and management expects it to turn profitable over the full year but gave no quarterly guidance.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order pipeline (above INR 6,000 crore), the 20-25% growth guide and the 12-14% margin guide, but was defensive on the export order cancellation, the JNK Global governance dispute and the EBITDA guidance reconciliation, and several answers were deferred to filings.

544172|2026-03.headline: Indegene Q4 FY26 revenue crossed ₹1,000 crore for the first time (+32.8% YoY); FY26 revenue ₹35,105 million, up 23.6% in INR.
544172|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the first quarter above ₹1,000 crore revenue, up 6.5% QoQ and 32.8% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA rose 23.2% YoY to ₹1,889 million, but after a ₹241 million forward-contract hedge charge the reported EBITDA was ₹1,648 million. Reported Q4 PAT was ₹797 million after a ₹203 million one-time provision for a 2020 US TCPA class action; management says adjusted PAT grew 12.7% YoY for FY26. Management declined to give formal revenue guidance but said the pipeline is larger and better qualified than at any prior year end.

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 PAT excluding one-offs and retroactive cash flow hedge accounting

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹4,419 million in FY25 (162% of PAT)

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and investments at year end
financial_highlights.change: ₹1,258 million lower YoY after ₹7,253 million acquisition outflows

segments.name: Enterprise Commercial (ex-BioPharm)
segments.commentary: Grew about 17% YoY; BioPharm (acquired October 2025) grew 15% QoQ in Q4. Q4 included a Tectonic engagement with the largest customer for Germany.

segments.name: Enterprise Medical Services (EMS)
segments.commentary: Grew about 16% YoY. Q4 wins included a MedInfo engagement with a biotech, and a GenAI pharmacovigilance win with a medical devices client using NAEM.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: North America 71.6%, Europe 25.5%, Rest of World 2.9%; North America rose about 2 points on BioPharm, which is entirely US-focused.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue guidance; management said the pipeline entering FY27 is stronger, more balanced and better qualified than any prior year end.
Management expects profitability and EBITDA margins to improve in FY27, with the second half of FY27 reverting to earlier higher margin levels as the ~150 bps investment drag is absorbed.
Margins are expected to stay within the historical range; any leverage above that will be reinvested.
PAT in FY27 expected to rise significantly, helped by higher interest income on cash, amortization stabilizing in the latter half of FY27, and fading one-offs.
The $10 million+ ACV omnichannel deal signed in Q3 has started but will be fully recognized in FY27 because of outcome-based pricing.
Tectonic is expected to become a material growth driver for enterprise commercial in FY27; the largest customer is targeted to cross $50 million.
BioPharm G&A synergies expected to show from the next quarter, with data subscription and go-to-market synergies phasing in through FY27.
Final dividend proposed at ₹2.25 per share, up from ₹2 (12.5%), subject to AGM approval.
capex_capacity: R&D spend rose to slightly above 2% of revenue in FY26, with GTM and domain-expertise investments continuing.
Integration of BioPharm completed ahead of schedule in late February 2026; transition services from the seller were originally planned to end in March.
Global innovation center pilot for a large US biotech and an Agency-of-record pilot (3 months to 3 days) are in early stages, with conversion to engagements targeted within FY27.
Five next-generation operating models are being run in market: One-Click submissions, human-less medical legal review, agentic AOR, AI-embedded engagement, and intelligent R&D operations.
Headcount is above 5,000 colleagues globally.
demand_pricing: Active customers rose from 73 to 91; customers above $1 million grew from 41 to 53 (about 30%), and several have scaled to $5 million ACV.
Top 20 customer revenue rose from ₹22,082 million to ₹25,200 million in FY26. A third account crossed $25 million, and the largest customer is in an early phase of a Germany Tectonic engagement.

Q4 bookings: one $3 million+ ACV clinical deal with a new customer; seven $1 million+ ACV deals, four from top 20 customers; one expansion of an omnichannel project; two new engagements (a biotech MedInfo deal and an upcoming pharma launch).
Revenue per employee about $75,000 in FY26, up from $66,000-67,000 a year earlier and $56,000 three years back.
Management says the pricing model is predominantly managed-outcome and output-based rather than timesheet-based, and it sees Indegene as taking share from agencies and CROs.
Constant-currency organic growth was 12% YoY and a little over 3% QoQ, per the CFO in response to a question.
DSO fell to 63 days from 72 days; guidance is mid-60s to 70 days on a steady basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the number of $10 million+ clients stayed at 10, and is there a product life cycle issue for large clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cohort is stable, with one client at $9.9 million placed in the lower bucket. Some large clients are taking longer to change operating models, but management expects the cohort to grow.

qa_highlights.question: How defensible is the domain-knowledge moat against LLM commoditization?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the moat is domain expertise plus proprietary data, with multiple frontier models and specialist AI partners orchestrated together. It said LLMs are not reliable enough for regulated operating-grade work over the next 3 to 5 years, so human-in-the-loop remains necessary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk that AI investment keeps margins from recovering?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are expected to recover within a few quarters because investments are absorbed, and that it will reinvest any excess above the current margin range rather than expand margins beyond it.

qa_highlights.question: What is Cortex, and is the AI in-house or a wrapper?
qa_highlights.answer: Cortex is a knowledge engineering platform for building agentic workflows for life sciences with enterprise security. It sits on frontier models plus specialist AI such as computer vision and large action models, with the domain layer decoupled from the technology layer.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 growth drivers and what would be different?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described FY27 as a year of scaling FY26 initiatives, pointing to Tectonic with two customers in long-term engagements, the $10 million deal converting in FY27, and consistent $1 million+ wins.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a strategy for small and mid-size pharma and generics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is expanding rapidly in mid-size and small companies, with launch models for small biotechs. Generics contribute some revenue, but innovator pharma is prioritised because of the $100 million client opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: What was the constant-currency organic growth in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said 12% YoY organic in constant currency and a little over 3% QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook after integrating BioPharm?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said integration finished ahead of schedule in late February, with G&A synergies expected from the next quarter and data, operations and GTM synergies phasing in through FY27.

risks_watch: The ₹241 million hedge charge and the forward-contract cash flow hedge accounting change make Q4 EBITDA comparisons harder; adjusted and reported figures differ.
The US TCPA class action settlement is pending court approval (₹203 million provision); management says no further fax-related exposures exist.
Whether the largest customer converts the Germany Tectonic engagement into broader multi-region revenue in FY27, and the $50 million+ milestone.
Whether the $10 million outcome-based deal recognises revenue on schedule in FY27.
Margin recovery in 2H FY27 depends on absorbing the ~150 bps investment; reinvestment is expected.
Interest income and amortization effects from acquisitions on PAT; the CFO expects both to improve in FY27.
The low-visibility AI pilots (Agency-of-record, global innovation centre) have not yet converted to engagements.
544172|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and forward-leaning, especially on AI differentiation and FY27 pipeline, though management explicitly declined formal revenue guidance and framed margin expansion conservatively. The CFO was precise on adjustments and one-offs, but pushed a PAT recovery story heavily on adjusted figures.
key_quotes: Q4 FY26 was the first ever quarter in our history where our revenues exceeded ₹1,000 crores.
Indegene is not an IT services company that happens to serve life sciences.
GenAI equalizes access to technology. It does not equal access to knowledge.
I want to be direct, we're not providing formal revenue guidance.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects EBITDA margins to improve in FY27 with H2 FY27 reverting to earlier higher levels as the ~150 bps investment drag is absorbed, though any leverage above the historical range will be reinvested.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Constant-currency organic growth was 12% YoY and a little over 3% QoQ; active customers rose from 73 to 91, customers above $1M grew from 41 to 53 (about 30%), and the $10M+ ACV omnichannel deal converts fully in FY27.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined formal revenue guidance but says the FY27 pipeline is stronger and better qualified than any prior year end, and PAT is expected to rise significantly.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management is confident on the pipeline, Tectonic and the $10M+ deal, and FY26 revenue grew 23.6% in INR (18.2% in USD), though the Q4 hedge charge (₹241m) and the pending TCPA settlement (₹203m) add reporting noise.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Five next-generation operating models are running in market and the Cortex agentic platform is in use, but the AI pilots (global innovation centre, agency-of-record) are early stage and conversion to engagements is targeted only within FY27.

rows.label: Tectonic becomes material growth driver; largest customer targeted to cross $50M
rows.why: Largest customer is in early phase of Germany Tectonic engagement and a third account crossed $25M; management expects Tectonic to be material for enterprise commercial in FY27.

rows.label: $10M+ ACV omnichannel deal fully recognised in FY27
rows.why: Deal was signed in Q3 FY26 and has started; outcome-based pricing means full recognition in FY27, with Q4 bookings including seven $1M+ ACV deals and one $3M+ clinical deal.

rows.label: BioPharm G&A and data/GTM synergies phasing in
rows.why: Integration finished ahead of schedule in late February 2026, with G&A synergies expected from the next quarter and data and GTM synergies phasing in through FY27 after the ₹7,253m acquisition outflow.

tone.note: Management was confident on AI differentiation, the FY27 pipeline and Tectonic, and cautious on margins, which it framed conservatively with reinvestment; analysts pushed on the $10M+ client cohort staying flat at 10, AI commoditisation risk, and whether AI spend would keep margins from recovering.

544172|2026-06.headline: Indegene Q1 FY27 revenue rose 39.7% YoY to INR10,631m, with EBITDA margin at 16.9% and guidance for a return to 19–20% by Q4 FY27.
544172|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR10,631 million, up 39.7% YoY in rupee terms and 6% QoQ, with USD revenue of $112.5 million up 26.5% YoY and 2.5% QoQ. Reported EBITDA was INR1,795 million at a 16.9% margin, up 50 bps QoQ against a prior quarter hit by roughly 240 bps of undesignated forex mark-to-market. PAT rose 45.9% QoQ to INR1,162 million (10.9% of revenue). Management reiterated that margins will normalise to the 19–20% band by Q3/Q4 FY27, driven by a large outcome-based omnichannel deal recognising revenue from Q3 FY27 and workforce productivity gains.

financial_highlights.change: +50 bps QoQ reported; prior quarter hit ~240 bps from MTM on undesignated hedges

segments.name: Enterprise Commercial
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 70.6% of revenue in Q1 FY27; segment mix described as stable QoQ.

segments.name: Geography: North America
segments.commentary: 75.1% of revenue; mix described as stable.

segments.name: Accounts beyond top 20
segments.commentary: Contribute 33.4% of total revenue; almost doubled YoY in rupee terms; management says this drove growth.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected back in the 19%–20% range in H2 FY27; management confirmed 19–20% for Q4 FY27 when asked, pulling forward the earlier 6–8 quarter normalisation window (from Oct 2025) to 6 quarters, i.e., by Q4 FY27.
Organic growth in FY27 expected to be better than FY26, with acceleration in H2.
Outcome-based omnichannel engagement (north of $10 million ACV) starts recognising revenue from Q3 FY27; costs already incurred since Q4 FY26, so most revenue expected to drop to bottom line.
Q2 wage hike cycle expected to be offset by workforce transformation savings and Tectonic-related revenue ramp, keeping margins stable rather than declining as in historical Q2.
Undesignated hedges remain material until December 2026; management says hedge accounting adoption removes future MTM volatility from operating margins.
capex_capacity: Management said proprietary tech investment (data layer, Cortex context layer, apps and workflows) has been ratcheted up, but costs continue to be expensed rather than capitalised, though management acknowledged a technical case for capitalisation.
Workforce transformation and Gen AI productivity initiatives across operations and support functions expected to widen progressively.
demand_pricing: Active client count rose 14 QoQ to 105; customers in $10M–$25M bucket increased by 2 to 9; $1M+ clients rose from 36 to 54 over two years (per management, since Q1 FY25).

Q1 deal wins: one $3M–$5M deal with a top-5 customer (content platform migration); four $1M–$3M annual contracts (three commercial, one medical), including Tectonic extension from Germany to Spain; several sub-$1M lead-in deals.
Large Tectonic (Gen AI) engagement in Germany showed measured offtake on existing scope but expanded to Spain.

Outcome-based (pure) contracts are a small part; about 60% of revenue is output-plus-outcome based, with the rest largely hybrid FTE contracts. Hybrid deals typically take 3–4 quarters to ramp to full output revenue.
Renewals run on Jan–Dec cycles; net revenue retention stated above 100%; no major enterprise renewal loss historically.
Industry: top 20 global pharma revenue growing roughly 10%–12% YoY in calendar Q1 2026; immunology, oncology and mental health growing double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a delay to margin normalisation, given Q4 vs H2 wording, and what is the nature of the investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no delay: the normalisation is now targeted within 6 quarters from Oct 2025 (by March 2027), not the 6–8 range. Investments were in onsite commercial, medical, consulting and tech staff, plus large strategic deals (Tectonic; a >$1B US brand portfolio physician-outreach contract). Management confirmed this holds despite these deal investments.

qa_highlights.question: What was organic growth and BioPharm contribution; what was constant-currency growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management no longer splits BioPharm organic vs inorganic; it is now well integrated and both are in the base sequentially. Constant-currency growth was estimated at about 2.6%–2.7% QoQ, versus USD growth of 2.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What share of contracts are outcome-based and how does revenue and order book flow?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60% of contracts are output or outcome based; dedicated FTEs outside this are specialist roles supporting those contracts. Hybrid deals start FTE revenue within a month and ramp output revenue over 3–4 quarters. The large omnichannel deal is pure outcome-based with about 3 quarters of revenue deferral; the client has shared revenue upticks for 5 months.

qa_highlights.question: Gen AI strategy, IP protection, and data ownership concerns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a layered stack: Indegene data universe at the base, Cortex knowledge layer that is model-agnostic, agent layer (Content Super App, Medical Writing platform), and Transform AI workflows. Management said clients keep data ownership via contract and expect larger pharma to move toward on-prem open-weight models.

qa_highlights.question: What percentage of revenue is AI-led, and what are the margin drivers beyond already-incurred costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify AI-led revenue, saying AI is embedded across all work; content volumes rose 5–7x with falling unit costs. Other margin drivers are growth on fixed GTM and leadership costs and the Tectonic revenue uptick.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 19–20% margin target for Q4 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed yes for Q4 FY27 when asked directly.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the outcome-based omnichannel deal recognising revenue from Q3 FY27 and on the Tectonic and other large deals ramping; delays would push back the 19–20% target.
Enterprise AI adoption described as measured; Tectonic offtake on existing scope is slow.
Undesignated hedges remain material until December 2026, with residual accounting volatility.
US policy and drug pricing / MFN decisions flagged as the key external watch item; management currently sees the policy outlook as stable.
Receivables: DSO up 4 days to 67; management sees credit risk as minimal, but biotech and emerging-pharma contracts and outcome-based milestones are being monitored.
Q2 wage hike cycle could pressure margin before offsets kick in.
key_quotes: Nothing we have seen in this quarter changes that expectation. And if anything, our conviction that we are on track for this has increased.
What we are also seeing is that while the enthusiasm is real, enterprise adoption remains measured and the pace of change on the ground is slower.
No, there is no delay. In fact, what we said is 6 to 8. We had got a range over there. We are saying we don't need this range.
We're not breaking up organic and inorganic growth from a BioPharm perspective, anymore.
544172|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on margin recovery and deal pipeline, repeatedly saying nothing this quarter changes the 19–20% expectation and that conviction has increased. More guarded on enterprise AI adoption (described as measured and slower), and declined to quantify AI-led revenue or split BioPharm organic vs inorganic growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management reiterated 19-20% EBITDA margin by Q4 FY27 (confirmed when asked) from 16.9% in Q1, driven by the omnichannel deal (>$10M ACV) recognising revenue from Q3 FY27 with costs already incurred since Q4 FY26, plus workforce productivity savings.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides FY27 organic growth better than FY26 with H2 acceleration; Q1 USD revenue up 26.5% YoY to $112.5m and 2.5% QoQ, with active clients up 14 QoQ to 105 and $1M+ clients up to 54.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation not disclosed and no capacity additions discussed; proprietary tech spend is expensed rather than capitalised, and no new plant or capex plan was guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides FY27 organic growth better than FY26 with H2 acceleration; USD revenue grew 26.5% YoY to $112.5m, but no numeric FY27 revenue guide was given to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margin recovery to 19-20% by Q4 FY27 depends on the >$10M ACV omnichannel deal starting revenue in Q3 FY27 and on Q2 wage hikes being offset; Q1 EBITDA margin was only 16.9%, so a slip of the deal ramp would push the target back.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Gen AI stack (Cortex knowledge layer, agent layer with Content Super App and Medical Writing platform, Transform AI workflows) is described, but no specific launch dates were given.

rows.label: Omnichannel outcome-based deal revenue from Q3 FY27
rows.why: Deal above $10M ACV recognises revenue from Q3 FY27 with about 3 quarters of deferral, and costs already incurred since Q4 FY26, so most of the revenue should drop to margin.

rows.label: Workforce transformation and Gen AI productivity savings
rows.why: Savings are expected to offset the Q2 wage hike cycle and keep margins stable, versus the usual Q2 decline.

rows.label: Tectonic Gen AI expansion from Germany to Spain
rows.why: Tectonic extended to Spain in Q1 via a $1-3M annual contract, but offtake on existing German scope is measured and hybrid deals take 3-4 quarters to ramp.

tone.note: Management was confident that the 19-20% EBITDA margin is back by Q4 FY27 with no delay, backed by the omnichannel deal and workforce savings, but was guarded on enterprise AI adoption and declined to quantify AI-led revenue or split BioPharm organic versus inorganic growth.

544172|2026-09.headline: Indegene Q2 FY27 revenue rose 39.5% YoY to INR11,223 million, with EBITDA margin at 16.7% and a 19%+ target for Q4.
544172|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR11,223 million, up 39.5% YoY and 5.6% QoQ in INR, the fifth straight quarter of more than 5% QoQ INR growth. EBITDA was INR1,873 million at a 16.7% margin, absorbing about 150 bps from the annual wage hike, which productivity and favourable exchange rates largely offset. PAT rose 10% YoY to INR1,123 million, though a sharp fall in interest income (down 44% QoQ) weighed below EBITDA. Management reiterated a quarterly EBITDA margin of 19%+ by Q4 and said H2 would be stronger than H1, while the largest client dipped slightly and the $10 million outcome-based contract is expected to peak in Q4.

financial_highlights.change: +39.5% YoY, +5.6% QoQ in INR; +27.5% YoY and +4.4% QoQ in USD

financial_highlights.metric: Net DSO (net of unearned and unbilled revenue)

financial_highlights.change: Up from about US$69,000 a year ago

segments.name: Enterprise Commercial
segments.commentary: Contributed about 71% of revenue; deal wins skewed to Commercial and management expects Commercial to outgrow Medical over the next few quarters.

segments.name: Enterprise Medical
segments.commentary: Contributed about 25% of revenue; growth was weaker this quarter against a strong prior base, though $2 million-plus Medical deals were closed.

segments.name: Others (incl. Clinical)
segments.commentary: About 4% of revenue; growth lifted by a large Clinical deal that ramped in August and will annualise in Q3.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: North America 74%, Europe 23%, rest of world 3% of revenue.

guidance_outlook: Quarterly EBITDA margin of 19%+ by Q4 FY27, unchanged; management says H2 margin growth should outpace revenue growth as Q4 exits.
Organic growth for FY27 expected to be better than FY26; management says FY27 will be organically stronger than last year and H2 stronger than H1.
Wage hike is fully in the base; productivity, workforce transformation and operating leverage expected to add to EBITDA in Q3 and more in Q4.

Amortisation charge to decline from Q3 onward; yields expected to rise with higher rates and a shift to held-to-maturity instruments. Together these add about 90-95 bps to PBT, helping PAT margin expand faster than EBITDA margin.
Management does not give formal or quarter-on-quarter guidance.
BioPharm earnout: second tranche expected close to maximum payout, already fully provided on the balance sheet.
capex_capacity: Revenue per employee rising as GenAI platforms lift output and more work is priced on output or outcomes rather than time spent.
Tectonic run rate grew from about $1 million a quarter to $1.7 million this quarter; contracts now exceed $2 million a quarter.
Approximately 75% of the next two quarters' forex exposure is already hedged.
Dedicated tech partnership team in the US and India to work with frontier model and other technology companies.
demand_pricing: Q2 deal wins: 9 deals with ACV around $1 million or more, including one $5 million-plus win (expansion of the top-5 client's content migration outside the US), one $3-5 million global content factory win with a top-20 pharma, and one win with a top-30 pharma replacing an incumbent.
Four further deals in the $1-3 million range, split evenly between Enterprise Commercial and Enterprise Medical; Tectonic extended to Canada, the first market outside Europe.
Top 5 accounts grew 9.2% QoQ in INR; top 20 grew about 6.7% QoQ. Active clients 107 (31 more YoY); clients above $1 million rose to 59 from 54; clients above $10 million at 13.
Largest client is 7.8% of revenue; top 10 clients are 49%. This client's revenue eased as Tectonic ramps slowly, and one customer dropped from the $25 million-plus cohort to just below it.
Most Q2 wins were output- or outcome-based rather than FTE-based. The company is converting FTE contracts to hybrid contracts at renewal.
A $10 million ACV outcome-based contract (calendar-year threshold) recognised only a small amount in Q2; the bulk is expected in H2, with a true-up in Q4 after customer confirmation in Feb/Mar.
BioPharm: cost synergies of about $1.5 million a year reinvested in expanding BioPharm's go-to-market team from 3 to 9. Transition services closed by end-February, ahead of the March target.
Management sees competition from agencies and CROs, not IT services firms, in the deals it pursues.

qa_highlights.question: What are Tectonic run rates and contract values?
qa_highlights.answer: Tectonic grew from about $1 million a quarter to $1.7 million this quarter; contracts have crossed $2 million a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the largest client's ramp slower while scope grows, and how is Tectonic ROI measured?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to central teams driving centralisation while local brand teams stay decentralised; it expects this to play out over time. Tectonic is not measured standalone; ROI will be judged across the full upstream value chain.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a cap on outcome-based revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not give a cap. Most Q2 wins were output- or outcome-based, and FTE contracts are being converted to hybrid models at renewal.

qa_highlights.question: Is the $10 million outcome-based deal in revenue yet, and when will it ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: A small amount was recognised in Q2; most is ahead, with H2 the main recognition period and Q4 the peak after the true-up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin walk from 16.7% toward 18-19%?
qa_highlights.answer: Productivity and workforce transformation added about 85 bps in Q2 QoQ; favourable FX and operating leverage should keep helping in Q3 and Q4, with the $10 million contract adding more in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the largest client's dip temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; the client's $5 million-plus win is ramping, and management expects it back above $25 million in 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company expect H2 to be stronger than Q2 momentum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not guide quarterly, but expects FY27 organic growth above FY26 and H2 stronger than H1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the frontier model AI a threat, and how do TCS-type IT players affect competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not see frontier labs as a threat and is partnering with them; it sees little IT services competition in the Commercial and Medical deals it pursues.

risks_watch: Largest client (7.8% of revenue) revenue eased QoQ; Tectonic ramp is slow and the client's central and local teams are not yet aligned.
A top client slipped below the $25 million-plus cohort; recovery depends on the $5 million-plus deal ramping over 2-3 quarters.
The $10 million outcome-based contract's revenue and margin benefit depends on meeting a full-year threshold, with the true-up in Q4 after February-March confirmation.
DSO rose to 69 days and unbilled revenue increased; management expects normalisation in Q3-Q4.
Interest income fell 44% QoQ on mark-to-market losses; recovery depends on yields rising as expected.
Medical segment growth lagging Commercial; the company is still investing in Medical.
Frontier AI labs moving into pharma drug discovery and content; management views this as a partnering opportunity rather than a threat.

544174|2026-03.headline: TBO Tek Q4 FY26 grew YoY on top and bottom line despite Middle East war; Q1 FY27 guided better than Q4 and last year, with no figures given.

January and February showed strong operating leverage, margin expansion and EBITDA growth YoY, but March was a washout and erased the quarter-level leverage. Management expects Q1 FY27 to beat Q4 and last year on both GTV and gross profit, while declining to quantify it. Cash flow from operations was negative in FY26, which management attributed mainly to timing items (Brazil anticipation discontinuation, war-related receivable delays, PLB payouts and deposits classified as working capital) and expects reversion to over 100% cash conversion by year-end.

544174|2026-06.headline: TBO TEK Q1 FY27: EBITDA-to-GTV of 1.3% and operating leverage shown despite Middle East disruption; 24% Europe growth, 15% organic CC growth.
544174|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) as the toughest in two years due to Middle East-driven travel disruption, yet reported top-line and bottom-line growth. Europe grew 24% YoY and Middle East was flat (1% CC growth), with Classic Vacations (acquired about six months ago) adding North America scale. EBITDA margins expanded faster than gross profit, which management cited as evidence of operating leverage. Management began reporting constant-currency numbers because a roughly 11% INR-vs-CC gap in hotel GTV distorted YoY growth. Management declined to give a timeline for Middle East normalisation or a long-term margin target.

544174|2026-09.headline: TBO TEK Q2 FY27: GTV up 16% while adjusted EBITDA rose 27%, but management expects a tough Q3 with Middle East and Europe disruption.
544174|2026-09.overview: Management reported 16% GTV growth and 27% adjusted EBITDA growth for Q2 FY27, its second consecutive quarter of operating leverage. Middle East grew 10% in constant currency and Europe and APAC grew over 30%, despite conflict and October disruptions in Saudi Arabia and European cities. Management said Q3 will be tough and is aiming only for year-on-year growth in top line and bottom line, with the U.S. elections seen as an inflection point. Classic Vacations (acquired about a year ago) is expected to weigh on reported growth, and a Rs. 8.1 crore fraud loss in the UAE subsidiary was flagged as exceptional.

segments.name: Middle East
segments.commentary: Most impacted market due to conflict; grew 10% in constant currency (about 20% reported), still below prior-year baseline; management believes it is gaining share.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Now the largest source market, growing about 36% and about 36% of total GTV; newer markets such as Germany and Eastern Europe grew triple digits on small bases, while UK and Ireland grew on a much larger base.

segments.name: APAC
segments.commentary: Grew north of 30% in the quarter, per management.

segments.name: Classic Vacations (North America)
segments.commentary: Acquired about one year ago; about 20 sales hires added, with about half under six months tenure. Management expects it to be a drag on reported growth near term; TBO sales into Classic rose to about 8% of Classic GTV from about 5% last quarter.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Monthly transacting buyers grew 1% in the quarter and 4% in H1 across about 24,000 quarterly active agents; management is pushing non-air business, which has higher profitability.

segments.name: Hotels
segments.commentary: Management expects hotel GP margins in Q2 levels to hold if conditions stay stable, but may need to change stance if supply rises and demand falls.

Operating leverage expected to hold over the next two to eight quarters if SG&A growth stays below GP growth; trailing 12-month margin suggested as the better guide given seasonality.
No incremental investment needed for operating leverage; upside in GP expected to flow to bottom line.

demand_pricing: Demand pressure intensified in October after attacks on Saudi airports hit Saudi inbound and outbound travel, with prior bookings cancelled; rioting in European cities (Paris, Madrid, Barcelona, Italy) raised cancellations.
Management is prioritising market share gains via agent penetration, and focusing on dollar revenue stability and high-value transactions over volume.

Hotel and air GP margins held; organic gross profit margin held at 5.5-5.6% despite lower take rate due to supplier mix (commission vs net models).
Business mix between API and B2A (smaller agents) remained about 50:50; B2A GP margin slightly higher than API.

Management views AI-driven B2C/OTA entry into agency as a threat but limited, citing credit-line knowledge and channel conflict with suppliers; sees complex, high-value itineraries as the defensible segment.

qa_highlights.question: How is demand holding up given elevated international airfares and geopolitical risk, especially at the premium end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed pressure that intensified in October due to Saudi airport attacks and European rioting; the company is focusing on share gains and dollar revenue stability.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 be lower than H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to forecast H2 precisely; internal aim is year-on-year growth in top line and bottom line for Q3, with U.S. elections seen as an inflection point.

qa_highlights.question: Will Classic be a drag on overall growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman-level answer: mathematically yes near term, since Classic is not yet growing near 30%; but Classic GP is about double organic GP per dollar of GTV, and its revenue reflects bookings made about a year earlier for groups.

qa_highlights.question: Classic integration milestones and timing of acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales team ramp and CRM are largely complete; TBO platform beta for Classic due late November, with gradual rollout over several months; results expected within the next couple of quarters, without a firm number.

qa_highlights.question: Rs. 8 crore fraud: what happened and what are the implications for the FEMA penalty?
qa_highlights.answer: Suspected employee collusion led to unauthorised bookings in a government travel agency account in the UAE subsidiary; police complaints filed in India and UAE, insurance claim initiated. FEMA adjudication order received after quarter-end; company will appeal and has not provided, citing high chances of winning.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the air take rate fall and is there reversal potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower incentives and refund income in H1; management expects GP to remain in a 1-1.2% range, with occasional quarterly dips and ad hoc airline incentives.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in FX loss and the working capital release?
qa_highlights.answer: FX loss reflects hedging premium costs plus losses on unhedged exposure (about 25% unhedged) versus last year's gain; working capital release reflected reversal of Middle East overdues and Brazil timing items, plus new credit lines replacing virtual cards, with positive impact expected through year-end.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 is the weakest quarter for Classic because it books on check-in basis, so Q3 should be better than Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Hotel GP margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to maintain Q2-like hotel margins if conditions stay the same, but may adjust if supply rises and demand falls.
