rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Classic Vacations sales team added about 20 hires (half under six months tenure) and TBO platform beta due late November with gradual rollout over several months; no physical capacity or plant capex discussed, and market development investments held flat for rest of FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 GTV grew 16% with Europe and APAC over 30% and Middle East 10% constant currency, but India monthly transacting buyers grew only 1% in the quarter and October disruptions in Saudi and Europe hit bookings; Q3 aim is only YoY growth, with no numeric guide.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the brief reports no utilisation figure and no new plant or land plan.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to forecast H2 precisely and only aims for YoY growth in Q3 on top and bottom line, with October disruptions in Saudi and Europe already hitting bookings.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management called Q3 tough with low visibility from Saudi conflict, European rioting and prior-booking cancellations; the Q3 aim is only YoY growth, and a rise in cancellations could push it below that.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: TBO platform beta for Classic Vacations is due late November, followed by gradual rollout over several months, with demonstrable Classic results targeted by summer season Q2 FY28 if macro clears.

rows.label: Classic Vacations results acceleration
rows.why: Management expects Classic to show better results over the next two to three quarters, with demonstrable results likely by summer Q2 FY28 if macro clears, but gave no firm number and Classic is not yet growing near 30%, so it remains a drag on reported growth near term.

rows.label: FEMA adjudication penalty outcome (UAE fraud)
rows.why: A FEMA adjudication order was received after quarter-end with no provision booked; the company will appeal, and the worst-case outcome is not quantified, while the Rs. 8 crore UAE fraud loss has an insurance claim initiated.

rows.label: Air take rate recovery
rows.why: Organic air take rate fell to about 2% from 2.3-2.4% on lower airline incentives and refunds; management guides air GP to 1-1.2% and expects only occasional quarterly dips, so no clear reversal.

tone.note: Management was confident on operating leverage, Classic's long-term thesis and the Europe/APAC growth, but cautious and evasive on Q3 and H2, declining to quantify currency-adjusted growth, Classic synergies or FY28 budget; analysts pressed on the Q3 outlook, Classic drag, demand at the premium end

544176|2026-03.headline: Aadhar Housing Q4 FY26: AUM crossed INR30,571 crore (+20% YoY), FY26 PAT INR1,096 crore (+20%), GNPA eased to 1.08%.
544176|2026-03.overview: Aadhar closed FY26 with AUM of INR30,571 crore, up 20% YoY, and record Q4 disbursements of INR3,087 crore (+20% YoY). FY26 disbursements were INR9,556 crore (+17%) and PAT was INR1,096 crore (+20%), or INR1,108 crore before the one-time Labour Code charge. GNPA was 1.08%, down 30 bps QoQ but up slightly from 1.05% a year earlier, with 1+ DPD improving 78-80 bps QoQ. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 20% AUM growth, about 20% profit growth and 17-18% disbursement growth, with spreads expected to contract 8-10 bps.

financial_highlights.change: -30 bps QoQ; vs 1.05% in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Exit cost of funds / exit spread

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: 73% of AUM; home loan disbursements grew about 26% YoY in Q4, helped by PMAY subsidies (about INR50 crore to about 15,000-16,000 customers) and a push on emerging markets.

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP / non-housing)
segments.commentary: 27% of AUM; LAP disbursement mix was about 24-25% in Q4 versus 28-29% typical, deliberately held back since the tariff shock. Management is open to lifting it to 27-28% of disbursements, but not in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Emerging and urban geographies
segments.commentary: Average ticket about INR10.9 lakh on the book. Emerging C is about INR8.5-8.6 lakh, emerging B INR10 lakh, emerging A INR12 lakh, urban INR17-18 lakh. Urban traction is 'encouraging' per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: about 20% AUM growth, about 20% profit growth, and 17-18% disbursement growth.
Spreads expected to contract by about 8-10 bps YoY, given incremental yields of about 13% against a book yield of about 13.52%; partly offset by LAP mix and self-employed shift.
Cost-to-income ratio expected to fall by about 50 bps in FY27, driven by productivity and AI-led sales tools.
Cost of funds expected to hold broadly flat for the next 2-3 quarters; management would be 'very happy' to hold the 7.7% exit rate through FY27.
Direct assignment (DA) volume expected to grow 10-15% in FY27 from about INR1,725 crore in FY26.
Long-term AUM milestone of INR50,000 crore targeted in about 3 years.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 626 across 22 states and more than 550 districts, after 5 branches added in Q4 and 46 in FY26.
Four branch categories: ultra micro (50-60 sq ft), micro, small and main. Small branches take 9-12 months to turn productive and urban branches 12-15 months.
Undrawn sanctions of INR1,687 crore, of which INR246 crore from NHB.
Liquidity of INR1,425 crore at end-Q4 FY26.
Employees: on-roll about 5,400-5,430 and off-roll about 3,900-3,965 at March 2026, versus 4,600 on-roll and 4,300 off-roll a year earlier.
Management expects Uttar Pradesh to be the largest contributor to growth; West Bengal flagged as a potential new state.
demand_pricing: Demand described as end-user driven, with first-time homebuyers prominent. Competition from banks is elevated in urban markets but steady in low-income segments.
Management cited state-level BLC and AHP pipelines (for example, 25,000+ units in Odisha) as supporting demand.
Bounce rates stable for six quarters and unaffected by West Asia conflict; collections team of about 2,000 briefed to be careful.
Low-income segment: management says about 18% share of the low-income HFC peer group, up from 16-17%.
Borrowing mix at March 2026: banks 51%, NHB 22%, NCD 19%, ECB 5%, others 4%. 76% of borrowings are floating; 73-74% of assets are floating.
NCDs are 22% of borrowings, of which 68% are fixed. NHB funding is roughly 50% fixed and 50% floating.

qa_highlights.question: Why has LAP growth lagged, and what is the outlook for other income and ESOP cost?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP slowdown was deliberate since the tariff shock; LAP is 27% of AUM and LAP mix in Q4 was about 26%. Assignment income reflected spreads 80-85 bps better, not larger volumes. About INR6-7 crore of Q4 fee income was one-time. ESOP charge of INR13.5 crore is a Q4 item.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for yields and spreads in FY27 given the rate environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a 2-3 quarter rate hold. Spread contraction of 8-10 bps is guided at the current 25-26% LAP mix. Each 5 percentage points shifted from HL to LAP adds about 400 bps on that portion.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 1+ DPD improvement and the sequential jump in disbursements?
qa_highlights.answer: 1+ DPD fell about 80 bps (not risen, as the analyst framed it) over 18 months of focus on collections. Sequential disbursement strength came from Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Delhi, Karnataka and Uttarakhand. Incremental borrowing cost rose about 10 bps QoQ because bank drawdowns were deferred into Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why did opex-to-AUM rise sequentially in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 always carries sales contests and one-time incentive costs. Cost-to-income improved YoY from 37.9% to 37.1% in Q4. Full-year cost-to-income was 35.9%, down from 36.4%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ticket size trends and the sources of the home loan growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental ticket size ranged INR12.5-13.5 lakh over recent quarters, against INR10.9 lakh on book. Management aims to hold book ticket size at INR10-11.5 lakh, and to hold non-home loans to about 70:30 with home loans over the medium term.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the funding book can still reprice, and how far has cost of funds fallen?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental cost fell from 8.4% to 7.6% YoY, with banks passing on 70-75 bps. Exit cost of funds moved from 8.14% to 7.72%, with 15 bps passed to customers. NCDs (22%) are mostly fixed, so the remaining repricing is limited to bank and floating NHB funds.

risks_watch: Geopolitical (West Asia) stress on borrowers; bounce rates and collections are the early indicators to watch.
Spread compression of 8-10 bps YoY if LAP mix stays at about 25-26%; cost of funds could rise given the 76% floating-rate liability book.
Competitive pressure from banks in urban markets.
Ticket size drift: management targets INR10-11.5 lakh, with construction-cost inflation expected to push it higher.
LAP usage is a lever to protect yields but is deferred; delinquency on LAP is about 0.7-0.75% higher on GNPA and must be watched when mix is raised.
Labour Code exceptional charge of INR16 crore taken in Q3; ESOP cost of INR13.5 crore in Q4 is a one-time item per management.
544176|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and execution, with guidance reiterated. Cautious and deliberate on LAP and rates, explicitly holding back on LAP and expecting a 2-3 quarter rate hold. Some answers were loose on numbers, with corrections made live (for example, 1+ DPD fell rather than rose).
key_quotes: On all the 3 critical parameters, we have stood by our guidance and commitment to the market.
We don't want to do something in haste, which will go out and look at our delinquency numbers.
Our view is that the interest rate cycle has stagnated and to a certain extent, will be stagnant for at least two, three quarters.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided spreads to contract 8-10 bps YoY in FY27 on incremental yields of about 13% vs book yield of 13.52%; cost-to-income down about 50 bps is the only offset, and cost of funds is expected flat for 2-3 quarters at a 7.7% exit rate.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Network at 626 branches after 46 added in FY26 (5 in Q4), undrawn sanctions of INR1,687 crore and state BLC/AHP pipelines support growth, but no forward branch count or capacity target was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Guidance held at about 20% AUM growth and 17-18% disbursement growth after FY26 disbursements of INR9,556 crore (+17%) and Q4 record of INR3,087 crore (+20%).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20% AUM, 20% profit and 17-18% disbursement growth without raising it, and expects spreads to contract 8-10 bps.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Spread compression of 8-10 bps YoY and 76% floating-rate borrowings expose margins if rates move, and West Asia stress is a watch item, though bounce rates were stable for six quarters and GNPA eased to 1.08%.

rows.label: LAP mix lift to 27-28% of disbursements
rows.why: LAP is 27% of AUM but only 24-25% of Q4 disbursements vs 28-29% typical; management is open to lifting it to 27-28% but not in Q1 FY27, and each 5 pp shift from HL to LAP adds about 400 bps on that portion.

rows.label: Direct assignment volume growth
rows.why: DA volume guided to grow 10-15% from about INR1,725 crore in FY26, with Q4 assignment income lifted by spreads 80-85 bps better rather than larger volumes.

rows.label: Cost-to-income down about 50 bps in FY27
rows.why: FY26 cost-to-income was 35.9% vs 36.4% in FY25 and management guides another 50 bps via productivity and AI-led sales tools, with on-roll staff down to about 5,400-5,430 from 4,600 a year ago.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, asset quality (GNPA 1.08%, collections above 99.8%) and reiterated FY27 guidance, but was deliberately cautious on LAP and expects a 2-3 quarter rate hold; analysts probed spreads, LAP mix, DPD trend and ticket size, and some answers were corrected live.

544176|2026-06.headline: Aadhar Housing Q1 FY27 PAT rose 19% YoY to INR282 crores on AUM of INR31,364 crores (+18%), with disbursements hit by a switch to cheque-clearance recognition.
544176|2026-06.overview: AUM reached INR31,364 crores, up 18% YoY, and exit spread held at 5.8% despite a 15 bps RPLR cut in February 2026. Disbursement was INR2,036 crores on the new cheque-clearance basis, against INR2,359 crores (+19% YoY) on the old cheque-handover basis, as the company moved recognition to clearance from Q1 FY27. Asset quality was stable YoY, with GNPA at 1.31% (down 3 bps) and Stage 2 at 3.3% (down 40 bps), though Q1 credit cost rose seasonally. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20% AUM growth, 20% PAT growth and 17-18% disbursement growth, with the next three quarters targeted above 20%.

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: 73% of AUM; non-home loans 27%. Incremental disbursement mix currently 76:24 home vs non-home, versus a historical 70:30.

segments.name: Non-home loans
segments.commentary: Disbursement growth slowed to about 22% in the quarter by the analyst's read; management called the slowdown a deliberate choice linked to the West Asia situation and the riskier profile of these loans.

segments.name: Emerging vs urban branches
segments.commentary: About 450 of 628 branches are in emerging locations. Emerging yields are 14-14.8% versus 11.5-12% in urban; average ticket size rose only from INR10.4 lakh to INR11 lakh.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance held: 20% AUM growth, 20% PAT growth, 17-18% disbursement growth for the full year.
Disbursement growth above 20% targeted for each of the next three quarters; management expects Q2 to close the Q1 shortfall, with Q2 growth of about 23-24% or more.
July 2026 disbursement close to INR900 crores, per management.
Spread floor of 5.5% reiterated; over 2-3 years spreads expected to end near 5.5%, ROA 4.3-4.4% steady state, and ROE around 17% in a couple of years.
Cost-to-income expected to fall 30-40 bps a year; cost-to-AUM about 6-7 bps a year.
Credit cost expected to settle at 23-25 bps for the full year, with GNPA targeted at about 1.1% at year end.
Branch openings of 45-50 planned for Q3; Q1 had only 2 openings versus a 40-50 annual pace.
capex_capacity: Network at 628 branches across 22 states and 550+ districts as of June 2026.
New branches target productivity within 9-15 months; Q1 opened only 2 branches, with 5-7 planned and pushed into July.
Capital adequacy of 42.9% Tier 1 gives room for growth; the IPO's INR1,000 crores primary raise is meant to fund growth for the next 3-4 years. No plan to return capital.
Operational-risk capital set aside at about 6-7% of capital; balance-sheet risk weight about 45%.
demand_pricing: Demand described as healthy and end-user, first-time-buyer driven, particularly in emerging markets; management reports no demand-side issues in urban locations.
Spreads held at 5.8% after a 15 bps RPLR cut in February 2026; management says it protects spreads over chasing yields.
Management expects 5-7% overlap with new affordable-segment entrants; Aadhar sits one notch below in low-income housing.
Incremental yields flat QoQ; management expects no decline if the urban/emerging mix moves toward 50:50.
NRI-linked exposure described as minimal; state-level rule caps any state at 15% of AUM, incremental disbursement or distribution.
Delhi's share rose slightly, a lower-yield state, yet yields held.

financial_highlights.change: includes ~INR14 crores quarterly ESOP cost; ~33-34% excluding it

qa_highlights.question: How is the company sustaining asset yields despite the 15 bps RPLR cut and competition, and is it due to pricing, mix, or segment changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited the urban/emerging strategy (about 450 of 628 branches in emerging locations) and a ticket size that moved only from INR10.4 lakh to INR11 lakh. Delhi's share rose slightly though it is a lower-yield state, and yields still held. No major state-mix shift was reported.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company plan to sustain 20% growth and the 5.5% spread floor amid new affordable-segment entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Book spread is about 5.8%. Management expects a 5-7% overlap with new entrants, since Aadhar sits one notch below them in low-income housing, and says the emerging tilt will keep spreads above 5.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the July disbursement number and how will the cheque-clearance change be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: July disbursement is close to INR900 crores. Management expects Q2 growth of about 23-24% or more, with Q2 substantially covering the Q1 shortfall as the carry-forward business is recognised over a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cheque-clearance change affecting interest income, and what drove the sequential employee cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest income is affected by only 2-3 days, which management called immaterial. Sequential employee cost rose on the annual increment of about 10-12%. Year-on-year, the 27% rise is mainly INR14-15 crores of quarterly ESOP cost; excluding it, employee cost growth is about 14-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 rise in GNPA and Stage 2 seasonal, and what is the full-year credit cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 credit cost is seasonally high at 40-45 bps for the last 2-3 years. Management expects the year to end with credit cost of 23-25 bps and GNPA near 1.1%. Q1 rose 25 bps versus a usual 30-35 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the liquidity buffer and cost-of-funds outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Liquidity was INR2,371 crores at quarter end, above 10% of borrowings, but management targets 7-8% intra-quarter and this rises at quarter end from drawdowns. Cost of funds moved little in Q1. Management sees no near-term impact from rate rises and says 75% of assets can be repriced.

risks_watch: Disbursement and PAT growth depend on Q2 catching up on the cheque-clearance shortfall; management targets Q2 growth of about 23-24% or more and above 20% for the next three quarters.
Non-home loan disbursement growth slowed to about 22%, and the home/non-home mix stood at 76:24 against a historical 70:30; management expects normalisation from Q3 once West Asia uncertainty eases.
Credit cost and GNPA: Q1 credit cost rose seasonally by 25 bps; the year-end GNPA target of about 1.1% and credit cost of 23-25 bps must hold.
Competitive pressure from affordable-segment entrants with a 5-7% overlap; spread floor of 5.5% and incremental yields flat QoQ.
Branch expansion slowed to 2 openings in Q1 against a 40-50 annual pace; 45-50 openings are planned for Q3 and 5-7 were pushed into July.
Cost of funds and interest-rate risk, with management expecting no imminent pass-through in the current or next quarter.
Monsoon and West Asia-related stress on rural and semi-urban cash flows, and NRI-linked exposure, which management called minimal.
key_quotes: Effective quarter 1, we have taken a step of transitioning our loan accounting to cheque clearance basis model of disbursement recognition, which is a forward -looking approach and a significant milestone in our commitment to governa nce, transparency and putting customer at the forefront.

Our approach, as always, has been to protect spreads rather than c hase yields, which we are doing by tilting the mix towards emerging branches by staying disciplined on loan against property and by continuing to drive productivity per branch and per employee, so that operating leverage does the work that pricing cannot.
And as we look at the current quarter and the upcoming quarter, which is quarter 3, we stand by our numbers of 45 to 50 branches.
So, I think Q2 itself, you will compensate the loss which we saw in Q1.
544176|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and reassuring on FY27 guidance and asset quality, with management reiterating 20% AUM and PAT growth. It is more cautious on the West Asia situation, monsoon risk and non-home loan slowdown, and it defended the cheque-clearance accounting change as a governance step rather than a loss.

rows.why: Management stands by 45-50 branch openings for FY27 (Q3 stated) against 628 branches today, but only 2 opened in Q1 and 5-7 slipped into July, so timing is at risk.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.why: FY27 guidance of 20% AUM and 20% PAT growth was only reiterated, with Q1 disbursement hit by the accounting switch, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.why: Q1 disbursement is on a new basis that lags, Q2 must deliver 23-24% growth to close the shortfall, and non-home growth slowed to about 22% with West Asia and monsoon stress flagged.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products, brands or loan segments were discussed in the brief.

rows.label: Q2 catch-up of cheque-clearance shortfall
rows.why: Management expects Q2 disbursement growth of about 23-24% or more to substantially cover the Q1 shortfall, with July disbursement close to INR900 crores.

rows.label: Credit cost and GNPA normalisation
rows.why: Management targets full-year credit cost of 23-25 bps and GNPA near 1.1% at year end, versus GNPA of 1.31% today and Q1 credit cost up 25 bps seasonally.

rows.label: Non-home loan and mix normalisation
rows.why: Home/non-home mix stands at 76:24 against a historical 70:30 and non-home growth slowed to about 22%; management expects normalisation from Q3 once West Asia uncertainty eases.

544177|2026-03.headline: Aztec H2 FY26 revenue up 12.4% YoY to ₹47.61 cr; FY26 revenue up 9.2% to ₹96.53 cr with EBITDA margin at 14.3%.
544177|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹96.53 cr (+9.2% YoY) and H2 revenue of ₹47.61 cr (+12.4% YoY). EBITDA rose 9.6% to ₹13.96 cr, with margin at 14.3% versus 14% a year earlier, while PAT was ₹7.41 cr, held back by higher depreciation, write-offs (up 85%), lower other income and tax. Management said the growth was below the earlier double-digit guidance and that it will prioritise margins over top-line growth. Capex is planned across infrastructure, exports and technology, but the absolute amount has not been disclosed and funding (internal accruals, debt, possibly equity) is still under evaluation.

financial_highlights.change: Impacted by higher depreciation, write-offs (+85% YoY) and lower other income
Tech infrastructure, systems, manufacturing, digital platforms

segments.name: Jettings (acquired subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹19.22 cr (+7%); EBITDA up over 18%. Employee cost down 20% and operating expenses down 11%, while purchases rose 41.5% to about ₹9 cr. Interest cost is the remaining weak point due to working capital intensity.

segments.name: Consumables (inks, wash, makeup/cleaner fluids)
segments.commentary: Management said makeup and cleaner fluids grew about 15% YoY and inks about 12.5% YoY in selling volumes. Ink and solvent mix is expected to shift as ink formulation is modified to reduce solvent consumption.

segments.name: Printers (CIJ, TIJ, DOD, laser, TTO, PIJ)
segments.commentary: An installed base of 8,000+ printers was cited, with 1,550 printers sold in FY26 per the call; the group-level tally was not reconciled on the call. Extrusion accounts for the largest share of CIJ applications (about 85%), and CIJ is said to make up ~95% across extrusion, food and FMCG.

segments.name: Government tenders and automation projects
segments.commentary: Two government tenders were won last year and more are in the pipeline. Management says project business is multi-month, high-ticket and built around a separate North and South team.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated sustainable double-digit medium-term growth but did not give a near-term number, and said margins take priority over top-line growth.
Management said it expects to hold the current EBITDA margin (about 13-14%) in FY27 and does not plan to chase top-line growth at the expense of margins.

Capex is split broadly as 41% infrastructure capacity, 30% exports and global expansion, 8% tech and ERP, 3% R&D and 5% product development and other initiatives. The absolute amount is still under board consideration.
Management said the full-year effect of recent investments will show up in FY27, and free cash flow is expected to rise with that.
capex_capacity: Capex is planned over the coming period across infrastructure capacity (41%), exports and global expansion (30%), tech and ERP (8%), R&D (3%) and other product development (5%). The absolute rupee amount has not been disclosed.
Funding is planned through internal accruals and debt, which management said have high visibility; equity remains under evaluation.
Backward integration: inks, wash and solvents are about 100% in-house; about 95% of the ink portion is integrated. Printer spares are 40-50% indigenised, with more in beta testing.
The Jettings integration progressed through the year-end and is contributing to operational synergies.
Management said the capex was deferred because of Middle East conflict visibility, and it was not committing advances until the outlook clears.
demand_pricing: Management said extrusion (PVC/CPVC pipes and wires) slowed in FY26 due to Middle East conflict effects on input costs, while FMCG and food did not see substantial slowdown.
Customer mix: extrusion is the largest vertical; others include food/pharma/FMCG, industrial equipment and automation, agriculture, packaging and printing, and 'others' at about 16.6% of top line.

Pricing: management said the company passes input cost increases on through service-linked AMCs, and that customers negotiate but ultimately accept. Inventory was built only to the extent customers could absorb, and the company declined to stock up at war-peak prices.
After-sales economics: management cited ₹80,000-1,20,000 per printer per year for extrusion customers (about ₹60,000 for some pharma and FMCG accounts), roughly equal to the printer cost per year.
Competition: management cited a fully integrated ink-to-printer model, backward integration and import-duty advantage over MNCs with overseas manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: Installed base of 8,000+ printers versus 1,550 sold in FY26 does not reconcile with the prior 5,000+ base.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the installed base includes Jettings-led sales and after-sales, and that the group-level number is correct. It was not broken down by company.

qa_highlights.question: Growth outlook: why should double-digit growth return after the 9.2% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Devraj Pandya said growth is the result of recent investments flowing into revenue over time, and that margins will be protected even if top-line guidance is missed. He cited diversification beyond extrusion as a hedge.

qa_highlights.question: Jettings acquisition: benefits achieved and performance versus plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Jettings' revenue rose 7% to ₹19.22 cr and EBITDA margin rose to 10.2%, with lower employee and operating costs. It said the interest cost is still high because of working capital needs.

qa_highlights.question: Government tenders and automation: size and timing of contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two tenders were won last year with more in the pipeline and that project business is multi-month, with a separate North and South team. The revenue size was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Capex amount and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the absolute capex is under board consideration and that broad percentage allocations are set. Funding is planned through internal accruals and debt; equity is still being evaluated.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the Iran/Middle East conflict on raw material prices and pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory was built only to customers' absorption capacity, and that service-linked AMCs make it easier to pass through costs. It expects the disruption to ease but said post-ceasefire effects can last 3-5 months.

risks_watch: Revenue growth of 9.2% fell short of the earlier double-digit framework, and PAT growth was held back by depreciation, write-offs and tax.
Supply chain: heavy reliance on imported printheads and electronic components; management acknowledged this and cited a Taiwan Strait scenario as a risk.
Equity dilution: management said equity is still under consideration, while an analyst argued against it given the market capitalisation of about ₹123 cr versus reserves of about ₹44 cr.
Jettings working capital intensity and high interest cost.
Middle East conflict effects on raw material cost, CPVC/PVC demand and extrusion customer spending.

544179|2026-03.headline: Go Digit reports 17.7% post-tax ROE on Indian Accounting Standards basis for FY26 and a 105.7% combined ratio, with GDPI up 16.2%.
544179|2026-03.overview: Management presented FY26 results re-based to Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS, effective 1 April 2026), which were audited for the first time, while stressing its internal KPIs remain NEP-based combined ratio plus DAC and IGAAP solvency. Full-year profit before tax on Ind AS plus DAC was INR239 crores in Q4 (vs INR142 crores) and post-tax profit was INR179 crores (vs INR106 crores). Q4 GDPI grew 21.3% and full-year GDPI grew 16.2%, while Q4 GWP growth slowed to about 6.2% because of a health reinsurance non-renewal. Solvency improved to 2.42 and AUM reached about INR23,000 crores (up 16.3%). Management said it sees motor pricing correcting in April and expects a regulatory response on expense of management (EOM) within 2-3 months.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Private car 44%, two-wheeler 32%, commercial vehicles 24% of business. OD/TP mix 38/62 vs industry 41/59. Own-damage loss ratio rose YoY; corrective action started, with impact expected from July-September quarter.

segments.name: Health (incl. group)
segments.commentary: Q4 health reinsurance non-renewal cost about INR252 crores (about INR200 crores in Q3). Retail is under 7% of health; employer-employee about 73% and non-employer-employee about 22%. Health market share about 1.3-1.4%.

segments.name: Fire / commercial
segments.commentary: Fire gross loss ratio 51% in FY26 vs 48% in FY25; net loss ratio rose on two large claims (INR55 crores gross in Q4). Cat treaty retention raised from INR36 crores to INR45 crores; earthquake limit raised from INR1,600 crores to INR2,000 crores.

segments.name: Two-wheeler
segments.commentary: Q4 two-wheeler premium was INR556 crores vs INR365 crores a year earlier, which pushed up EOM by about 3.5% in the quarter. Management estimates about 40% of FY26 two-wheeler business was new business.

segments.name: Crop
segments.commentary: Management plans to bid directly in government crop tenders this year, having previously written crop mainly through reinsurance acceptance; scheme structure not yet announced.

guidance_outlook: Management gives no numerical guidance; it said ROE and profitability are the focus.
Motor OD loss ratio expected to stabilise in July-September 2026 quarter and then fall; motor overall loss ratio targeted not to rise YoY in FY27.
New specialty commercial lines expected to reach about INR1,000 crores premium over 3-5 years.
Equity allocation at 8.5% of AUM with a 12.5% ceiling considered comfortable; fixed income duration at 4.5 years, with room to extend if rates rise.
Management expects EOM-related regulation within 2-3 months and expects the commission/management-expense split to be fixed.
Next year's effective tax rate expected at 25.2%.
capex_capacity: Reinsurance renewed for FY27: fire and other treaty capacity increased; property and engineering capacity raised with better commission terms.
A new miscellaneous treaty covers new risk types; an 11% quota share on non-motor, non-health premium was added to cap accumulation in Gujarat, Maharashtra and NCR.
Net retention for scooters and school buses was lowered through funds-withheld reinsurance after the Kolkata incident; management said this does not affect AUM.
Leverage rose to 5% (4.65% in June 2024); management expects it to hold around 5% over the next two years.
demand_pricing: Motor: management sees April 2026 price and commission correction in the market, and believes the market cannot sustain current prices. Growth outlook depends on the new-vehicle cycle, which was strong in H2 FY25.

Health: management plans to grow group health only if pricing improves by about 5%, and expects growth of 50-60% if loss ratio also falls by about 2%.
TP pricing: no motor TP hike this year; management said it is not privy to regulator thinking.
Competition: new non-life entrants are coming; management said it is not losing sleep over them and that EOM relief for new insurers should be split between commission and management expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Will fire profitability fall given higher cat reinsurance cost, net loss ratio deterioration, and a possibly softer fire market? Also, what is the crop strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is comfortable with fire profitability, citing better commission in fire and engineering and profit commission on earned premium. Crop: will bid directly in tenders this year, pending government scheme structure.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fairfax keep its stake after the reverse merger?

qa_highlights.question: Why did motor OD loss ratio rise and what is the retention and renewal data?

qa_highlights.question: How will EOM compliance be managed at company level and how does Indian acquisition cost compare internationally?

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the discounting benefit and will long-run Ind AS investment yield match IGAAP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the discount-rate effect is stable unless rates move sharply; it moved to 7.09% from 6.9%. Management said investment decisions should be judged on ROE, not on mark-to-market, and that risk-based capital may favour companies with high equity allocation.

Fixed income duration and rates: duration is 4.5 years; an interest rate move could affect unrealised losses (INR99 crores at 31 March 2026).

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the 11 June 2026 Supreme Court TP ruling on TP loss ratio and reserving, and is the step-up recurring?

qa_highlights.answer: Chairman confirmed one large fire claim in Q1, but said gross fire loss ratio was 67%; he argued loss ratios are assessed on a gross basis because 80% of fire risk is ceded to reinsurers, and the company gives up treaty commission on some business to protect treaty profitability.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 36,000 TP claims settled since inception, 83% by compromise and 17% by court award; it reported reserve release of INR204 crore for FY18-19 falling to INR132 crore over later years, said no MAD concept is used, and declined to guide on future releases. qa_highlights.question: Why has the gap between normalized rent and cash-flow rent widened?

qa_highlights.question: Why is Transform's third-party share about 92%, and what are its margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Transform has shifted to third-party work; the 92% reflects this quarter's delivery mix and is expected to stay structurally high. Margins: about 15% on landlord-partner work and 18-20% on third-party, blending to 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the implied FY27 cash EBITDA margin only about 10% when occupancy is strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the exit of one large client, where the company kept fixed costs on five centres to refill them, and a timing gap of 3-4 quarters between landlord rent resets (many 2021 leases) and customer repricing. H2 is expected to be better, with Q4 showing a meaningful improvement.

qa_highlights.answer: About 37 of 242 live centres (about 15%) are Gold/premium. Of the 13 properties in LOI or fit-out, about 10 are premium. The premium mix is expected to reach about 80:20 by end FY27. All pipeline assets are institutional.

544181|2026-09.headline: Awfis Q2 FY27 normalized revenue rose 26% YoY to INR 451 crore and cash EBITDA rose 45% to INR 49 crore at a 10.8% margin.

Reported revenue was INR 439 crore (up 20%) and reported PBT nearly doubled to INR 31 crore. Occupancy rose at both mature centers (84.1%) and the blended portfolio (76.2%) despite net seat additions. qa_highlights.question: Why was AI spend capitalised, what is the amortisation period, and is any hotel spend capitalised?

544198|2026-06.headline: DEE Development Engineers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 31.6% YoY to Rs 294.5 crore and EBITDA margin hit 16.9%, despite ~Rs 25 crore of dispatches slipping into Q2.
544198|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs 294.5 crore, up 31.6% YoY, with operating EBITDA of Rs 49.7 crore (16.9% margin vs 16% a year earlier). Management said about Rs 25 crore of oil and gas dispatches, deferred by export customers amid Middle East disruption, moved into Q2. Profit after tax was Rs 16.1 crore, and the Rs 300 crore preferential issue (net ~Rs 293 crore, ~Rs 225 crore earmarked for debt repayment) closed in July. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of Rs 1,500 crore+ revenue, EBITDA margin above 19%, and order inflow of at least Rs 2,000 crore.

segments.name: Piping and heavy fabrication (core)
segments.commentary: Management guides Rs 1,150-1,250 crore from piping for FY27, with the balance from subsidiaries including Thailand. Piping and heavy fabrication are the large majority of revenue and order book.

segments.name: Thailand subsidiary
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about Rs 130 crore; target Rs 170-200 crore. Management says it is practically 100% booked for three years and no expansion is planned.

segments.name: Power PPA / non-core (Malwa, biomass pellets)
segments.commentary: Pellet plant (72,000 MT p.a., Muktsar) commissioned mid-Q1 FY27, so only partial contribution this quarter. Target combined non-core revenue around Rs 80 crore. Management said PPA EBIT went slightly negative (about Rs 1 crore) as fuel was diverted to the pellet plant; full operation expected from October.

segments.name: Seamless pipe plant (Anjar)
segments.commentary: Commissioned in FY26. Existing orders include about Rs 68 crore from L&T and a Rs 200 crore BHEL order, of which Rs 80-90 crore is expected to use in-house pipe. Management targets about 20% EBITDA on seamless pipe.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 1,500 crore+ reiterated; management called it a minimum and said the plan is to exceed it. Q1 is the weakest quarter, with Q4 typically the strongest.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided above 19%; management said it is 'absolutely on track'.
FY27 order inflow expected at least Rs 2,000 crore; Rs 700 crore already received, with Rs 1,300-1,800 crore expected in the rest of the year.
Net debt expected to be no more than Rs 400-425 crore by FY27 end; no plans for new debt this year.
Anjar plant utilisation expected at 60-65% this year and near 100% by end of FY28. Anjar revenue target of about Rs 1,500 crore by FY28-29.
Inventory days targeted at 150-160 by Q2 and 180-200 days for the overall working-capital cycle.
capex_capacity: Anjar pipe fabrication facility fully operational; seamless pipe plant commissioned in FY26. Plan is roughly 50-50 split between captive and outright-sale use of Anjar capacity.

Nuclear sector entry planned via a partner; management aims to finalise the partnership agreement in Q2 FY27.

Preferential issue proceeds of about Rs 293 crore net: about Rs 224-225 crore for debt or working-capital repayment, balance for general corporate purposes.
demand_pricing: Revenue slippage: about Rs 25 crore of oil and gas dispatches deferred to Q2 as export customers delayed take-offs due to the Middle East situation; material is ready.
GE: GT orders continuing; HRSG order from GE yet to come, though an agreement exists for around 15-16 units. A GE meeting is set for 14 September.
Siemens: MoU for GT piping starting at 10 units next year, then 15, then 25-30 units. Each GT unit is about EUR 1-1.5 million. Siemens team to visit Anjar in the third week of August.
BHEL: slower than expected, but about Rs 200 crore order received last quarter and more tenders expected to be finalised next quarter. L&T has awarded all orders offloaded so far.
Export mix: about 50% export and 50% domestic for FY27. The order book includes about Rs 400 crore of India HRSG work and about Rs 200 crore from Thailand.
Gross margin pressure attributed to higher material content in power-sector jobs (versus job-work) and the mix shift. Management said conversion costs are lower for power jobs.
Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited domestic order of Rs 386.82 crore received in the quarter, described as one of the largest single orders in recent history.
Gulf reconstruction: inquiries are coming via OEMs; not yet direct, and not included in projections for five years.

qa_highlights.answer: GE GT orders continue, HRSG order yet to come despite agreement for 15-16 units. Siemens MoU for 10 units next year, 15 the year after, then 25-30. Each GT unit about EUR 1-1.5 million.

544202|2026-03.headline: Stanley Lifestyles FY26 gross margin rose 151 bps to 57.5%, but Q4 revenue fell on B2B export pull-down and management guides only conservative FY27 growth.
544202|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a transition year spent acquiring franchise markets (Chennai, Hyderabad, Pune) into company-owned stores and consolidating subsidiaries into one listed entity. Q4 FY26 saw a decline in B2B demand from mid-Q4, with roughly Rs. 15 crore of B2B revenue pulled down due to West Asia conflict disruptions to a large export client. Gross margin for FY26 improved to 57.5% from 56.3%, while cash was about Rs. 200 crore versus Rs. 215 crore a year earlier despite capex above Rs. 60 crore. Management opened 11 stores and closed three over 12 months, and guided to aspirational double-digit growth but a conservative stance for FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Mature stores have grown about 4% a year; the flat revenue reflects a 35% drop in franchisee business and about Rs. 18-20 crore lost from leather trading moved to cash-and-carry, plus Rs. 24 crore cited in total.

qa_highlights.question: What were the short-term disruptions in the last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: A large global furniture brand's B2B exports to the Middle East were halted by the war-related logistics standstill; orders were postponed and recovery is expected by Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why not pursue low-end B2B inquiries given low plant utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its back-end is built for premium B2C and it cannot compete with unorganised low-end B2B; it is pursuing high-end B2B inquiries from MNCs and considering exports.

qa_highlights.question: Store economics and when stores start generating cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says ROI, including interest on capex, is about 3 years; some catchments take 15-18 months and Bangalore micro-markets 24-36 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross margin down sequentially in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 to raw material delays due to the US-Iran war and about Rs. 15 crore B2B revenue pull-down; it said full-year gross margin improved and B2C margins are secure.

qa_highlights.question: Digital discovery, website and pricing policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management admitted it has been slow on digital, said SAP is implemented, and promised a new AI-assisted website, with AR/VR tools, by end FY27.

Mass Premium & Others drove growth, with Prestige & Above volume growth slowing to 6.1% YoY. Net debt rose to ₹1,273 crore, pushing Net Debt/EBITDA to 2.2x, marginally above the 2.0x framework.

segments.name: Prestige & Above
segments.commentary: Sales ₹605 crore (+13.4% YoY, +7.5% QoQ); volume 4.5 million cases (+6.1% YoY); realisation ₹1,339/case (+6.9% YoY). Share of value 56.4% (vs 56.9%) and of volume 45.0% (vs 47.1%).

segments.name: ICONiQ White
segments.commentary: 3.2 million cases in Q2 FY27 (+20.6% YoY from 2.6 mn); H1 FY27 at 6.2 million cases (+26.8% YoY). FY27 target about 14 million cases (FY26: 10.7 million).

segments.name: ABD Maestro (super-premium to luxury)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales about ₹40 crore; FY27 target about ₹80 crore. Present in about 80% of addressable markets in India, 7 export countries, and 6,000 premium touchpoints at FY26 exit.

guidance_outlook: Topline expected to grow in line with the stated guidance of mid-teens for FY27.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided broadly in line with FY26; management says the West Asia-related disruption cost about 250 bps of margin, and it expects to match FY26 margin by FY27 close.
H2 FY27 gross margin expected to gain about 100 bps from seasonality and premium mix (vs 46% in Q1 and 45.3% in Q2).
Backward integration expected to add about 300 bps EBITDA margin by FY28 and a further 150 bps in FY29 (management also cited 400-450 bps cumulative by FY29 in one answer).
ICONiQ White target of about 14 million cases in FY27; management aspires to 20 million cases within two years.
Net Debt/EBITDA and Net Debt/Equity expected to return within the 2.0x and 0.75x frameworks on a full-year basis.
Export footprint target of 50-plus countries within 12 months (42 at Q2 FY27).
capex_capacity: Total capex programme about ₹1,600 crore; about 25% spent through FY26, about ₹300 crore spent in FY27 so far, balance over the next 3 years. Management sees no capex beyond this other than maintenance.
Maintenance capex estimated at ₹75-100 crore per year across 40 manufacturing plants.
Rangapur, Telangana: captive malt distillery commissioned in October 2026, about ₹75 crore investment, 4.0 million bulk litres per year. PET bottle plant (commissioned FY26) is EBITDA accretive.

Minakshi Agro (Aurangabad, Maharashtra): bottling unit expected operational in the next couple of months; ENA distillery expansion has environment clearance, construction under way, targeted for H1 FY28.

Uttar Pradesh (Moradabad): bottling facility commenced commercial operations in October 2026 with 6 million cases per year initial capacity; plan to expand to 13 million cases by Q3 FY28. New 66 million bulk litre per year dual-mode distillery announced August 2026 at about ₹293.5 crore; separate ~₹202 crore for bottling expansion, molasses refurbishment and land; overall UP investment above ₹600 crore.
demand_pricing: Volume growth was broad-based across Mass Premium & Others and Prestige & Above; all four millionaire brands grew sequentially. Record monthly volume above 3.5 million cases in September 2026.
Officer's Choice Blue refreshed packaging launched September 2026 in UP, Maharashtra, Haryana and West Bengal; management reports quarter-on-quarter growth in Q2 after YoY declines moderated.
The Indian Edit launched September 2026 in 7 states, priced around ₹1,550 in Maharashtra per an analyst question.

Karnataka: market about 65 million cases a year; ABD holds about 40,000-50,000 cases a month; premium is 10-12% of market; sub-premium brands cut prices by lowering alcohol strength. ICONiQ growth seen over the last 2 months.
Tamil Nadu (over 50 lakh cases a month) seen as opening up, with new brands being registered; management expects value and margin accretion.
Pricing: management is lobbying for price increases in Telangana and other states; no quantified price increase given.
India-UK FTA: management expects about 70 bps margin benefit this year, but uncertainty over bulk scotch import duty under applicable HSN codes; stocks last until early December.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ICONiQ White volume grow only marginally QoQ (3.1 mn in Q1 to 3.2 mn in Q2), and is it maturing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called Q1 an aberration; FY27 target is about 14 million cases (over 25% growth), and the brand has exceeded 1 million cases a month since April.

qa_highlights.question: Will further capex be announced beyond the current programme, and what is maintenance capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Current programme is about ₹1,600 crore, of which 25% spent through FY26; no further capex beyond this apart from maintenance of ₹75-100 crore a year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Prestige & Above growth (about 6%) lag Mass Premium (about 15%), and how will P&A recover?
qa_highlights.answer: P&A volume grew 6% but value 13.4%; Mass Premium's revival diluted P&A salience. Management targets 50%+ volume and 60%+ value saliency within a year, with ICONiQ seasonally weighted to H2 and an OC Blue and Sterling Reserve reset planned, plus a vodka launch before year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How should gross margin progress in H2 given the supply chain impact and UK FTA benefits?
qa_highlights.answer: Market seasonality should add about 100 bps to gross margin in H2; backward integration benefits are expected in FY28-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Is ICONiQ cannibalising the other brands, and what is being done on OC Blue and Sterling Reserve B7?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied cannibalisation, citing ICONiQ at more than 1 million cases a month; SR B7 packaging roll-out is targeted for Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company funding capex with leverage above the framework?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 FY27 operating cash flow was ₹269 crore (vs ₹147 crore); management expects metrics to fall within the framework by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pricing strategy given cost inflation and how much margin is lost to the West Asia conflict?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is lobbying states (Telangana the main near-term case) for price increases; it estimates the West Asia-linked inflation cost about 250 bps of EBITDA margin and expects it to be temporary.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from global supply chain disruption (₹29 crore in Q2, ₹53 crore in H1); management says inflationary pressure persists and Q4 should be better.
Net Debt/EBITDA of 2.2x and Net Debt/Equity of 0.8x are above framework; full-year compliance depends on capex timing and cash generation.
ICONiQ White must grow about 30% in H2 to reach 14 million cases, with Q2 volume only marginally above Q1; Karnataka competitive changes are unresolved.
Prestige & Above volume growth of 6% and declining share of P&A volume; OC Blue and SR B7 recovery depends on packaging resets due H2 and Q4 FY27.
India-UK FTA bulk scotch duty uncertainty; management expects resolution within about a month, with stock cover to early December.
Telangana price revision and dues clearance still pending.
key_quotes: So, I have lost about 250 basis points of EBITDA margin because of the West Asia crisis.
This is just an aberration. The plan for ICONiQ during the current year is to reach a level of close to 14 million cases, which is in excess of 25% growth by the year-end.
So, we are not scared of competition, but we will just concentrate on elevating our position in the market over the next 2 years.
But right now, the pressure is on.

544209|2026-03.headline: Bansal Wire FY26 revenue up 19% to INR 4,160 crore and volume up 33% to 4.58 lakh t, but gas disruption cut March output to 35% and Q1 FY27 is expected to be subdued.
544209|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 volume was 1.17 lakh t (+20% YoY, slightly down QoQ) and revenue was INR 1,136 crore (+21% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 80 crore (7% margin) and net profit of INR 40 crore (+21%). For FY26, revenue rose 19% to INR 4,160 crore, EBITDA rose 17% to INR 325 crore and PAT rose 10% to INR 161 crore. A natural gas disruption linked to Iran-Israel tensions cut production to 35% in March, and management said April volumes were recovering to about 80-85% of normal. Management kept a 20% medium-term growth target once conditions normalise, and said cash flow reached INR 333 crore against a INR 250 crore target.

vs initial target of INR 250 crore; total INR 600 crore target by 2027

segments.name: Product mix (volume, approx.)
segments.commentary: Low carbon about 55%, high carbon about 25%, stainless about 20%; speciality under 3-4% currently. Management said mix is unchanged and gave no segment EBITDA split, only blended EBITDA per ton.

segments.name: IHT Wire (speciality)
segments.commentary: Phase-I ramping ahead of expectations; March utilisation about 25%, expected to rise 10-15 points per month. EBITDA turns positive above about 50% utilisation. Phase-II adds 6,000 t to the existing 9,000 t.

segments.name: LRPC wire
segments.commentary: 18,000 t capacity started toward end of FY26 and is generating positive EBITDA.

segments.name: Steel Cords
segments.commentary: Planned 2 lakh t capacity; first trial order expected soon from one of the top four Indian tyre companies. Fire in the Steel Cords shed caused about a 6-month delay.

segments.commentary: Management said automotive is the only segment still growing; the auto share of revenue was cited as about 22% in a question.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 expected to be subdued: volumes were cut 35% in the last month, recovering to about 80-85% of normal; sales visibility is limited until conditions normalise.
Medium-term target of about 20% volume and EBITDA growth (management also cited 20-25% a year), once conditions normalise; EBITDA per ton expected to be the same or better after normalisation.

Gas prices still up about 50% blended for Q1 (up to 300% at some units); management expects about 50 of 90 Q1 days at standard EBITDA, with the INR 2,000-2,500 per ton hit limited to the 30-40 day order book.

Capex capped at about INR 150-200 crore a year; capacity to reach at least 8 lakh t by end FY27 (1.2 lakh t at Dadri, late in the year) and 8.5-8.6 lakh t with Sanand, which is now expected to be usable in FY28.
Steel Cords first trial order expected in FY27 H2 with other customers by year-end; management said about 20 kt run-rate could come within this financial year.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 6.80 lakh t after adding about 1.2 lakh t at Dadri in FY26 (Phase-I complete); about 60,000 t commissioned in April 2026, with INR 213 crore capital WIP.
Dadri Phase-II (1.2 lakh t) expected toward end of FY27; Sanand 0.9 lakh t expected late FY27 and usable in FY28. Timelines flexible based on utilisation.

Steel Cords: 2 lakh t planned; total investment INR 2,000-2,500 crore over 5-7 years, EBITDA INR 600-800 crore at maturity per management's ballpark. Management said the first 20,000 t has been done at lower capex per ton.
Sanand balance 50% land to be sold for cash; backward integration deferred at least two years.
Balaji Wire and Bansal High Carbon near-zero utilisation; about 95% of volume already moved to Bansal Wire, with the last 4-5% expected to shift in 6-8 months.
demand_pricing: Demand outside automotive is sluggish (consumer durables, infra and others), attributed to a steel price rise of 10-15% over three months and the geopolitical situation.
Cost-plus model with 30-40 days of inventory and 30-40 days of order book; fresh orders are priced with the gas-related increase, but the existing order book is absorbing the cost.
Steel Cords pricing: management said a large discount is not expected because the company is the first Indian entrant, and it claimed about 10% import arbitrage plus duty protection.

Payables rose sharply because of purchase inverse discounting with banks; management expects payable days to rise further as it reduces working capital days, with only a modest increase in interest cost.

qa_highlights.question: How much volume and gas-related disruption is expected in Q1 FY27, and can higher steel prices offset lower volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes were cut 35% last month and are recovering to 80-85% of normal. Management said higher prices may support revenue but EBITDA per ton would take a hit, and it could not quantify the figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% growth guidance at risk given the April production cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 20% growth is achievable only once conditions normalise, and it cannot give a number for the current period.

qa_highlights.question: What are the blended gas price increase and the expected April EBITDA per ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended gas escalation of at least 50% for Q1, with some units up to 300%. The INR 2,000-2,500 per ton hit applies only to the 30-40 day order book; management expects about 50 of 90 days at standard EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: How does the Steel Cords trial and approval process work and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The first trial order is from one of the top four Indian tyre makers, with one customer having removed the field trial. Other customers are expected by year-end, and about 20 kt run-rate could come within FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did payables rise sharply, and will this continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it reflects purchase inverse discounting with banks, while suppliers are still paid in advance. Payable days can rise gradually as working capital days are reduced.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% growth target conservative, and what is the FY26 utilisation and FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has grown about 20% over the last 10 years, with 30% in FY26 due to pent-up demand. FY26 utilisation was 67-68%; 80-85% is its preferred level, but at least 70% is the working target for FY27.

risks_watch: Gas supply and pricing: blended gas cost up about 50% for Q1 and volumes cut 35% in the last month of FY26; recovery pace uncertain.
Demand outside automotive remains weak after a steel price rise, affecting Q1 visibility.
Steel Cords ramp-up depends on first trial order and customer qualification, with a 6-month delay caused by the fire and a long approval cycle.
Rising payables through inverse discounting increase reliance on bank limits and may add to finance cost.
Gross margin pressure in the 30-40 day order book until fresh pricing flows through.

544209|2026-06.headline: Bansal Wire Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 25% YoY to INR 1,168 crore, with EBITDA of INR 57 crore and PAT of INR 20 crore after a gas-driven margin hit.
544209|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was hit in its first 45 days by a spike in gas and consumable costs (about INR 5,000 a tonne blended) linked to West Asia tensions, and management chose to absorb the cost on about 30-40 days of firm-price orders, cutting blended EBITDA to about INR 2 a kg. Margins recovered to about INR 7-8 a kg from around May 15, and management says operations are back to normal levels. Sales volume was 112,000 tonnes versus 104,000 tonnes a year earlier, and operating cash flow was about INR 121 crore. Management reiterated 20% volume and EBITDA growth for the rest of FY27 and kept capex at INR 200-250 crore a year.

financial_highlights.value: about INR 4-4.5 a kg for the quarter
financial_highlights.change: first 45 days about INR 2 a kg; later period INR 7-8 a kg

segments.name: Core B2B wire business
segments.commentary: Absorbed a cost shock on about 30-40 days of firm-price orders; new orders were priced at INR 8 a kg blended. Management says volume growth lagged its 20% target because of a demand dip and customer destocking.

segments.name: B2C (farming, fencing, poultry steel wire)
segments.commentary: Launched in the quarter and contributed about 10% of sales. Management targets B2C at 25% of total sales, which is 50% of the low-carbon business, and says B2C EBITDA per tonne is 20-30% above B2B low-carbon.

segments.name: Speciality wires (IHT, OHT, Steel Cord)
segments.commentary: IHT capacity is 9,000 tonnes, rising to 15,000 tonnes with OHT by year-end. IHT utilisation is at 35-40% and targeted at about 50% next month. Steel Cord has a 20,000-tonne pilot and received its first trial order from a leading Indian tire maker; four trials are expected, each taking about two to three months.

EBITDA per kg is expected to stay around INR 7-8 a kg after the Q1 disruption.

Target of 25% ROCE in the current business over a short period.
Operating cash flow target of INR 350 crore for FY27, per management.

Management aims to start each year with 20-25% spare capacity and historically runs at 85-90% utilisation.

Dadri greenfield facility had early hiccups that management says are resolved, and ramp-up is now under way.
OHT wire is expected to commission shortly and be fully operational by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins and growth hold if the geopolitical and oil-price issue persists for several quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management absorbed about INR 5,000 a tonne of consumable cost on firm-price orders for the first 45 days, which took EBITDA down to about INR 2 a kg. Margins have been back at INR 7-8 a kg since about May 15.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company run a cost-plus model, and why did the quarter's margin fall so sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: The model is cost-plus, but about 30-40 days of inventory was tied to fixed-rate orders, so the cost rise hit immediately. New orders were booked at escalated prices from April.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book from the first Steel Cord trial customer and when will a firm order come?
qa_highlights.answer: It is only a trial order with no firm order book yet. Four trials are expected, each taking about two to three months, so a firm order could take six to eight months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CFO guidance rise to about INR 800 crore across FY27 and FY28 from about INR 600 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 600 crore figure was a combined two-year target. FY26 delivered about INR 330 crore against a INR 250 crore target, and FY27's target is INR 350 crore, with INR 115 crore already generated in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What are the IHT and OHT margins and utilisation path?
qa_highlights.answer: IHT is at 35-40% utilisation, targeting about 50% next month. Break-even is at about 60% utilisation, with decent margins at 70-80%. Combined IHT and OHT EBITDA is expected at INR 10-20 a kg.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is capped at INR 200-250 crore a year to support 20-25% volume growth. Management said there will be no unusually high capex year apart from Speciality.

risks_watch: Gas and consumable costs had not eased by the call, and a reversal could create inventory losses on the 30-40 days of stock held at cost.

Receivable and payable days: the company used payables financing and vendor advances, and management plans to cut receivable days.

We will cap our CAPEX at about INR 200 crore-INR 250 crore every year to give us runway for each year.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 85% and the company runs at 85-90% historically, but capex is capped at INR 200-250 crore a year, so new capacity beyond the 90,000 t Sanand expansion and 60,000 t reserve is not signalled.

rows.why: Four trials of about two to three months each, from a first trial order with no firm order book yet, so a firm order could take six to eight months.

rows.label: IHT utilisation ramp to 60-80%

rows.label: Receivable days cut and FY27 operating cash flow of INR 350 crore
rows.why: Management plans to cut receivable days and has INR 115 crore of operating cash flow in Q1 against a INR 350 crore FY27 target, though payables financing and vendor advances were used.

544209|2026-09.headline: Bansal Wire posted record Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 1,308 crore (+24% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 105 crore, with EBITDA/ton near Rs 8,000 aided partly by inventory gain.
544209|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a record quarter for revenue, EBITDA, PAT and EBITDA per ton, recovering from a Q1 hit from industrial gas disruption and higher input costs. Sales volume was about 1,29,000 tons versus 1,14,609 tons in Q2 FY26, and operating cash flow was Rs 218 crore in the quarter and Rs 339 crore in H1. Management said about Rs 200/ton of EBITDA was a one-time inventory gain and guided to Rs 7,000-7,500/ton for H2. Raw material (wire rod) shortages hit October output, which management said is a short-term issue.

segments.name: IHT / OHT specialty wire
segments.commentary: IHT wire reached positive EBITDA last quarter; management cites Rs 15,000-20,000/ton EBITDA for the specialty wire group. IHT capacity is 9,000 tons, with 6,000 tons OHT being installed to reach 15,000 tons in one to two quarters.

segments.name: Steel tyre cord
segments.commentary: Current capacity about 20,000 tons, with a goal of 2 lakh tons. Pricing is about Rs 130-140/kg. First trial order received in Q2, with a second trial order expected in 10-15 days; commercialisation possible within this year.

segments.name: Bead wire
segments.commentary: Nameplate capacity about 30,000 tons, with 10,000-15,000 tons currently run annually. Management cites Rs 12,000-15,000/ton EBITDA. Approvals not yet started; focus to resume in one to two quarters.

segments.name: LRPC
segments.commentary: Less than 1% of sales. Management said it earns modest margins (about Rs 5,000-8,000/ton typical) due to industry overcapacity.

segments.name: B2C (farming, fencing, poultry)
segments.commentary: About 10-12% of Q2 volumes; management says B2C EBITDA is at least 50% higher than B2B.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth of 20% YoY for H2 FY27 (Q3 and Q4 vs prior-year H2); management said Q1 losses cannot be recovered.
EBITDA per ton guidance of Rs 7,000-7,500/ton for H2 FY27; management said Rs 7,000-8,000/ton is achievable for FY27 barring major geopolitical change.
Operating cash flow target of about Rs 800 crore across FY27 and FY28 combined; about Rs 350 crore already generated in H1 FY27.
Capacity to rise from 6.8 lakh tons to about 8.3 lakh tons by end of next year (60,000 tons Dadri brownfield plus about 90,000 tons Sanand greenfield).
Indicative annual capex of Rs 200-225 crore (also cited as Rs 200-250 crore per year), funded from internal accruals.
Long-term EBITDA/ton target of Rs 8,000-10,000, and above Rs 10,000 as specialty wire scales.
capex_capacity: Dadri: 60,000 tons additional low and high carbon wire capacity, mostly built; capitalisation expected by end of Q3 or Q4 FY27. Also 6,000 tons OHT wire, expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27.

Sanand (southern Gujarat) greenfield: about 90,000 tons of stainless steel and low carbon wire, with about Rs 150 crore capex excluding land (land acquired about a year ago). Some capitalisation expected from next quarter or the quarter after.
CWIP closing balance Rs 177 crore.
Steel tyre cord: 20,000 tons current capacity, with a 2 lakh ton goal; a bigger capex will follow customer approvals.
Management expects 4-5x asset turnover on new capacity.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as healthy across automotive, infra, agriculture, power and transmission, and general engineering. Constraint is raw material supply rather than demand.
Wire rod shortage over the last 1.5-2 months as suppliers shifted output to TMT. Company holds about 1.5 months of inventory; October output was hit at some plants, which management says is now back.
Low carbon was about 55% of volume in Q2 (lower end of 55-60% target), supporting blended margin.
Gas prices are about 2.5x the regular level, passed through to customers. Availability has been stable for about one quarter.

Steel tyre cord India demand is 2.5-3 lakh tons, mostly imported. Management expects radialisation (about 60% in India truck/bus) to drive growth. Management says there is no Indian domestic competitor; Bekaert is the main competitor.
Management says it will cap any single customer at 20-25% of total sales for steel cord.

qa_highlights.question: When will steel tyre cord and IHT/OHT translate into revenue and EBITDA, and what is the EBITDA per ton for specialty wire?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel tyre cord is in trials, with a second trial order expected in 10-15 days and commercialisation possible within the year. Specialty wire EBITDA is about Rs 15,000-20,000/ton, and IHT has turned EBITDA positive.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 EBITDA/ton came from inventory gains, and is Rs 7,000-7,500 conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory gain was about Rs 200/ton, so underlying EBITDA was about Rs 7,800-7,900/ton. Management said its own strategy is Rs 7,000-7,500 and it is not guiding above that.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% volume growth guidance for H2 only, and is it at risk from raw material shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: It applies to H2 FY27, meaning Q3 and Q4 volumes up 20% YoY. Management said raw material shortages are temporary and that lost days can be made up the following month.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of Sanand and Dadri CWIP and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: CWIP is Rs 177 crore, mostly Dadri 60,000 tons. Sanand needs about Rs 150 crore capex excluding land.

qa_highlights.question: Steel cord capacity plan and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity is 20,000 tons, the target is 2 lakh tons, and realisation is about Rs 130-140/kg. Management said a major capex will follow customer approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Is Rs 7-7.5/kg the right base for H2 earnings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs 7,000-7,500/ton is the H2 EBITDA commitment, and a better outcome is possible but not guided.

risks_watch: Raw material (wire rod) availability: shortages in October and supplier breakdowns could cut Q3 and Q4 volumes below the 20% growth guidance.
Gas prices at about 2.5x normal; management says pass-through to customers is in place, but this is a margin risk.
Q2 EBITDA/ton includes about Rs 200/ton inventory gain, so sustainability of the Rs 7,800-8,000 level is uncertain.
Steel cord commercialisation depends on customer approvals; management expects the first two quarters of ramp-up to be slow.
Sanand greenfield and Dadri ramp-up execution; capex may move beyond the stated timelines.
LRPC is loss-making at the margin due to industry overcapacity; management says it is less than 1% of sales.
544209|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on results and guidance, with management saying it prefers to guide conservatively. It was candid about near-term raw material disruption and the Q1 gas hit. Answers on steel cord timelines were more hedged, using phrases such as "hopefully" and "if everything goes well".
key_quotes: We have achieved our highest ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA, and profit after tax.
So, we will rather be a little conservative than not delivering on our guidance.
Sir, our thought process is that we should maintain our margins at about Rs. 7,000 to Rs. 7,500.
In the long run, yes, we would definitely look at Rs. 8,000 to Rs. 10,000.

rows.why: Guidance of Rs 7,000-7,500/ton for H2 is below the Q2 underlying level of about Rs 7,800-7,900, with the inventory gain not repeating and gas at about 2.5x normal, so margins are more likely to ease than expand; the long-term Rs 8,000-10,000 target is not a near-term call.

rows.why: Dadri 60,000 t brownfield is mostly built with capitalisation expected end Q3 or Q4 FY27, Sanand greenfield (~90,000 t, Rs 150 crore capex ex-land, CWIP Rs 177 crore) starts capitalising next quarter or the one after, taking capacity from 6.8 to ~8.3 lakh t by end of next year.

rows.why: Indicative capex is held at Rs 200-225 crore a year, but a bigger steel cord capex is to follow customer approvals from a 20,000 t base against a 2 lakh t goal, with utilisation not disclosed and no new plant beyond Dadri and Sanand approved.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides H2 EBITDA/ton at Rs 7,000-7,500 but says a better outcome is possible and is not guiding above it, with underlying Q2 at about Rs 7,800-7,900 excluding a ~Rs 200/ton inventory gain.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Wire rod shortages hit October output and suppliers shifted to TMT over 1.5-2 months, and the company holds only ~1.5 months of inventory, putting the 20% H2 volume guide at risk even though management says lost days can be made up.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Steel tyre cord had a first trial order in Q2 with a second expected in 10-15 days at Rs 130-140/kg, and commercialisation is possible within the year, though management says the first two quarters of ramp-up will be slow.

rows.label: Steel tyre cord second trial order
rows.when: within 10-15 days of the call, then commercialisation within
rows.why: First trial order received in Q2 and a second trial order expected in 10-15 days, with Indian steel cord demand at 2.5-3 lakh t, mostly imported, and no domestic competitor per management.

rows.label: Debt reduction and cash generation
rows.why: Total debt is ~Rs 300 crore with D/E about 0.2 after a ~40% cut in H1, operating cash flow was Rs 339 crore in H1 against a ~Rs 800 crore target for FY27-FY28 combined.

rows.label: IHT/OHT specialty wire scale-up to 15,000 t
rows.why: IHT capacity is 9,000 t with 6,000 t OHT being installed, and specialty wire earns Rs 15,000-20,000/t EBITDA, but timing is hedged as 'hopefully'.
