544210|2026-03.headline: Emcure FY26 revenue crossed INR9,204 crore (+16.6%), but Q4 domestic growth slowed to 5.2% on Zuventus disruption; FY27 guided to low-to-mid-teen growth.
544210|2026-03.overview: Emcure reported FY26 revenue of INR9,204 crore (+16.6% YoY), with adjusted PAT up 41% to INR1,008 crore and EBITDA margin up 80 bps to 19.4%. Q4 revenue rose 16.7% to INR2,470 crore, but domestic growth slowed to 5.2% because of attrition and restructuring at the newly consolidated Zuventus business. International markets grew 25.7% in Q4, with Europe and Canada leading. Management said April is on plan and guided FY27 to low-to-mid-teen revenue growth and 75-100 bps of EBITDA margin expansion.

financial_highlights.change: +24.5% YoY; margin up from 18.4% in Q4 FY25
Up YoY due to Manx payouts and Zuventus minority stake buyout

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR4,027 crore (+10%), led by women's health, cardio, CNS and oncology. Q4 revenue INR977 crore (+5.2%) was hit by Zuventus. Management said ex-Zuventus Q4 growth was below 8% and the full-year ex-Zuventus base growth was high single digit.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR5,177 crore (+22.2%). Q4 revenue INR1,493 crore (+25.7%); currency added roughly 7-8% overall, about 11-12% in Europe.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,850 crore (+25.5%). Q4 revenue INR538 crore (+35.8%), helped by Manx and Amphotericin B. Management expects mid-teens CAGR over the next two years.

segments.name: Canada
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,487 crore (+18.7%). Q4 revenue INR399 crore (+28.6%), driven by market share gains and launches.

segments.name: Rest of World / Emerging markets
segments.commentary: FY26 ROW revenue INR1,840 crore (+21.8%), with ARV and non-ARV both contributing. Q4 emerging markets revenue INR556 crore (+15.5%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at low-to-mid-teens.
EBITDA margin expansion of 75-100 bps in FY27, assuming stable regulations, macro conditions and no major geopolitical upheaval.
Domestic target: grow faster than industry (8-9% expected), at low double-digits.
FY27 capex guided at roughly INR400-425 crore.
FY27 average currency assumption of INR92/USD.
Gross margin expected to stay around 60% for the full year.
Employee expense growth expected at about 10% in FY27 versus about 7% in FY26.
Canada semaglutide launch via Dr. Reddy's partnership in Quebec, expected around Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at roughly INR400-425 crore.
Field force around 4,000 MRs; about 40% sit in Zuventus. Field productivity rose from INR5.4 lakh to INR7 lakh per MR over two years.
Amphotericin B launched in select European markets in H2 FY26; expansion to Europe and rest of world planned for FY27.
Bevacizumab ophthalmic biosimilar endorsed by CDSCO SEC; launch planned H1 FY27 pending approval.
Lenacapavir: DMF filed; product registration sought in FY27.
demand_pricing: Zuventus: Q4 restructuring (new management after October minority buyout, portfolio and team reorganisation) drove high field attrition; management says April is on plan. Normal MR attrition is 20-30%.

Poviztra (Novo Nordisk rDNA semaglutide, India exclusive): early uptake promising after April 2026 price cut; about 1,000 sales reps promoting it. Management says the product is differentiated versus synthetic generics.
In-licensed products make up about 15% of domestic sales. The Roche nephrology brands (2-3 key brands) are under INR50 crore annualised with no upfront payment.
Market share in covered markets was roughly flat for FY26 after the Q4 impact.

Raw material and solvent prices have risen with the Middle East conflict. Freight and insurance costs are also up. Company holds 1-2 quarters of inventory and says there are no supply issues yet. IPA is seeking a domestic price hike.
Canada: Dr. Reddy's partnership via Mantra subsidiary in Quebec, where pricing is expected to be more favourable. Apotex and Reddy's received semaglutide approvals recently.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify Zuventus impact on India growth and whether restructuring will weigh on the next few quarters.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full-year ex-Zuventus base growth would have been 9-10%, and Q4 ex-Zuventus was below 8%. It expects the impact to fade, with April back on track.

qa_highlights.question: What operational synergies are expected from Zuventus?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manufacturing synergies are limited because the plants serve different products. Gains are expected in sales and marketing organisation and support functions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 domestic growth outlook and the currency assumption behind guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry growth is expected at 8-9% and Emcure aims for low double digits. The guidance assumes INR92/USD.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the raw material and geopolitical cost pressure is in guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory covers 1-2 quarters, so impact is limited near term. Management said guidance includes current pricing, and the industry is facing solvent and freight cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Canada semaglutide path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Quebec partnership with Dr. Reddy's aims for an early launch around Q2 FY27, and its own filing will target the rest of Canada in the medium term. Deal terms were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is Emcure open to more in-licensing deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the focus is organic growth but in-licensing will continue where it is accretive.

risks_watch: Zuventus recovery: whether April's on-plan trend holds through Q1 FY27 after high attrition.
Poviztra price war and whether market share recovers after the April 2026 price cut.
Raw material, solvent, freight and insurance inflation if the Middle East conflict persists beyond the 1-2 quarters of inventory.
Rising debt (net debt INR1,054 crore) after the Manx and Zuventus payouts.
Q4 Mantra earn-out exceptional charge of INR43 crore, which was above initial expectations.
Currency: a weaker rupee supports international revenue, but the INR92/USD assumption needs monitoring.
544210|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and optimistic on FY27 and on the Zuventus recovery, though Q4 domestic softness was openly acknowledged. Management was noticeably evasive on monthly April growth and on the semaglutide market-share recovery. It was also cautious on cost pressures, saying the impact is hard to quantify.
key_quotes: FY26 marked the start of our 5-year strategy, focusing on turning last year's operational changes into measurable outcomes.
Ex of the Zuventus impact for the full year would have been close to the 9% - 10% base business growth that we have been talking about, that we delivered even in the first 9 months.
I think we continue to expect industry growth to be around 8% to 9% , and for us, the target, is to grow faster than the industry – probably at low double-digits.

In FY27, we project low to mid -teen revenue growth and as I have been explaining in the last meet and a few calls that I have had the privilege of addressing to you guys that EBITDA margin expansion will happen as committed between 75 to 100 basis points going forward, assuming stable regulations and macroeconomic conditions.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided 75-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion in FY27 after FY26 margin of 19.4% (+80 bps), with gross margin held near 60% and employee cost growth of about 10% vs about 7% in FY26; raw material and freight inflation is a watch item.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to low-to-mid-teens (midpoint about 12.5%) with domestic targeted at low double-digits vs industry 8-9%, and International +25.7% in Q4 led by Europe +35.8% and Canada +28.6%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex of INR400-425 crore is already guided, but no new capacity or utilisation figure was disclosed, so no further capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was set as a fresh low-to-mid-teen range with April described only as on plan; no sign of a beat that would prompt a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Ex-Zuventus Q4 growth was below 8% with high field attrition (normal 20-30%), and raw material, solvent and freight costs are rising with only 1-2 quarters of inventory cover, while net debt rose to INR1,054 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Bevacizumab ophthalmic biosimilar launch planned H1 FY27 pending approval, Canada semaglutide via Dr. Reddy's in Quebec around Q2 FY27, and Amphotericin B expansion to Europe and RoW planned for FY27.

rows.label: Zuventus recovery after Q4 restructuring
rows.why: Ex-Zuventus full-year base growth was 9-10% and Q4 ex-Zuventus below 8%; management says April is on plan, but monthly April growth was not quantified and field attrition was high.

rows.label: Poviztra semaglutide uptake after April 2026 price cut
rows.why: About 1,000 sales reps are promoting Poviztra and early uptake is called promising, but management was evasive on market-share recovery and the price war risk is open.

rows.label: IPA domestic price hike for raw material inflation
rows.why: Solvent and freight costs are rising with the Middle East conflict and the industry body is seeking a domestic price hike, but no approval is confirmed and inventory covers only 1-2 quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 guidance, the Zuventus recovery and International growth, but was evasive on April monthly growth and semaglutide share recovery and cautious on cost pressures; analysts focused on Zuventus drag and quantifying it.

544210|2026-06.headline: Emcure Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.8% YoY to INR 2,580 crore, with EBITDA of INR 508 crore (19.7% margin) and PAT up 35-36%.
544210|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 22.8% YoY to INR 2,580 crore, led by international markets (up 34.2% to INR 1,485 crore) while India grew 10.2% to INR 1,095 crore. EBITDA rose 25.8% to INR 508 crore with margin up 50 bps to 19.7%, and PAT grew about 36% to INR 292 crore. Gross margin fell to 58.4% on geographic and product mix, and net debt rose to INR 1,103 crore. Management reiterated low-to-mid teens FY27 revenue growth (now toward the higher end) and 70-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion. Board changes were announced: Chairman Berjis Desai retires at AGM and CEO Satish Mehta becomes Chairman; Samit Mehta becomes COO and CEO of Gennova, which is now 100% owned.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,095 crore, +10.2% YoY. Ex-Sanofi OAD and Roche in-licensed brands, growth was about 6-7%. Price contributed about 4-5%, new launches 1-2%. Management says no channel filling in the quarter.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 537 crore, +32.8% YoY, driven by base business and liposomal amphotericin B (Ampho). Ampho is introduced in pretty much all countries, but tender-based procurement means lumpy orders.

segments.name: Canada
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 427 crore, +24.6% YoY, on new launches and share gains. Semaglutide filing expected in the next few months; Quebec launch via Dr. Reddy's is uncertain.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 522 crore, +44.8% YoY, led by ARV. About two-thirds of ROW was ARV this quarter; management expects ARV at about 50-55% of ROW for the full year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at low-to-mid teens, with management now more comfortable at the higher end of that range, driven by ARV order book visibility.
EBITDA margin expansion of 70-100 bps for FY27 reiterated.
FY27 gross margin guided at about 59% (earlier 60-61% framing), as higher international and ARV mix dilutes gross margin while EBITDA is accretive.
R&D for FY27 guided at 4-5% of revenue; spend expected to pick up in the rest of the year.
India growth expected in line with industry in Q2 FY27 and faster than industry in H2 FY27 as the Zuventus base effect eases.
Net debt expected to rise to about INR 1,450 crore by end-Q2 FY27 after the Mantra and Gennova payouts (INR 450-500 crore), then turn net cash by end-FY28.
Management expects sequential improvement each quarter.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were given on the call.
Gennova consolidated to 100% after acquiring a 12.05% minority stake; Mantra acquisition payout completed in July 2026.
demand_pricing: International constant-currency growth about 12% (about 12-13% per later answer), against about 6-7% FX tailwind at company level.
India price growth about 4-5% YoY; new launches 1-2%; the remainder is volume.

Poviztra (semaglutide biosimilar with Novo Nordisk) is growing month on month, but management says 40-50 brands have launched in the market and it is hard to separate channel stocking from consumption. Pricing was set very competitively.
Gross margin pressure reflects B2B-type international businesses (lower gross margin, higher EBITDA contribution), with Europe and ARV growing faster.
Management says Zuventus is stabilised and consolidated, now moving to acceleration.

qa_highlights.question: Is India's double-digit growth clean, or is there channel filling after Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no channel filling this quarter; growth is normalised and expected to improve further in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What share of ROW is ARV, and does FY27 base make FY28 harder?
qa_highlights.answer: About two-thirds of ROW is ARV this quarter; full-year ARV share is expected at about 50-55% of ROW, with growth in both ARV and non-ARV.

qa_highlights.question: When will domestic growth be back in line with the market, and what is organic growth ex-in-licensed brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 FY27 is expected to be in line with industry and H2 faster. Ex-Sanofi OAD and Roche, growth was about 6-7%. Poviztra is a new launch; OAD moves into the base next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is constant-currency international growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Company-level FX impact was about 6-7%; international growth would have been about 12% in constant currency (12-13% in later answer).

qa_highlights.question: Why is Canada semaglutide a second-wave filing, and what is the Quebec launch timing with Dr. Reddy's?
qa_highlights.answer: Filing expected in the next few months, delayed because semaglutide was pursued as a global development. Quebec timing depends on Dr. Reddy's supply; management will defer to them.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin decline and where does it settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix from Europe and ARV growth; FY27 gross margin guided at about 59%. Management says B2B international businesses are EBITDA-accretive despite lower gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: When will net debt turn to net cash and how does it trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt expected at about INR 1,450 crore by end-Q2 after acquisition payouts; net cash by about end-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 R&D spend?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is guided at 4-5% of revenue for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: from INR 99 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,103 crore (CFO also cited INR 1,560 crore in Q&A)

risks_watch: India growth: management guides Q2 FY27 in line with industry and H2 faster as the Zuventus base eases; Q1 organic ex-in-licensed growth was about 6-7%, so watch whether the Q2 and H2 acceleration materialises.

Poviztra (semaglutide biosimilar) competition: 40-50 brands launched, management cannot separate channel stocking from consumption and says the market needs 3-6 months to play out; pricing set very competitively.

544224|2026-03.headline: Afcom Q4 FY26 revenue rose 87.8% YoY to INR191.88 crore and PAT to INR44.66 crore, on war-driven charter demand.
544224|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR191.88 crore (+87.8% YoY), EBITDA of INR74.08 lakh per the call (+51.52%), and PAT of INR44.66 crore (+72.85%) under Ind AS. Full-year revenue was INR587.72 crore (+143.86%) and PAT INR121.90 crore (+230.05%), with PAT margin of 20.74%. Growth was driven by stranded-cargo charters after Middle East disruption in March 2026, with 415 of 602 Q4 trips being pure charters. Fleet expansion is the key near-term constraint: a third aircraft is operational, with fourth and fifth expected before the next quarter and wide-bodies (Boeing 777) planned from late 2026.

Management called a 777 revenue of about 3x a 737-800 at 14-15 rotations/month and 75% load factor, implying roughly INR75 crore/month per 777 as a conservative estimate; management said FY27 revenue could be at least double FY26 on existing resources.
ATF pass-through via fuel surcharge; designated carrier status cuts fuel-related VAT, adding about 5-7% benefit to overall fuel cost from the next financial year.
Maintenance reserve now expensed to P&L under Ind AS; management says no further fundraise needed for the fleet plan after QIB and preferential issues.
capex_capacity: Three aircraft in operation: VT-AFO, VT-AFN and the newly inducted third aircraft (VT-AFJ per Q&A), with the third aircraft held for a fresh C-check and contracted Middle East flying from late June.

FY26 capacity utilisation 81.42% on gross weight basis; utilisation hours per aircraft per day peaked at 11.45 (VT-AFO) and 10.51 (VT-AFN) in Q4 versus industry best 10-14 hours and Asia Pacific average 7.9.
Lease-related liability: three aircraft ROU assets INR306 crore, total lease liability INR338 crore, current lease dues INR49 crore plus INR16.1 crore lease finance cost over 12 months.

Funding: QIB and preferential allotment (INR200 crore each per analyst) stated to cover wide-body induction; fourth and fifth aircraft costs largely covered, with customs and minor expenses remaining.
demand_pricing: March 2026 saw a sudden capacity withdrawal from Middle East carriers; Q4 month-end revenue ran about INR42-44 crore per month, with March about 22-23% above the Jan-Feb average.

Management said April and May demand remained above average but below March panic levels; fuel prices (ATF) at INR2,24,000/KL were offered at INR1,69,000/KL under designated carrier status, versus INR85,000/KL before.
Q4 yield USD2.72/kg versus IATA industry average cited at INR222/kg; management said company yield per kg is better than the IATA average.

Over 60% of billing is in USD. Receivables about 60 days on recent billing (IATA norm 45 days); management said no receivables older than 6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for fourth, fifth and wide-body aircraft induction?
qa_highlights.answer: Third aircraft operational; fourth and fifth to be operational before next quarter; one 777 targeted in last quarter of FY27, with four 777s in total per management's later clarification, fully operational by second half of calendar 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of ATF price surge and pass-through to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fuel is passed through 100% via fuel surcharge; the market absorbed the April spike, which tapered in May and June; designated carrier status yields a fuel price benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 yield only USD2.72/kg despite higher freight rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher charter share (415 of 602 Q4 trips) and short-sector stranded-cargo flights lowered yield per kg; more weight-based cargo would have raised yield.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue potential of 777 aircraft?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 777 can do 14-15 rotations per month at 75% load factor, giving about 3x a 737-800's revenue; an analyst's estimate of about INR75 crore per month per 777 was described as conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q4 EBITDA margin lower than Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to Ind AS adjustments, particularly a large forex loss charged to P&L, and maintenance reserve now expensed.

qa_highlights.question: Ideal FY27 revenue expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said resources would at least double FY26 revenue on a conservative basis; no numerical guidance given.

risks_watch: Fuel price volatility (ATF up sharply from April) and dependence on a fuel surcharge pass-through; pricing could soften if the Middle East disruption ends.
Revenue dependence on temporary war-driven charter demand; management acknowledged yields hardened in March and the sea-freight alternative is also rising in cost.
Ind AS restatement now shows large forex losses and maintenance reserve charges, which compress reported margins; Q4 EBITDA margin lower than Q3.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is framed as meeting targets (Uniware 15%+, Shipway 20%+ from Q4 FY27, Shipway breakeven Q3 FY27) after a quarter where Uniware grew 12.8% and Shipway 16.8%, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Uniware must accelerate from 12.8% to 15%+ and Shipway from 16.8% to 20%+ within Q4 FY27, with ESOP running INR2.5-4 crores per quarter and H1 Shipway below breakeven; the investment amount is unquantified ('a few crores').

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management cited upcoming AI-led launches and a checkout product under evaluation (no timing), after three modules (UniCapture, UniReco, UniBot) in the last 12-18 months; UniReco adoption is 6-7% and UniCapture 3-4% of enterprise customers.

rows.label: Shipway breakeven in Q3 FY27
rows.why: Management is targeting Shipway adjusted EBITDA breakeven in Q3 FY27 after H1 below breakeven, with profits reinvested, against a market where it holds a single-digit share of a INR4,000 crore addressable market.

rows.label: Enterprise customer adds and marquee wins
rows.why: 115 enterprise adds in Q1 FY27 (vs 88 a year ago, Q4 FY26 ~149) and 30-50% above the 85-90 per quarter listing-time run rate; marquee wins include Amul, Haldiram's and Mahindra Logistics.

rows.label: Uniware realisation stable
rows.why: Average realisation is about INR1 lakh per month and broadly stable across 1,100+ enterprise customers, with NRR said to be 100%+ but no current-quarter figure given.

tone.note: Management was confident on Uniware stickiness and the medium-term growth outlook but vague on quantification (investment only 'a few crores', no current-quarter NRR, no M&A target details); analysts probed margins, ESOP and Shipway ramp, and the CEO was unwell during the call.

544227|2026-09.headline: Unicommerce Q2 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to INR59.1 crore, but adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 17% from 22.2%.
544227|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY to INR59.1 crore in Q2 FY27, with both Uniware and Shipway growing double digits. Adjusted EBITDA fell to INR10 crore (17% margin) from INR11.4 crore (22.2%) as management front-loaded investments in AI-led product, talent, and sales and marketing. PAT rose to INR6.4 crore from INR5.8 crore, helped by deferred tax recognition. Management guided that investment pace moderates in H2 FY27, with Shipway reaching adjusted EBITDA break-even in Q3 and PAT profitability in Q4.

UniReco and UniCapture run-rate exceeds INR3 crore (about 2.5% of Uniware revenue), used by more than 150 clients.

segments.name: Shipway
segments.commentary: Grew more than 15% YoY and crossed INR100 crore annualised revenue run rate. Estimated market share is below 5% of a roughly INR4,000 crore courier aggregation market. Guided to adjusted EBITDA break-even from Q3 FY27 and PAT profitability from Q4 FY27.

B2B and quick commerce are used by 45-50% of the client base; management said per-transaction realisation is not like-for-like because bulk items carry lower realisation per item. B2C realisation stated as stable.

Shipway cross-sell: about 10% client overlap with Uniware, yet 20-25% of Shipway shipment volumes come from Uniware clients.

Courier aggregation market is structured with one leader holding 20-25% share and about 45 fragmented players; management claims Unicommerce plus Shipway is the only player with a comprehensive suite.
Management said Uniware gross margin is around 80% and Shipway gross margin around 20%, in line with industry benchmarks.

qa_highlights.question: Why is average realisation per order declining despite enterprise client growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2B and quick commerce (used by 45-50% of clients) lower per-item realisation, so the metric is not like-for-like; it does not track rate per transaction and tracks NRR, new client adds and profit instead.

qa_highlights.question: Was the employee cost step-up proactive or overdue, given reports of tech stack issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the investments proactive, tied to AI, and said the platform is mission-critical with a 50% price premium; it disputed the tech stack criticism and cited 2x quick commerce peak processing growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H1 tax expense much lower on a consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to recognising deferred tax on expected tax benefits linked to Shipway turning profitable from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 3-5 year plan and when can margin reach 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 5x revenue growth over five years with adjusted EBITDA margin returning to 20%+ at steady state; the CFO said Uniware margin is 36% and consolidated is 17%.

qa_highlights.question: Is M&A planned, given the rise in current investments?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said current and non-current investments should be read together, as the gap is largely fixed deposits maturing within 12 months. CEO said M&A must meet four criteria (customer fit, good product and team, profitable or path to profit, reasonable valuation) and there is no fixed timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Does the market size support Shipway's growth and what is the right to win?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a INR4,000 crore courier aggregation market, a 20-25% leader, and right to win from the OMS/WMS suite, sticky Uniware cross-sell and a service-first approach; D2C market growing in double digits.

544232|2026-03.headline: Interarch FY26 revenue rose 31% to Rs 1,898 crore; FY27 guided to Rs 2,150-2,200 crore, with order book at Rs 1,700 crore.
544232|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue reached Rs 1,898 crore (up about 31% YoY) and EBITDA Rs 176 crore (margin 9.3%), with PAT of Rs 135 crore. Q4 revenue was about Rs 500 crore (up 8.7% QoQ), with volumes near 41,000 tons and EBITDA of Rs 53 crore at a 10.5% margin, which management said was held down by about Rs 5-5.5 crore of one-offs (labour code provision, export certifications, outsourced high-rise engineering, bid costs). Capacity is fully utilised, so growth depends on new plants: the Gujarat PEB plant (fifth integrated plant) targets July 2026 commercial production, and the Andhra heavy structure plant starts in July-August. Management said Q4 was lower than the expected seasonal step-up because Q3 had already run at full capacity; cash flow from operations turned negative in FY26 due to milestone-based receivables and inventory build-up.

financial_highlights.change: +25% YoY vs Rs 108 crore; tax rate about 27% in FY26 vs 24% prior year

financial_highlights.change: About 3.2% YoY per analyst; Rs 1,650 crore QoQ per management

segments.commentary: Order book of Rs 1,700 crore is almost entirely PEB; realisation about Rs 120 per kg. Realisation was higher in Q4 and may fall Rs 4-5 per kg as steel prices soften.

segments.commentary: Not yet in revenue. First heavy structure order (Rs 102 crore, Delhi Rajpath government building) announced, with supply from September 2026. Realisation about Rs 95-100 per kg, as only structure is supplied without secondaries or cladding.

Net PAT margin guided at 7-7.5% for FY27; EBITDA margin expected around 9.3-9.5% on an annual basis.
Heavy structure plant (Andhra) expected to sell 10,000-12,000 tons in FY27 (Rs 120-130 crore), with full capacity of 18,000-20,000 tons (Rs 200-210 crore a year).

Plans to raise funds via QIP within two to three months, mainly for heavy structures.
capex_capacity: Gujarat PEB plant (fifth integrated plant, about Rs 2,500 crore capacity): building complete, machinery installation from first half June, trial production June, commercial production July 2026; Phase 2 machinery by end-2026. Delay of about 1-1.5 months was due to high water table requiring foundation redesign.
Andhra Pradesh heavy structure plant: Phase 1 in July-August 2026; Phases 2 and 3 planned to be accelerated, targeting completion around end of next year. Machinery imported from Germany and Italy.
Current capacity about 160,000 tons (four plants) plus outsourcing, quoted at about 180,000 tons a year; running at about 40,000 tons a quarter.
Additional land bought in Gujarat for a second PEB or heavy structure plant; combined planned capacity of Rs 3,000 crore PEB and Rs 500 crore heavy structures.
Canadian partner JV for 100% export unit (open web joist) under MoU signed 20 May 2026; plant expected in about a year (around August-September 2027).
demand_pricing: Pipeline 1 (orders expected within 60 days) about Rs 800-900 crore; Pipeline 2 (bid, decision in 2-7 months) about Rs 3,500 crore, mainly PEB.
Order intake limited by delivery capacity; management said it would not take orders it cannot deliver and sees no demand slowdown.

Steel supply: no disruption to projects per management; relationships with SAIL, JSW and AMNS cited. Labour shortage in March (LPG crisis, elections) cost about Rs 20-25 crore of revenue, now back to normal.

Cash flow from operations turned negative in FY26 due to larger milestone-based orders (Rs 100 crore plus) and steel inventory built ahead of price rises; management expects it to turn positive quickly.
Margins: management targets 9.5-10% EBITDA over time and cites hidden costs of new businesses; said North America exports offer better margins.

qa_highlights.question: Steel supplier concentration and whether disruptions hit Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no project disruptions; steel suppliers were stable through long relationships. The Q4 shortfall was driven by labour shortages in March, not steel supply.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue impact from site clearance delays in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact was about Rs 20-25 crore, with the quarter only held back to avoid spoiling material.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the order book not growing and how does the pipeline look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said orders are capped by delivery capacity. Pipeline 1 is Rs 800-900 crore and Pipeline 2 about Rs 3,500 crore, and the pipeline is growing.

qa_highlights.question: Will heavy structure be included in FY28 Rs 2,500 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said HSS is assumed in that number, but it will update guidance after Q3 or Q4 of this year, once it has sales data.

qa_highlights.question: Why is OCF negative and when will it turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed larger milestone-based receivables and inventory build-up for the negative OCF, and expects it to turn positive quickly as it tightens payment terms.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin excluding one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one-offs of Rs 5-6 crore would add about 0.25 percentage points, taking margin to about 9.7% from 9.3%.

Labour availability for construction sites flagged as the biggest challenge for FY27.
QIP fundraise (to be finalised within two to three months) and its size and use, mainly for heavy structures.

544232|2026-06.headline: Interarch Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20.7% YoY to INR460 crores, EBITDA up 24.6% to INR39 crores, PAT flat at INR28 crores; order book INR1,864 crores.
544232|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 20.7% YoY to INR460 crores and EBITDA grew 24.6% to INR39 crores, with margin stable at 8.6%. PAT was flat at INR28 crores as other income fell because IPO cash was spent on capex. Management raised FY27 revenue to INR2,700 crores for FY28 (from INR2,500 crores) and kept FY27 guidance at INR2,150-2,200 crores. Order book stood at INR1,864 crores as of 31 July 2026, and a QIP was approved at INR250 crores, up from INR100 crores earlier.

financial_highlights.change: up ~9% QoQ per analyst; management said increased over last 3 months
positive; prior-year Q1 had negative operating cash flow

segments.name: Pre-engineered buildings (PEB)
segments.commentary: Core business; capacity about 221,000 tonnes after Kheda (Gujarat) Phase 1 inauguration; FY26 sales 162,000 tonnes (~80% of installed, ~88% of utilisable capacity). Gujarat plant started 9 July 2026; Phase 2 expected by October 2026.

segments.name: Heavy structures (Andhra Pradesh, Pantnagar Kichha line)
segments.commentary: Trial production started; commercial production expected around end-August/early-September 2026. Phase 2 targeted by March 2027 and Phase 3 by December 2027, for a total of about 75,000-80,000 tonnes. Management expects about INR100-150 crores of FY27 revenue from heavy structures.

segments.name: Buildings segment (multi-storey, data centres, hotels)
segments.commentary: Around 10% of Q1 revenue, versus about 0-2% previously, including a data centre order for RailTel in Noida. Management said about 35% of order book comes from new-age industries and new segments.

segments.commentary: JV with a Canadian partner (ER Steel) for a 15,000-tonne plant; first phase 4,000-5,000 tonnes (~$7.5m, ~INR70-75 crores) with ~20% EBITDA margin targeted. Production expected by July-end 2027. Management targets exports at about 10% of turnover in the short to medium term (1-2 years).

EBITDA and PBT targets for FY27 unchanged; FY28 EBITDA margin aim of 9.5-10%.

Margin expansion expected mainly in FY28 rather than immediately, as new plants carry upfront costs.

Timing not decided; may be within the next 4 months.
About INR240 crores of capex spent from April 2024 to date, versus INR180 crores raised in the IPO.

Management said competition is intensifying but pie is expanding; price pressure exists, but management is focused on profitability over revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 revenue (INR460 crores) lower than Q3/Q4 last year and even Q2, given the INR600 crore quarterly run-rate target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the seasonal Q1/Q2 dip to site clearances and monsoon; it said order book and capacity are in place and the run-rate will vary (e.g. INR550-620 crores), needing about INR1,700 crores over the next 9 months. The Andhra phase 2 (about 20,000 tonnes) came online in September 2025.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned use of the INR250 crore QIP, and why was it raised from INR100 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Heavy structure Phases 2-3 in Andhra about INR140-150 crores, Gujarat Plant 2 INR50-60 crores, and the Canadian open web joist export unit INR50-60 crores. Management said the expansion is being sped up, and the IPO raised about INR180 crores against about INR240 crores of capex spent since April 2024.

qa_highlights.question: Details on the ER Steel Canada JV: rationale, and revenue potential over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Partner handles sales, engineering and customers in North America; Interarch handles manufacturing. The 15,000-tonne plant could yield about $20-23 million at full capacity over 2-3 years. Phase 1 is 4,000-5,000 tonnes (about $7.5m, INR70-75 crores) at about 20% EBITDA, with production targeted by July-end 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Current capacity utilisation and margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 sales were 162,000 tonnes against 200,000 tonnes capacity (about 80%, about 88% of utilisable capacity). Capacity is now about 221,000 tonnes and Q1 volume was 38,499 tonnes (about 80% of 50,000 tonnes quarterly capacity). Margin gains are expected mainly in FY28, not immediately, as new plants carry upfront costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise QIP when cash generation appears sufficient, and what capex is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited working capital needs for larger orders and a desire to raise funds once for the next two years. Capex is about INR129 crores in FY27 and INR133 crores in FY28. Timing is undecided and could fall within about 4 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why are some energy-sector orders on 15-16 month execution periods, and what is the export contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: The orders are for HVDC valve halls from EPC contractors on variable-price terms, and site clearances take about 6 months versus 2-3 months normally. qa_highlights.question: Why was finance cost up sharply, and what is the debt position?

544238|2026-03.headline: Premier Energies FY26 revenue rose 20.7% to INR8,026 crore and PAT 61.1% to INR1,510 crore, with order book at INR14,010 crore (+66% YoY).
544238|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue of INR8,026 crore (+20.7% YoY) and PAT of INR1,510 crore (+61.1% YoY), with operational EBITDA margin of 30.4% and PAT margin of 18.8%. The 5.6 GW Sitarampur module plant is complete and expected to reach full ramp-up in about two months, and the Transcon 51% acquisition is closed. Capacity is set to rise to 16.75 GW by July 2026, with FY27 capex of INR5,100 crore. Management guided to no specific margin numbers, citing rising cell, silver and freight costs, and said it would pass silver risk to customers on new orders. The K-Solar acquisition was dropped, and the company is pursuing an inverter JV with SMA SGS as first preference.

segments.commentary: Module capacity 11.1 GW; management says utilisation is about 75% (roughly 7-7.5 GW). The 5.6 GW Sitarampur plant uses about 40% less manpower per MW than existing plants. Management expects DCR share to rise every quarter.

segments.commentary: Acquired 51% stake; FY revenue INR423 crore and PAT INR45 crore. Plant due for completion in July 2026; management says it has secured some first orders, and ramp-up is expected to take about two years.

segments.commentary: Inverter business pursued via a JV with SMA SGS (first preference) after K-Solar deal lapsed. BESS capacity pace is deliberately slowed due to imports at about 11% duty; localisation policy expected around FY28.

544238|2026-06.headline: Premier Energies Q1 FY27 revenue rose 34% YoY to INR2,508 crores, PAT up 53% to INR472 crores at an 18.8% margin.

544239|2026-03.headline: ECOS Q4 FY26 revenue up 16.65% to INR2,067.6 million, EBITDA down to INR241.5 million; FY27 guided to 18-20% growth at 11-13% margin.
544239|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 16.65% YoY to INR2,067.60 million, while EBITDA declined to INR241.53 million from INR264.67 million in Q4 FY25, reflecting continued investment in people, technology and leadership. For FY26, revenue rose 23.58% to INR8,081.58 million and EBITDA was INR939.29 million, with margins hit by higher manpower cost, tech spend, ETS price competition and a one-time doubtful-debt provision of about INR80 million. Management said the Middle East crisis dented CCR growth in March, and guided FY27 revenue growth of 18-20% and EBITDA margin of 11-13%, with cost growth expected to be lower than revenue growth. Analysts pressed on margin compression, falling revenue per trip and competitive pricing in ETS; management attributed the trend partly to shorter trips and airport transfers.

vs 4.04 million in FY25, approx. +29% YoY

segments.commentary: 58% of FY26 revenue and 57% in Q4 FY26. Stable demand from IT/ITES and a strong surge from GCC clients, but competitive pricing pressure was most visible here.

Demand from GCCs and manufacturing facilities is a notable driver of ETS enterprise wins; CCR growth is diversified across sectors.
Competitive price pressure is mainly in ETS, led by new entrants; management says prices should rise once operations prove unsustainable.

qa_highlights.question: How is the West Asia crisis affecting demand, and what is FY27 growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CCR growth slowed in March after the Middle East crisis, with a bounce back expected if the disruption is short. Management aspires to 18-20% growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can fuel price hikes be passed on, and what is the margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Most contracts have pass-through clauses triggered above roughly 5%, with lags of days to weeks. Management says the 6-7% increase has been fully passed on.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the INR8 crore receivable provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Legal proceedings for recovery are ongoing and management is hopeful. Recovery may come in FY27 or later.

qa_highlights.question: What are the expected growth rates for employee and other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is budgeted to grow about 13-16% and other expenses about 8-9%, both below the revenue growth target. Management expects operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue per trip declining, and is pricing pressure easing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited ETS pricing pressure and shorter trips plus airport transfers. Pressure appears to have stabilised in the last quarter, while the company is also winning larger enterprise contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins recover to the earlier 14-16% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 11-13% for FY27 and the next couple of years. It expects CCR brand premium to offset ETS price competition over time.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin in FY26 was about 11.6%, down from roughly 15% at IPO, and Q4 EBITDA fell YoY despite 16.65% revenue growth.
Falling revenue per trip (about INR1,550 in FY26) indicates pricing pressure in ETS from new entrants.
Pending legal recovery of the roughly INR80 million doubtful debt; timing is uncertain.
Middle East and fuel-price volatility affecting CCR demand and the lag in fuel pass-through.
Cost growth versus revenue growth in FY27: the company needs to deliver operating leverage against its 13-16% employee cost budget.
Dividend decision pending a separate board meeting.

rows.why: Direct web booking portal launched in Q4 FY26 for pre-scheduled rides and a new core backend platform launched, but no further product launch dates were given.

tone.note: Management was confident on client wins, GCC-driven ETS demand and the CCR brand premium, and cautious on near-term margins, the March CCR slowdown and EV capex. Analysts pressed on margin compression (FY26 about 11.6% vs roughly 15% at IPO), falling revenue per trip and ETS pricing competition.

544239|2026-06.headline: ECOS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.7% to INR2,113.7 mn, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.3% and FY27 margin guidance was cut to ~10%.

EBITDA was flat YoY at INR218.47 million, and margin fell to 10.3% from 12.0% a year ago and 11.7% in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the drop to higher operating costs, a higher ETS mix and more intense pricing pressure, especially in ETS. The FY27 EBITDA margin guidance was lowered to around 10% from the earlier 11-13% range, while revenue growth guidance of 15-18% was retained.

544240|2026-03.headline: Raymond Lifestyle FY26 total income hit record INR7,034 crore (+11% YoY) and EBITDA rose 23% to INR804 crore; Q4 EBITDA up 53% to INR152 crore.
544240|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a recovery year, with record annual total income of INR7,034 crore (+11% YoY) and EBITDA of INR804 crore (11.4% margin, +23%). Q4 FY26 total income was a record INR1,810 crore (+15% YoY), with EBITDA up 53% to INR152 crore and margin up 210 bps QoQ to 8.4%. The company remains debt-free with a net cash surplus of INR179 crore, and net working capital days fell from 87 to 77. Management labelled FY27 a "Year of Consolidation", guiding to double-digit top-line and bottom-line growth without numeric EBITDA guidance.

capex_capacity: Chennai fastener plant: installed capacity 4,600 MT; Phase 1 reached about INR5 crores per month (about INR60 crores annualised) from August 2025 ramp-up; plant utilisation about 35% in FY26.
Chennai Phase 2 capex to complete by June-July 2026, adding another INR5 crores per month (about INR60 crores annual); total Chennai capacity INR120 crores per annum by year-end.
Wada plant: no additional land; disc spring running about 80% utilisation; coil spring and fastener capacity have headroom, to be unlocked via productivity, line balancing and outsourcing.
Wada land purchase of 5 to 10 acres under negotiation for an own-land expansion; Chennai backup option is a SIPCOT long lease or an existing building to shift stud manufacturing.
Renewable and mobility capex: 1.8 MW open access solar plant ordered for captive consumption.
demand_pricing: Wind: about 60% to 65% of wind sales from India and 30% to 35% from exports; first high-tensile bolt supply to a global wind OEM in India from Chennai in Q4 FY26.
Growth mix in FY26 cited as about 10% from new customers, 10% to 12% from new parts with existing customers, and 5% to 7% organic growth.
Addressable market expanded: studs cover about US$1 billion; bolts and nuts take it to about US$2.5 billion. Global fastener market cited at about US$100 billion.
CSS competitors named as NHK Spring and Stumpp Schuele & Somappa; some imports from Europe remain a substitution opportunity.
Raw materials are 100% passed through to customers; process costs (gas, diesel) are being repriced from April 2026, with recovery expected on an annualised basis.
Hedging policy cut from 70% to 40% of estimated export collections, covering 12 months, net of imports for USD exposure.
Management says a currency depreciation gave a top-line benefit in Q4 but also created a non-cash forward-cover loss; the amount was not quantified on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What wind-energy order book and growth visibility exist for the coming year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 25% to 30% growth in short-term wind fasteners and springs; wind sales are about 60% to 65% India and 30% to 35% exports.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Chennai revenue ramp and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 ramped from INR1 crore to INR5 crores per month from August; Phase 2 adds INR5 crores per month by June-July, with INR80 crores targeted for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall to 16.5%, and how is raw-material inflation handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop from about 17.1% mainly to a roughly 1% (INR3.23 crore) forex loss, not mix or raw materials; raw materials are fully passed through with a lag.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a land and expansion plan beyond Chennai?
qa_highlights.answer: Wada land (2 to 3 plots) is in advanced talks, likely finalised June-end or July; a 15 to 18 month build is expected, with about INR50 crores of capex in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the EU-India FTA and CBAM matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Current EU import duty of 3.7% on Gala products would fall to zero when the FTA takes effect around January 2027, but CBAM could offset the benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hedging policy and export mix outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Forward cover is set at up to 40% of estimated export collections for 12 months; exports are expected to remain 35% to 40% of sales.

risks_watch: Forex volatility: a forex loss of about INR3.23 crores hit FY26 margins, and forward-cover losses can distort quarterly profit.
Chennai utilisation: FY26 was about 35%; the FY27 target of about INR80 crores depends on Phase 2 commissioning by mid-2026 and on scaling the bolt business.
Inventory: Chennai ramp-up adds inventory; working-capital days (103) and cash conversion are a watch item.
Wada land acquisition timelines could slip; Chennai backup plan depends on a SIPCOT lease or an existing building.
Pending patent suit on wedge lock washers: next hearing in June 2026; no arguments yet.
CBAM and EU trade changes could offset the expected FTA duty benefit.
Raw-material and gas cost pass-through is lagged; quarterly margin volatility is possible before price revisions take effect.
544244|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth and capacity plans, with specific timelines. Cautious and hedged on land acquisition and on quarterly forex and cost pass-through effects. Several answers were loosely worded, and exact figures (such as the currency benefit to revenue) were deferred.
key_quotes: And now we are seeing the similar runway as of now we will going to have in April, May, June.
So, we are quite close to in closing this land, but still not close, that is the fact.
So, with combination of this all, we are seeing that the current year whatever number we are targeting, we should be able to optimize our capacity utilization in Wada.
On the annualized basis, we will definitely see that whatever is been incurred is recovered.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects EBITDA margin to stabilise at 17-19% by FY27 end (Q4 FY26 at 17.57%, FY26 at 16.51%), assuming no further forex volatility; raw materials are passed through with a lag and process-cost repricing starts April 2026.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Chennai Phase 2 capex is under construction to add INR5 crores/month (about INR60 crores annual) by June-July 2026, taking total Chennai capacity to INR120 crores p.a., though Phase 1 utilisation was only about 35% in FY26.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 20-25% overall revenue growth (midpoint 22.5%), wind fasteners and springs 25-30%, and Chennai FY27 sales of about INR80 crores (67-70% of INR120 crores capacity) versus about 35% utilisation in FY26.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: next 2-3 quarters (Wada land finalisation June-end or July 2
rows.why: Wada disc spring runs at about 80% utilisation with no additional land, and management guided about INR50 crores of FY27 capex for a 5-10 acre own-land plant once land is finalised; timing depends on land negotiations.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided only 20-25% revenue growth and a 17-19% EBITDA margin band, with no sign of running ahead of these targets.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Forex losses (INR3.23 crores, about 1% of revenue) hit FY26 margins and forward-cover losses can distort quarters, while the INR80 crores Chennai FY27 target depends on Phase 2 commissioning and scaling from 35% utilisation.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First high-tensile wind bolt supply to a global OEM in India started in Q4 FY26 and offshore wind is targeted at about 10% of fastener sales within two to three years, but no specific new product launch dates were given.

rows.label: EU-India FTA removes 3.7% EU import duty
rows.why: The FTA is expected to remove the 3.7% EU duty around January 2027, but CBAM may offset the benefit, and the amount is not quantified.

rows.label: Exports held at 35-40% of sales with wind exports at 30-35%
rows.why: Management expects exports to stay at 35-40% of sales, with wind sales already 30-35% exports and a first global OEM bolt supply started in Q4 FY26.

rows.label: Process-cost repricing from April 2026
rows.why: Gas and diesel costs are being repriced from April 2026 with recovery on an annualised basis, and raw materials are 100% passed through with a lag, which should support margins once revisions take effect.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth targets, Chennai Phase 2 timing and wind orders, but cautious on Wada land timing, forex and lagged cost pass-through, and deferred exact figures such as the currency benefit to revenue; analysts pressed on margin dip drivers and land timelines.
